mayaṅkā marapiṉ eḻuttu muṟai kāṭṭi
malku nīr varaippiṉ aintiram niṟainta
tolkāppiyaṉ eṉat taṉ peyar tōṟṟip
pal pukaḻ niṟutta paṭimaiyōṉē.
translation:
In the virtuous Tamil-speaking land
That extends from
Vēnkatam in the north
And Kumari in the south,
He has treated units of sound and word
And semantic content as well,
Rooted as he remained
In traditions of common speeh and literary idiom;
Conversant he was of his predecessors’ works
That were in vogue and use on the soil
Which marked the cultivated idiom of the Tamil language;
He examined them in order
And has made a well-wrought work;
He presented this classic
In the assembly of Nilantarutiruvin Pāntiyan
Where at the head was Atañkōttācān
Endowed with a tongue of virtuous words
And in the wisdom of the four vedas rooted;
He expounded in terms irreproachable
The structure unambiguous of the language,
And thereby,
The sage of the man that he was
And of renown exceeding marked,
Established in the sea-girt world
His name Tolkāppiyan
Versed in the treatise Aintiram.

title: Coalescence with Human Class Nouns
transliteration:
uyir īṟu ākiya uyartiṇaip peyarum
puḷḷi iṟuti uyartiṇaip peyarum
ellā vaḻiyum iyalpu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Nouns of human generic class ending in vowels
And nouns of human generic class ending in consonants
As the preceding words
Shall have non-change coalescence
1: case-relations as well as non-case relations,
Thus does the authority hold.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
ikara īṟṟup peyar tiripu iṭaṉ uṭaittē.
translation:
Amongst these [153],
Nouns ending in /i/
Shall witness morphophonemic changes too
In certain contexts.

transliteration: aḵṟiṇai viravuppeyar iyalpumār uḷavē.
translation:
There is non-change coalescence too
Where
Nouns that designate
Both the human and non-human generic classes
Are the preceding words.

title: Changes Involving the Third Case
transliteration:
puḷḷi iṟutiyum uyir iṟu kiḷaviyum
valleḻuttu mikuti colliya muṟaiyāṉ

meymmai ākalum uṟaḻat tōṉṟalum
am muṟai iraṇṭum uriyavai uḷavē

translation:

Hard consonants

Where the preceding words

In case-relations coalescence,
Where the succeeding word

title: Changes Involving the Second Case
transliteration:
melleḻuttu miku vaḻi valippoṭu tōṉṟalum
valleḻuttu miku vaḻi melippoṭu tōṉṟalum
iyaṟkai maruṅkiṉ mikaṟkai tōṉṟalum

mey piṟitu āku iṭattu iyaṟkai ātalum

Occurrence of hard consonant! where soft one is in order,

Such of these morphophonemic variations
Do mark the behaviour of the second case [ai] morpheme
As it occurs before the succeeding word,

transliteration:
vēṟṟumai alvaḻi i ai eṉṉum

avaitām,
iyalpu ākunavum valleḻuttu mikunavum

translation:
Where there marks no declension by case,
The preceding nouns ending in /i/ and /ai/
Have three possibilities of morphophonemic coalescence :
Non-change', augmentation of succeeding words hard consonant and its
Thus has the authority ruled.

title: Coalescence with Words Declining for the Seventh Case
transliteration:

cuṭṭuc ciṉai nīṭiya ai eṉ iṟutiyum

translation:
The preceding word being

Augmentation of the succeeding words' hard consonant
And the optional augmentation of its hard consonant’,
So has the usage sanctioned.

title: Long and Short Vowels Followed by Consonants
transliteration:
neṭiyataṉ muṉṉar oṟṟu mey keṭutalum

translation:
That

And it is doubled after a short vowel?

transliteration:
āṟaṉ urupiṉum nāṉkaṉ urupiṉum

translation:
Followed
Morphemes of sixth [atu] and fourth [ku] cases,

Which has its initial long vowel shortened
Marks no augmentation of the word-final consonant as above [160]

transliteration: num eṉ iṟutiyum an nilai tiriyātu.
translation:

In accord with the norm above [161].

transliteration:
ukaramoṭu puṇarum puḷḷi iṟuti

translation:
The preceding word's word-final consonant [/ñ/ or /n/]
That is wont to coalesce with /u/ (uriñu, porunu)
Will go without the /w
When the succeeding word begins with /y/ or a vowel.

transliteration:
uyirum puḷḷiyum iṟuti āki
aḷavum niṟaiyum eṇṇum cuṭṭi
uḷa eṉappaṭṭa ellāc collum
tamtam kiḷavi tam akappaṭṭa
muttai varūum kālam tōṉṟiṉ

translation:
All words of vowel - or consonant-ending
Denoting measure of capacity, weight and number
Will have the appropriate empty morpheme /ë/ for
Where they are followed by terms
Denoting lesser units of measure, weight and number,

transliteration:
arai eṉa varūum pāl varai kiḷavikku

translation:
The empty morpheme /ë/ [164]
Does not accord with the term arai
Denoting the portion of a thing [half]
Which occurs as the following word.

transliteration:
kuṟai eṉ kiḷavi muṉ varu kālai

[Following the term of measure, weight or number},

The rule of coalescence for case declension
[There is the augmentation of the following word's initial consonant].

transliteration: kuṟṟiyalukarakku iṉṉē cāriyai.

And where the following word is kurai,
There occurs the empty morpheme in in between.

transliteration: attu iṭai varūum kalam eṉ aḷavē.

Between kalam the term of measure

paṉai eṉ aḷavum kā eṉ niṟaiyum

Panņai the term of measure
And ka denoting weight
Take the empty morpheme in after them
[Where the succeeding word is kurai].

transliteration:
aḷaviṟkum niṟaiyiṟkum moḻi mutal āki

avaitām,
ka ca ta pa eṉṟā na ma va eṉṟā
akara ukaramoṭu avai eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Nine are the letters marked
That begin terms of measure and weight,
Which are /K, /c/, /t/, /p/ and /n/, /m/, /v/ and /a/, /u,
Thus goes the sanction of usage.

transliteration:
īṟu iyal maruṅkiṉ ivai ivaṟṟu iyalpu eṉak
kūṟiya kiḷavip pal āṟu ellām
meyt talaippaṭṭa vaḻakkoṭu civaṇi
ottavai uriya puṇarmoḻi nilaiyē.
translation:
The norms varied enunciated above
Of the nature and modes of coalescence
Between the preceding and succeeding words
Are to be read appropriately
In relation to the worldly use current too.
The Deviant Forms of yavar and yatu

transliteration:

The elision of [va] in the nominative yavar
As it occurs preceded by a human generic class plural,

As it occurs preceded by a neuter singular —

title: The Empty Morpheme in
transliteration:

Between the preceding words of /a/, /å/, /u, /ū/, /&/ and /au/ endings
And the case morphemes going with them.

pallavai nutaliya akara iṟu peyar

That denote the plural number 'many'

From taking the empty morpheme varru.

transliteration: yā eṉ viṉāvum āyiyal tiriyātu.

Does not fail to go by the norm above (174)
[In taking the empty morpheme varru] [cf. 178].

title: The Empty Morpheme an
transliteration:

The word with the demonstrative word-initial [/a/, /i/ or /W]

transliteration:

translation:
The word with the demonstrative word-initial [/a/, /i/ or /u]
Has its word-final /ai/ unchanged too (cf. 122)
As it takes the empty morpheme varru
[Before the case morpheme ai).

transliteration:

Takes the empty morpheme varru,
Where its /v/ gets elided along with /ai/,
So rule the learned.
Coalescence Involving nī

Has its long vowel phoneme shortened [before case morpheme]
And there witnesses the occurrence of the consonant /n/ in between.

Before the case morpheme.

Terms with demonstratives [/a/, /i/, /u/] as word-initials

Will go in accord with the norm (178)
That governs the elision of word-final /ai/ along with its consonant
[The consonant is dropped and the empty morpheme varru follows].

For /v/ word-finals [tev] other than the ones above [183].

translation:

And the /m/ ending of yam as well
Go without the empty morphemes shown above [aftu and in]
In the case of yam with the /m/ word-final,
Its /ä/ changes to /e/

In between the stem ellam and its case morpheme,
And the empty morpheme um stands at the end.

When the noun ellam [189]
Comes to denote the human generic class,

Intervening between the noun and its case morpheme.

transliteration:
ellārum eṉṉum paṭarkkai iṟutiyum
ellīrum eṉṉum muṉṉilai iṟutiyum
oṟṟum ukaramum keṭum eṉa moḻipa
niṟṟal vēṇṭum rakarap puḷḷi

The word-final consonant of the third person pronoun el/larum
And the word-final consonant of the second person pronoun elfirum
Get elided along with the preceding vowel /u/,
So is it ruled;

The empty morpheme tam intervenes in the third person pronoun
Between the consonant /r/ and its case morpheme /ai/,

Between the consonant /r/ and its case morpheme /ai/.

tāṉ yāṉ eṉṉum āyīr iṟutiyum

As regards their morphophonemic coalescence,
The {word-final of tap and yâån
Does mark no dissimilarity
With the three nouns treated above [tam, nām, and yām (188)]
[The word-initial of tån has its length reduced
And yan
Has its /ā/ changed into /e/
With its /y/ elided].

transliteration:
aḻaṉē puḻaṉē āyiru moḻikkum
attum iṉṉum uṟaḻat tōṉṟal
ottatu eṉpa uṇarumōrē.

It is in accord with usage
For the two preceding terms alan and pulan
To take either of the empty morphemes attu and in
Before their case morphemes,

title: The Empty Morpheme an with ë!
transliteration:

Realizing a complementary function,
After words with shortened /u/ as word-final.

Occurring after the long vowels
And preceding the shortened /u/
Get doubled
Where these words are other than the ones above [195]
[Ending in ku, cu, tu, and pu).

avaitām,

[That double after long vowels]

Thus does the authority hold.

translation:
Shortened /u/ - ending words,
That denote numbers,

oṉṟu mutal āka pattu ūrntu varūum

Beginning with a demonstrative phoneme [/a/, /i/, /u/]

title: Nouns Denoting Directions
transliteration:

Other than those treated above,
When examined,
Are not bound to take intervening empty morphemes
As they combine with case morphemes.

akara iṟutip peyar nilai muṉṉar

The word-initial! consonants /k/, /c/, /t/ and /p/ of the succeeding words
[Or their corresponding consonants of articulatory proximity]

As the preceding nouns end in the vowel /a/.

viṉaiyeñcukiḷaviyum uvamak kiḷaviyum

ñāṅkark kiḷanta valleḻuttu mikumē.
translation:
Verbal participles' and comparison morphemes’,
The elliptical form ena’,
The demonstrative ending‘,
And the expletive åñnka’?

The consonants /V, /n/ and /m/

Witness their doubling therein.

translation:

Even where a vowel begins the succeeding word.

transliteration: nīṭa varutal ceyyuḷuḷ urittē.
translation:
Poetry admits of lengthening
[Of the preceding demonstrative /a/]
[Where the succeeding word begins with any but hard consonants].

cāva eṉṉum ceya eṉ eccattu
iṟuti vakaram keṭutalum urittē.
translation:

[Along with its clustered vowel]
In the ceya-formulaic verbal participle cava
Tends to be dropped too.

transliteration:
aṉṉa eṉṉum uvamak kiḷaviyum
aṇmai cuṭṭiya viḷinilaik kiḷaviyum
ceymmaṉa eṉṉum toḻil iṟu collum
ēval kaṇṇiya viyaṅkōṭ kiḷaviyum
ceyta eṉṉum peyareñcukiḷaviyum
ceyyiya eṉṉum viṉaiyeñcukiḷaviyum
amma eṉṉum uraipporuṭ kiḷaviyum
palavaṟṟu iṟutip peyarkkoṭai uḷappaṭa

translation:
The comparison morpheme anna’,
Vocatives used to call those in proximity’,
Finite verbs of the formulaic pattern ceymmana’,

ilakkaṇa maruṅkiṉ col āṟu alla.
translation:
Plural suffix to a noun denoting human species singular
And plural suffix to a noun denoting non-human species singular’
Are part of worldly usage in honour clothed
Not permitted they are by norms of grammar.

title: Persons
transliteration:
celaviṉum varaviṉum taraviṉum koṭaiyiṉum
nilai peṟat tōṉṟum an nāṟ collum
taṉmai muṉṉilai paṭarkkai eṉṉum
am mū iṭattum uriya eṉpa.
translation:
The four words —
celavu (to go), varavu (to come), taravu (to hand) and kotai (to offer)
Are assignable to the first, second and third persons,
So does the usage go.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
taru col varu col āyiru kiḷaviyum
taṉmai muṉṉilai āyīr iṭatta.
translation:
Among these four words [5l],
taravu (to hand) and varavu (to come)
Are first person and second person specific.

transliteration: ēṉai iraṇṭum ēṉai iṭatta.
translation:
The remaining two
[celavu (to go) and kotai (to offer)]
Are third person specific.

title: Things Unidentified
transliteration:
yātu evaṉ eṉṉum āyiru kiḷaviyum
aṟiyāp poruḷvayiṉ ceṟiyat tōṉṟum.
translation:
The two [non-personal] interrogative pronouns —
yatu and evan —
Seek to know the identity of things unknown.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
yātu eṉa varūum viṉāviṉ kiḷavi
aṟinta poruḷvayiṉ aiyam tīrtaṟkut
terinta kiḷavi ātalum urittē.
translation:
Between these two [514],
The interrogative pronoun yatu
Seeks references to specific features too
Of a thing whose identity is known.

transliteration:
iṉaittu eṉa aṟinta ciṉai mutal kiḷavikku
viṉaippaṭu tokutiyiṉ ummai vēṇṭum.
translation:
The subject denoting the limb or the whole
Whose number is made known
Takes the particle - um
Where it is followed by a predicate.

transliteration: maṉṉāp poruḷum aṉṉa iyaṟṟē.
translation:
Things transient or non-existent too
Take the particle - um (read with 516).

title: A Trade Register
transliteration:
ep poruḷ āyiṉum allatu il eṉiṉ
ap poruḷ allāp piṟitu poruḷ kūṟal.
translation:
1f one has to say
'It is but unavailable"
When a certain commodity is asked f Or,
One must do so
By pointing to something else that is available.

transliteration: ap poruḷ kūṟiṉ cuṭṭik kūṟal.
translation:
[To read with 518]
Where one has to affirm
The availability of the commodity asked for,
Its mention must be preceded by a demonstrative emphatic.

title: A Function of the Demonstrative Pronoun
transliteration:
poruḷoṭu puṇarāc cuṭṭuppeyar āyiṉum
poruḷ vēṟupaṭāatu oṉṟu ākummē.
translation:
Even where the demonstrative pronoun stands
Not being in kinship with the object mentioned,
There abides its reference to the object given.

title: Personal Pronoun as Co-referent
transliteration:
iyaṟpeyark kiḷaviyum cuṭṭuppeyark kiḷaviyum
viṉaikku oruṅku iyalum kālam tōṉṟiṉ
cuṭṭuppeyark kiḷavi muṟpaṭak kiḷavār
iyaṟpeyar vaḻiya eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Personal pronoun
As a co-referent to a proper noun
Does not occur ahead of the proper noun,
But, replaces the noun in a succeeding reference
Were both operate pairing with predicate,
So de the learned rule.

transliteration: muṟpaṭak kiḷattal ceyyuḷuḷ urittē.
translation:
[To read with 521]
In poetry,
Personal pronoun
As a co-referent to a proper noun
Does occur ahead of the proper noun too.

transliteration:
cuṭṭu mutal ākiya kāraṇak kiḷaviyum
cuṭṭuppeyar iyaṟkaiyiṉ ceṟiyat tōṉṟum.
translation:
A demonstrative word-initial [/a/, /i/, /u/] causal connective
Follows the proper noun as co-referent
In the way the personal pronoun does [521].

title: Positioning of Honorific Titles
transliteration:
ciṟappiṉ ākiya peyarnilaik kiḷavikkum
iyaṟpeyark kiḷavi muṟpaṭak kiḷavār.
translation:
Proper nouns should not precede
Honorific titles.

title: Nominal Epithets-Verb Concord
transliteration:
oru poruḷ kuṟitta vēṟu peyark kiḷavi
toḻil vēṟu kiḷappiṉ oṉṟu iṭaṉ ilavē.
translation:
Nominal epithets
Pointing to one person or object
Do not indicate the same person or object
Where they take different verbs.

title: A Norm of Usage
transliteration:
taṉmaic collē aḵṟiṇaik kiḷavi eṉṟu
eṇṇu vaḻi maruṅkiṉ viravutal varaiyār.
translation:
That
First person singular noun
And a non-human generic class noun
Are counted together
Is not inadmissible.

transliteration:
orumai eṇṇiṉ potup piri pāṟcol
orumaikku allatu eṇṇu muṟai nillātu.
translation:
The singular masculine and feminine gender specific forms
[oruvan and orutti (one man and one woman)]
That branch out from the common gender designation one [oruvar],
Do not lend themselves to enumeration.

title: Mixed Human and Non-human Class
transliteration: viyaṅkōḷ eṇṇuppeyar tiṇai viravu varaiyār.
translation:
It is not inadmissible that
Human-class and non-human class generic nouns intermingle
As they occur in enumerative linear sequence
Where a verb in the optative mood follows the sequence.

title: Common Noun and a Specific Verb
transliteration: vēṟu viṉaip potuc col oru viṉai kiḷavār.
translation:
Where a common noun embodies
Strands of meaning,
Each strand taking a verb of its own,
No one of these verbs
Shall constitute the predicate of that common noun.

transliteration: eṇṇuṅkālum atu ataṉ marapē.
translation:
The norm above [529] abides
Where terms,
Each of which collocates with a given verb,
Occur in an enumerative linear sequence too.

title: Reduplicative Term
transliteration: iraṭṭaikkiḷavi iraṭṭiṉ pirintu icaiyā.
translation:
A reduplicative term
Does not go ūnpaired.

title: Designation by Dominant Species
transliteration:
oru peyarp potuc col uḷ poruḷ oḻiyat
teripu vēṟu kiḷattal talaimaiyum paṉmaiyum
uyartiṇai maruṅkiṉum aḵṟiṇai maruṅkiṉum.
translation:
In both human and non-human generic classes,
One should go for designation
By things of a species constituting centrality and majority,
With things marginal of other species within
Being left unconsidered.

title: Common Terms and Specific Gender Designation
transliteration:
peyariṉum toḻiliṉum piripavai ellām
mayaṅkal kūṭā vaḻakkuvaḻip paṭṭaṉa.
translation:
That
Nouns and verbs
Of both human and non-human classes
That are common to genders masculine and feminine
Come to mark off senses gender specific
To the exclusion of the other gender —
Goes by sanction of usage alive,
And no ambiguity there attends.

title: Mixed Class Nouns in Enumeration
transliteration:
palavayiṉāṉum eṇṇut tiṇai viravuppeyar
aḵṟiṇai muṭipiṉa ceyyuḷuḷḷē.
translation:
In poetry [in general],
Where human and non-human class intermingle
In an enumerative linear sequence,
The sequence takes a (predicate) ending
That is appropriate to non-human class.

title: A Classification of Homonyms
transliteration:
viṉai vēṟupaṭūum pala poruḷ oru col
viṉai vēṟupaṭāap pala poruḷ oru col eṉṟu
āyiru vakaiya pala poruḷ oru col.
translation:
Homonyms. fall into two classes —
Those that take different verbs after them’
And those that take the same verb’.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
viṉai vēṟupaṭūum pala poruḷ oru col
vēṟupaṭu viṉaiyiṉum iṉattiṉum cārpiṉum
tēṟat tōṉṟum poruḷ teri nilaiyē.
translation:
Between these two above [535],
Homonyms that take different verbs
Have their sense come explicit
Through the distinguishing verb'
And through context and associaton’.

transliteration: oṉṟu viṉai maruṅkiṉ oṉṟit tōṉṟum.
translation:
The context of situation
Shall determine the sense
Where homonymous words take the same verb
[To read with 535 and 536}.

transliteration:
viṉai vēṟupaṭāap pala poruḷ oru col
niṉaiyum kālai kiḷantāṅku iyalum.
translation:
The homonym that takes the same verb
Should have the senses explicitly stated
[To read with 535 - 537].

title: Nature of Utterance
transliteration: kuṟittōṉ kūṟṟam terittu moḻi kiḷavi.
translation:
The addresser should formulate his utterance
In terms well-defined and manifest.

title: Human Class Terms Treated as Non-human
transliteration:
kuṭimai āṇmai iḷamai mūppē
aṭimai vaṉmai viruntē kuḻuvē
peṇmai aracē makavē kuḻavi
taṉmai tiri peyar uṟuppiṉ kiḷavi
kātal ciṟappē ceṟaṟcol viṟaṟcol eṉṟu
āvaṟu mūṉṟum uḷappaṭat tokaii
aṉṉa piṟavum avaṟṟoṭu civaṇi
muṉṉattiṉ uṇarum kiḷavi ellām
uyartiṇai maruṅkiṉ nilaiyiṉa āyiṉum
aḵṟiṇai maruṅkiṉ kiḷantāṅku iyalum.
translation:
Stature, masculinity, youth, oldness,
Slavery, strength, guest, council,
Femininity, kingship, progeniture, infancy,
Hermaphrodite, limb being deformed,
Terms of endearment, terms of honour,
Terms of wrath and terms of prowess —
These eighteen terms
And others of their kind too,
Which all feed on thoughts abstract,
Are treated alongside terms of non-human class
Even though they tend to abide as human class terms.

transliteration:
kālam ulakam uyirē uṭampē
pāl varai teyvam viṉaiyē pūtam
ñāyiṟu tiṅkaḷ col eṉa varūum
āyīr aintoṭu piṟavum aṉṉa
āvayiṉ varūum kiḷavi ellām
pāl pirintu icaiyā uyartiṇai mēṉa.
translation:
[To read with 487 and 540]
Time, world, soul, body,
God of Destiny, deed that bears fruits,
The elements (earth, air, fire, water and sky),
Sun, moon and the Word (Goddess Carasvati)
These ten terms
And others of their kind too
Do not mark gender distinctions of the human class words
[They are treated alongside non-human class words].

transliteration: niṉṟāṅku icaittal ivaṇ iyalpu iṉṟē.
translation:
These terms above [54]
Do not mark human class gender distinction
With their form remaining unchanged.

transliteration: icaittalum uriya vēṟiṭattāṉa.
translation:
Where their form finds variation [change of ending],
Human class gender distinction
Informs the words above [541].

title: Nature of Certain Assertions
transliteration: eṭutta moḻi iṉam ceppalum urittē.
translation:
An assertion made
May point to implication cognate.

title: Concord of Limbs in Pairs
transliteration:
kaṇṇum tōḷum mulaiyum piṟavum
paṉmai cuṭṭiya ciṉai nilaik kiḷavi
paṉmai kūṟum kaṭappāṭu ilavē
tam viṉaikku iyalum eḻuttu alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
Limbs in pairs
Such as eye, shoulder and breast
Need no plural suffix
Unless they are followed by plural verbs.

title: Case Types
transliteration: vēṟṟumaitāmē ēḻ eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Seven are the cases,
So is it held.

transliteration: viḷi koḷvataṉkaṇ viḷiyoṭu eṭṭē.
translation:
Vocative, that signals the one addressed, including,
They come to eight in number.

transliteration:
avaitām,
peyar ai oṭu ku
iṉ atu kaṇ viḷi eṉṉum īṟṟa.
translation:
The eight cases are:
The first [nominative] case (peyar vērrumai),
The second [accusative] case (ai - vërrumai),
The third [instrumenta] case (ofu - ` vērrumai),
The fourth [dative] case (ku - vērrumai),
The fifth [ablative] case (iz - vērrumai),
The sixth [genitive] case (atu - verrumai),
The seventh [locative] case (kan - vērrumai)
And the eighth [vocative] case (vili - vērrumai).

title: Nominative Case
transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
eḻuvāy vēṟṟumai peyar tōṉṟu nilaiyē.
translation:
Among them,
The first [nominative] case marks the subject of the sentence.

transliteration:
poruṇmai cuṭṭal viyaṅkoḷa varutal
viṉai nilai uraittal viṉāviṟku ēṟṟal
paṇpu koḷa varutal peyar koḷa varutal eṉṟu
aṉṟi aṉaittum peyarp payaṉilaiyē.
translation:
Where the nominative case marks the subject of the sentence,
The predicate that follows designates
The subject in its agentive role’,
The verb in the optative mood’,
The deed that the verb performs’,
An interrogative sequence‘
An attribute (current or resulting) of the subject’
A substitution subject‘.

transliteration:
peyariṉ ākiya tokaiyumār uḷavē
avvum uriya appālāṉa.
translation:
There are noun phrases
With nouns as the premodified too
Which are in the nominative case as above [550]
As they take predicates after them.

transliteration:
ev vayiṉ peyarum veḷippaṭat tōṉṟi
av iyal nilaiyal cevvitu eṉpa.
translation:
It is appropriate that
Nouns of the three (first, second and third) persons
Occur in forms explicit
As they take predicate after them as above [550].

transliteration:
kūṟiya muṟaiyiṉ urupu nilai tiriyātu
īṟu peyarkku ākum iyaṟkaiya eṉpa.
translation:
As said before [Il3, 116),
The case morphemes [ai, ofu, ku, in, atu, kan]
Get suffixed to the preceding nouns
With no variation in their forms,
So do the learned hold.

transliteration:
peyarnilaik kiḷavi kālam tōṉṟā
toḻil nilai oṭṭum oṉṟu alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
Nouns do not have time reference
Save for finite verbs substituting for nouns*.

title: Accusative Case
transliteration:
iraṇṭākuvatē,
ai eṉap peyariya vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi
ev vaḻi variṉum viṉaiyē viṉaikkuṟippu
av iru mutaliṉ tōṉṟum atuvē.
translation:
The ai morpheme constitutes the second [accusative]
Wherever it occurs,
It is suffixed to the object [affected recipient]
Going with the finite verb' or its appellative?.

transliteration:
kāppiṉ oppiṉ ūrtiyiṉ iḻaiyiṉ
oppiṉ pukaḻiṉ paḻiyiṉ eṉṟā
peṟaliṉ iḻaviṉ kātaliṉ vekuḷiyiṉ
ceṟaliṉ uvattaliṉ kaṟpiṉ eṉṟā
aṟuttaliṉ kuṟaittaliṉ tokuttaliṉ pirittaliṉ
niṟuttaliṉ aḷaviṉ eṇṇiṉ eṉṟā
ākkaliṉ cārtaliṉ celaviṉ kaṉṟaliṉ
nōkkaliṉ añcaliṉ citaippiṉ eṉṟā
aṉṉa piṟavum am mutaṟ poruḷa
eṉṉa kiḷaviyum ataṉ pāla eṉmaṉār.
translation:
The finite verbs or their appellatives — |
Protect, compare, ride (a vehicle), make (build),
Scare away, praise, despise, acquire,
Lose, love, anger, conquer,
Rejoice, learn, sever, shorten,
Gather, divide, weigh, measure,
Count, change, reach, advance,
Be accustomed to, look at, fear, ruin
And others of their kind
Go with the direct object
That takes the ai [accusative] declension as above [555],
Thus goes the norm of usage.

title: Instrumental Case
transliteration:
mūṉṟākuvatē,
oṭu eṉap peyariya vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi
viṉaimutal karuvi aṉai mutaṟṟu atuvē.
translation:
The otu morpheme constitutes the third [instrumental] case;
That marks the agentive or instrumental function.

transliteration:
ataṉiṉ iyaṟal ataṉ taku kiḷavi
ataṉ viṉaippaṭutal ataṉiṉ ātal
ataṉiṉ kōṭal ataṉoṭu mayaṅkal
ataṉoṭu iyainta oru viṉaik kiḷavi
ataṉoṭu iyainta vēṟu viṉaik kiḷavi
ataṉoṭu iyainta oppu al oppu urai
iṉ āṉ ētu īṅku eṉa varūum
aṉṉa piṟavum ataṉ pāla eṉmaṉār.
translation:
The instrumental case above [557] bears on
The material cause of a thing},
The defining attribute of the noun’,
The instrument of an action’,
The becoming due to the given cause’,
An object that facilitates an exchange’,
An object being mixed with another‘,
A common verb for one accompanying another’,
Different verbs for one pairing with another“,
One pairing with another of contrasting nature”,
One that informs the state of limbs and senses",
One that defines the cause of things",
And the ones of the kind above.

title: Dative Case
transliteration:
nāṉkākuvatē,
ku eṉap peyariya vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi
ep poruḷ āyiṉum koḷḷum atuvē.
translation:
The ku morpheme constitutes the fourth (dative) case
That marks the recipient function whatever it be.

transliteration:
ataṟku viṉai uṭaimaiyiṉ ataṟku uṭampaṭutaliṉ
ataṟkup paṭu poruḷiṉ atu āku kiḷaviyiṉ
ataṟku yāppu uṭaimaiyiṉ ataṉ poruṭṭu ātaliṉ
naṭpiṉ pakaiyiṉ kātaliṉ ciṟappiṉ eṉṟu
ap poruṭ kiḷaviyum ataṉ pāla eṉmaṉār.
translation:
The ku declension of nouns and pronouns [559]
Goes with words in concord
That are indirect objects or of recipient function:
The terminal object of an action’,
Subjecting oneself or consenting to an action’,
Thing or quality apportioned and assigned to an object,
That which takes to transformation‘,
That which goes in consonance with another’,
The cause of an effect‘,
And indications of
Friendship’, enmity*^, love’, and eminence",
So has it been said. |

title: Ablative Case
transliteration:
aintākuvatē,
iṉ eṉap peyariya vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi
itaṉiṉ iṟṟu itu eṉṉum atuvē.
translation:
The in morpheme constitutes the fifth [ablative] case
Which points to the nature of an object
As it stands in relation to another object.

transliteration:
vaṇṇam vaṭivē aḷavē cuvaiyē
taṇmai vemmai accam eṉṟā
naṉmai tīmai ciṟumai perumai
vaṉmai meṉmai kaṭumai eṉṟā
mutumai iḷamai ciṟattal iḻittal
putumai paḻamai ākkam eṉṟā
iṉmai uṭaimai nāṟṟam tīrtal
paṉmai ciṉmai paṟṟu viṭutal eṉṟu
aṉṉa piṟavum ataṉ pāla eṉmaṉār.
translation:
The in declension of nouns and pronouns [561]
Goes with words in concord that denote:
Colour, shape, measure, taste,
Coolness, hotness, fear,
Goodness, evil, smallness, largeness,
Hardness, softness, ferocity,
Agedness, youth, superiority, inferiority
Novelty, oldness, source (of becoming)
Absence, possession, smell, going without,
Multitude, fewness, detachment
And others of this kind,
So do the learned hold.

title: Genitive Case
transliteration:
āṟākuvatē,
atu eṉap periya vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi
taṉṉiṉum piṟitiṉum itaṉatu itu eṉum
aṉṉa kiḷavik kiḻamaittu atuvē.
translation:
The atu morpheme constitutes the sixth [genitive]
Which marks the possessive—
The subjective genitive!
And objective genitive’.

transliteration:
iyaṟkaiyiṉ uṭaimaiyiṉ muṟaimaiyiṉ kiḻamaiyiṉ
ceyaṟkaiyiṉ mutumaiyiṉ viṉaiyiṉ eṉṟā
karuviyiṉ tuṇaiyiṉ kalattiṉ mutaliṉ
oruvaḻi uṟuppiṉ kuḻuviṉ eṉṟā
terintu moḻic ceytiyiṉ nilaiyiṉ vāḻcciyiṉ
tirintu vēṟupaṭūum piṟavum aṉṉa
kūṟiya maruṅkiṉ tōṉṟum kiḷavi
āṟaṉ pāla eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The atu declension of nouns and pronouns [563}
Goes with words in concord
That do indicate:
A thing or person's being’,
Possession’, kinship’, relation of things to one another,
Deed done, consummation, occupation,
Instrument, companionship, document.
The whole, limb of a whole, collection,
Structured composition, state, residence,
And such of these as may be contrived to this declension,
Thus does the authority rule.

title: Locative Case
transliteration:
ēḻākuvatē,
kaṇ eṉap peyariya vēṟṟumai kiḷavi
viṉai cey iṭattiṉ nilattiṉ kālattiṉ
aṉai vakaik kuṟippiṉ tōṉṟum atuvē.
translation:
The kaņ morpheme constitutes the seventh [locative] case,
Which points to contexts - situational, temporal? and spatial’.

transliteration:
kaṇ kāl puṟam akam uḷ uḻai kīḻ mēl
piṉ cār ayal puṭai tēvakai eṉāa
muṉ iṭai kaṭai talai valam iṭam eṉāa
aṉṉa piṟavum ataṉ pāla eṉmaṉār.
translation:
The seventh case morpheme kan ramifies into
kaņ', kaf, puram’, akam,
ul, ula, kil, mēř,
pin”, car", ayal", putai“,
Markers of the cardinal points",
mun“, itai”, katai, talai"
valam“, itam" and others of their sort,
So have they been codified.

title: Functional Nature of Case Morphemes
transliteration:
vēṟṟumaip poruḷai virikkum kālai
īṟṟu niṉṟu iyalum tokaivayiṉ pirintu
pal āṟākap poruḷ puṇarntu icaikkum
ellāc collum uriya eṉpa.
translation:
The functions of case morphemes expand severally;
And all such suffixes
As are to senses linked in noun phrases
Do occur as case morphemes,
So has it been ruled.

title: Locative and Accusative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
karumam allāc cārpu eṉ kiḷavikku
urimaiyum uṭaittē kaṇ eṉ vēṟṟumai.
translation:
The seventh case morpheme kan
[Besides the second case morpheme al]
Does go with the noun
As its verb câr [lean] denotes the state of supporting or being supported.

transliteration:
ciṉai nilaik kiḷavikku aiyum kaṇṇum
viṉai nilai okkum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The second case morpheme ai
As well as
The seventh case morpheme kan
Gets suffixed to words designating limbs
As these words realize their verbal concord.

transliteration: kaṉṟalum celavum oṉṟumār viṉaiyē.
translation:
The verbs kanru (be accustomed to) and ce! (advance)
Have their preceding concordant nouns
Take the case morpheme kan besides the case morpheme ai [556].

title: Genitive and Accusative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
mutaṟciṉaik kiḷavikku atu eṉ vēṟṟumai
mutaṟkaṇ variṉē ciṉaikku ai varumē.
translation:
In an utterance
Where the whole precedes its part,
The part takes the second case morpheme ai
If the sixth case morpheme atu goes with the whole.

title: Locative and Accusative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
mutal muṉ ai variṉ kaṇ eṉ vēṟṟumai
ciṉai muṉ varutal teḷḷitu eṉpa.
translation:
That
[In an utterance
Where the whole precedes its part],
The part takes the seventh case morpheme kar
If the second case morpheme ai is suffixed the whole
Is held to be a norm explicit.

title: Context as Criterion
transliteration:
mutalum ciṉaiyum poruḷ vēṟupaṭāa
nuvalum kālai coṟkuṟippiṉavē.
translation:
Not fixed in sense
Are the whole of a thing and its part;
The context of the utterance shall determine them
[As they are governed by relational criteria].

title: Mass' Nouns
transliteration:
piṇṭap peyarum āyiyal tiriyā
paṇṭu iyal maruṅkiṉ marīiya marapē.
translation:
The suffixation of case morpheme
As regards the noun denoting a mass or a pile
Follows the norms mentioned above [57], 572],
A convention it is tradition antique has handed.

title: A Function of Instrumental Case Morpheme
transliteration: oru viṉai oṭuc col uyarpiṉ vaḻittē.
translation:
Where a common verb follows
The preceding noun with the third case otu morpheme
That designates 'one along with another’ [558],
The otu morpheme is suffixed to the superior of the two.

title: Ablative and Instrumental Case Morphemes
transliteration:
mūṉṟaṉum aintaṉum tōṉṟak kūṟiya
ākkamoṭu puṇarnta ētuk kiḷavi
nōkku ōraṉaiya eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
A careful examination shows that
The third case morpheme [otu]
And the fifth case morpheme [in]
Do share the sense signification
As they go with
‘Becoming due to a given cause' [558],
So do the learned hold.

title: ‘Seeing by the Mind's Eye
transliteration:
iraṇṭaṉ maruṅkiṉ nōkku al nōkkam av
iraṇṭaṉ maruṅkiṉ ētuvum ākum.
translation:
The act of seeing
Extending to 'seeing by the mind's eye' [nòkkal] nökkam],
With a reason thereof,
Is governed by third and fifth case declensions
As well as by the second case declension [556].

title: Genitive and Dative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
atu eṉ vēṟṟumai uyartiṇait tokaivayiṉ
atu eṉ urupu keṭa kukaram varumē.
translation:
Where the succeeding word
Is the human generic class [kinship denoting] noun,
The sixth case declension atu of the preceding word
Gets dropped,
And the fourth case morpheme ku takes its place.

title: Instrumental and Accusative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
taṭumāṟu toḻiṟpeyarkku iraṇṭum mūṉṟum
kaṭi nilai ilavē poruḷvayiṉāṉa.
translation:
Where needs to resolve ambiguity in sense
Of the noun with a participle modifier,
Suffixation of second case morpheme [a/]
Or the third case morpheme [ofu]
To the noun
Is not inadmissible.

transliteration:
īṟṟup peyar muṉṉar mey aṟi paṉuvaliṉ
vēṟṟumai teripa uṇarumōrē.
translation:
[Where such ambiguity persists (579)],
The words that follow
The last noun of the utterance
Will bring home the sense intended
To men of discernment.

title: Instrumental and Accusative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
ōmpaṭaik kiḷavikku aiyum āṉum
tām pirivu ilavē tokai varu kālai.
translation:
Both the second case morpheme aj
And the third case morpheme an
Where the noun phrase with an elliptical construction
Goes with the verb that denotes 'protection’.

title: Locative and Genitive Case Morphemes
transliteration:
āṟaṉ maruṅkiṉ vāḻccik kiḻamaikku
ēḻum ākum uṟai nilattāṉa.
translation:
The seventh case morpheme [kan] may there occur
Pointing to place of habitation
Substituting for the sixth case morpheme [atu]
Which informs the act of residing.

title: Dative and Genitive Case Morphemes
transliteration:
kut toka varūum koṭai etir kiḷavi
ap poruḷ āṟaṟku urittum ākum,
translation:
The word declining for the fourth case [ku]
And denoting thereby the recipient of a gift,
Shall take the sixth case morpheme [afu] too.

title: Ablative and Accusative Case Morphemes
transliteration:
accak kiḷavikku aintum iraṇṭum
eccam ilavē poruḷvayiṉāṉa.
translation:
Where the succeeding word points to 'fear',
The preceding noun
Has either the fifth case morpheme [ip]
Or the second case morpheme [ai]
Suffixed to it.

title: Interchange of Case Morphemes in Tune with Usage
transliteration:
aṉṉa piṟavum tol neṟi piḻaiyātu
urupiṉum poruḷiṉum mey taṭumāṟi
iru vayiṉ nilaiyum vēṟṟumai ellām
tiripu iṭaṉ ilavē teriyumōrkkē.
translation:
No lack of propriety do the discerning men find
As one case morpheme substitutes for another
And as one case morpheme points to a sense proper to another,
As shown in instances above
And in others of their kind too
All of which go undeviating from the tradition enduring.

transliteration:
urupu toṭarntu aṭukkiya vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi
oru col naṭaiya poruḷ cel maruṅkē.
translation:
A linear succession of words declining for case morphemes
In an utterance
Has a predicate ending that utterance.

title: Medial/Final Declension
transliteration:
iṟutiyum iṭaiyum ellā urupum
neṟi paṭu poruḷvayiṉ nilavutal varaiyār.
translation:
That
Where the sense intended is in order,
Words declining for case morphemes
May occur medially or finally
In an utterance
Is not inadmissible.

title: Dropping of Case Morphemes
transliteration:
piṟitu piṟitu ēṟṟalum urupu toka varutalum
neṟipaṭa vaḻaṅkiya vaḻi maruṅku eṉpa.
translation:
It is in accord with usage duly set
That there occur interchange of case morphemes
And their getting dropped too
[In relation to their noun stems in an utterance],
So has it been ruled.

transliteration:
aiyum kaṇṇum allāp poruḷvayiṉ
mey urupu tokāa iṟutiyāṉa.
translation:
No case morpheme save for ai and kan
Will stand elided from their nouns
Ai the end of utterances.

title: Contextuality of Case Morphemes
transliteration:
yātaṉ urupiṉ kūṟiṟṟu āyiṉum
poruḷ cel maruṅkiṉ vēṟṟumai cārum.
translation:
Whatever the case morpheme suffixed to nouns in an utterance.
The sense is contrived in accord with the context.

title: Case Morphemes in Negative Utterances
transliteration:
etir maṟuttu moḻiyiṉum tamtam marapiṉ
poruḷ nilai tiriyā vēṟṟumaic collē.
translation:
The case morphemes do not mark change of senses assigned
Even when the utterance takes a negative form.

title: Case Morphemes in Poetry
transliteration:
ku ai āṉ eṉa varūum iṟuti
avvoṭu civaṇum ceyyuḷuḷḷē.
translation:
In poetry,
The endings of case morphemes ku, ai and ān suffixed to nouns
Go pairing with [the particle] a after.

transliteration:
a eṉap piṟattal aḵṟiṇai maruṅkiṉ
kuvvum aiyum il eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
[Of the three morphemes ku, ai and āņ above (592)]
The endings of ku and aj do not pair with a
When they are suffixed to non-human class nouns,
So has it been ruled.

title: Sense Designations of the Dative Case Morpheme
transliteration:
itaṉatu itu iṟṟu eṉṉum kiḷaviyum
ataṉaik koḷḷum poruḷvayiṉāṉum
ataṉāṉ ceyaṟpaṭaṟku otta kiḷaviyum
muṟai koṇṭu eḻunta peyarccol kiḷaviyum
pāl varai kiḷaviyum paṇpiṉ ākkamum
kālattiṉ aṟiyum vēṟṟumaik kiḷaviyum
paṟṟu viṭu kiḷaviyum tīrntu moḻik kiḷaviyum
aṉṉa piṟavum nāṉkaṉ urupiṉ
tol neṟi marapiṉa tōṉṟal āṟē.
translation:
'Such is the nature of the thing that this has",
'One that holds another”,
'The thing that is apt to be done by one",
The nouns that designate kinship‘,
Terms denoting the extent of land delimited*,
One being spoken of in relation to another“,
That which denotes [appropriateness of] time’,
That which denotes sense of detachment“,
That which means 'turning oneself away’
And such of these Xpressions
[Which go with different morphemes]
The fourth case morpheme [ku] stands designate,
Thus goes the tradition of usage known for long.

title: Sense Designation of Other Case Morphemes
transliteration:
ēṉai urupum aṉṉa marapiṉa
māṉam ilavē col muṟaiyāṉa.
translation:
Other case morphemes too
Stand designating things
As does the fourth case morpheme above [594],
And no impropriety entails therein.

title: Things a Predicator Implies
transliteration:
viṉaiyē ceyvatu ceyappaṭuporuḷē
nilaṉē kālam karuvi eṉṟā
iṉṉataṟku itu payaṉ āka eṉṉum
aṉṉa marapiṉ iraṇṭoṭum tokaii
āyeṭṭu eṉpa toḻil mutaṉilaiyē.
translation:
The process, the doer, the object,
The place, the time, the instrument,
The recipient and the effect
Are the eight the learned find
That stand pivoting on the predicator.

transliteration:
avaitām,
vaḻaṅku iyal maruṅkiṉ kuṉṟuva kuṉṟum.
translation:
Among these eight above [596],
Some may remain unapparent
In actual usage.

title: Ramifications of Metonymy
transliteration:
mutaliṉ kūṟum ciṉai aṟi kiḷaviyum
ciṉaiyiṉ kūṟum mutal aṟi kiḷaviyum
piṟantavaḻik kūṟalum paṇpu koḷ peyarum
iyaṉṟatu moḻitalum irupeyaroṭṭum
viṉaimutal uraikkum kiḷaviyoṭu tokaii
aṉai marapiṉavē ākupeyark kiḷavi.
translation:
Metonymy ramifies into
Whole for the part, part for the whole’,
The place of production for the product’,
The characteristic for the object informed by it,
Cause for effect’,
Two-member compounds (one member denoting a part and the other an
And the doer for the thing done’.

transliteration:
avaitām,
tamtam poruḷvayiṉ tammoṭu civaṇalum
oppu il vaḻiyāṉ piṟitu poruḷ cuṭṭalum
ap paṇpiṉavē nuvalum kālai.
translation:
As we analyse them,
Metonyms mark a twofold behaviour:
Those that are akin to things cognate’,
And those that point to things non-cognate?.

transliteration: vēṟṟumai maruṅkiṉ pōṟṟal vēṇṭum.
translation:
The metonymic character above noted [598, 599]
Must be read alongside case morpheme suffixation.

transliteration:
aḷavu niṟaiyum avaṟṟoṭu koḷvaḻi
uḷa eṉa moḻipa uṇarnticiṉōrē.
translation:
Terms denoting measures and weights
Are such
As to be sharing the nature of metonyms,
So is it ruled by the literate.

transliteration:
kiḷanta alla vēṟu piṟa tōṉṟiṉum
kiḷantavaṟṟu iyalāṉ uṇarntaṉar koḷalē.
translation:
Where kinds of metonymy
Look further extendable,
Let them by understood
After what has been treated here.

title: The Vocative Case
transliteration:
viḷi eṉappaṭupa koḷḷum peyaroṭu
teḷiyat tōṉṟum iyaṟkaiya eṉpa.
translation:
Vocative case is
A distinctive signalling
Manifest in the noun that marks it.

transliteration:
avvē,
iv eṉa aṟitaṟku mey peṟak kiḷappa.
translation:
What the vocative case declensions are
Shali need elucidation [here].

title: Vocative Case Markers
transliteration:
avaitām,
i u ai ō eṉṉum iṟuti
ap pāl nāṉkē uyartiṇai maruṅkiṉ
meyp poruḷ cuṭṭiya viḷi koḷ peyarē.
translation:
/1/, /u/, /ai/ and /5/
Are the four vocative case markers
That stand as the word-finals of human class generic nouns.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
i ī ākum ai āy ākum.
translation:
Among these four markers [605],
/1/ gets modified to /i/
And /ai/ to åy.

transliteration: ōvum uvvum ēyoṭu civaṇum.
translation:
Among these four markers [605],
/0/ and /u/
Go pairing with /ê/ added after them.

transliteration: ukaramtāṉē kuṟṟiyalukaram.
translation:
The /u/ [mentioned above (607)]
Is the shortened /u.

transliteration:
ēṉai uyirē uyartiṇai maruṅkiṉ
tām viḷi koḷḷā eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Vowels other than the four above [/i/, /u/. /ai/ and /6/]
Do not decline for the vocative
In the nouns denoting human generic class,
So have the learned ruled.

transliteration:
aḷapeṭai mikūum ikara iṟu peyar
iyaṟkaiya ākum ceyaṟkaiya eṉpa.
translation:
The nouns with /i/ - ending
That take elongation
Do stand with the /i/ unchanged
[/i/ is not modified to /1/ (606).

title: Kinship Terms
transliteration:
muṟaippeyar maruṅkiṉ ai eṉ iṟuti
āvoṭu varutaṟku uriyavum uḷavē.
translation:
/ai/ - endings of kinship terms there are
That are modified to /3/ too
[Instead of being changed to åy (606)].

title: Proximate Addressee
transliteration: aṇmaic collē iyaṟkai ākum.
translation:
Declensions of /i/, /W, /ai/ and /5/
There do not mark
Where the addressee stands near at hand.

title: Consonantal Vocative Markers
transliteration:
ṉa ra la ḷa eṉṉum an nāṉku eṉpa
puḷḷi iṟuti viḷi koḷ peyarē.
translation:
Among the consonants
That occur as the word-finals of human class nouns,
/n, /r/, V and /V/ are the four
That mark the vocative case.

transliteration: ēṉaip puḷḷi īṟu viḷi koḷḷā.
translation:
Words of human generic class
Ending with consonants other than /p, /r/, // and Y
Do not inform the vocative case.

transliteration: aṉ eṉ iṟuti ā ākummē.
translation:
Among the four vocative consonants above [613],
The /n/-fina! an of the nominal element
Stands modified to /a/ in the vocative.

transliteration: aṇmaic colliṟku akaramum ākum.
translation:
The modified /ä/ above [615]
Does turn to /a/
Where the addressee stands near at hand.

transliteration: āṉ eṉ iṟuti iyaṟkai ākum.
translation:
The āån-ending of the nominal element
Does stand unchanged
As it constitutes the vocative.

transliteration:
toḻiliṉ kūṟum āṉ eṉ iṟuti
āy ākummē viḷivayiṉāṉa.
translation:
The an-endings of verbal nouns
Are modified to āy
As they decline for the vocative case.

transliteration: paṇpu koḷ peyarum ataṉ ōraṟṟē.
translation:
The change above [618]
Does mark the nouns denoting attributes too
[an-ending modified to åy].

transliteration: aḷapeṭaip peyarē aḷapeṭai iyala.
translation:
The nouns with ån-ending
That take elongation before
Do behave in the way
As do the nouns with /i/-ending
That take elongation [610]
[The n-ending remains undeclining
And it is the elongation of more than two phonic
n-ending Vocatives

transliteration: muṟaippeyark kiḷavi ēyoṭu varumē.
translation:
Kinship terms with /n/-ending
Take the vocative particle /ē/ after them.

transliteration:
tāṉ eṉ peyarum cuṭṭumutaṟ peyarum
yāṉ eṉ peyarum viṉāviṉ peyarum
aṉṟi aṉaittum viḷi kōḷ ilavē.
translation:
The [mixed person] pronoun fan,
The pronouns with demonstrative initials /a/, /i/ and /w,
The first person singular pronoun yan,
And the interrogative pronoun [yavan] —
None of these declines for the vocative case.
r-ending Vocatives

transliteration: ārum aruvum īroṭu civaṇum.
translation:
Vocative case declension
Finds the endings år and ar of [human class] nominal terms
Turned into 1r.

transliteration:
toḻiṟpeyar āyiṉ ēkāram varutalum
vaḻukku iṉṟu eṉmaṉār vayaṅkiyōrē.
translation:
Where it is a verbal noun,
No flaw there entails
If the ár and ar endings
Are turned into îr [as above 623],
And the vocative particle /ë/ is suffixed to r,
So do men of erudition hold.

transliteration: paṇpu koḷ peyarum ataṉ ōraṟṟē.
translation:
Nouns denoting the attributes of one
Do behave in the way as above [623, 624]
[ar and ar changed into īr
And īr taking the vocative particle /&ë/].

transliteration: aḷapeṭaip peyarē aḷapeṭai iyala.
translation:
The nouns with /r/-ending
Preceded by elongation
Do behave in the way
As do nouns with /p/-ending
That take elongation [620]
[The /r/-ending remains undeclining
And it is the elongation of more than two phonic measures]

transliteration: cuṭṭumutaṟ peyarē muṉ kiḷantaṉṉa.
translation:
The /r/-ending demonstrative [avar, ivar, uvar]
Are of the nature of -ending above [622]
[They do not decline for the vocative case].

transliteration:
nummiṉ tiripeyar viṉāviṉ peyar eṉṟu
am muṟai iraṇṭum avaṟṟu iyalpu iyalum.
translation:
The two forms —
nyir the modified form of the pronoun num,
And the /r/-ending interrogative pronoun yãåvar
Do go after the demonstrative pronouns above [627]
[They do not decline for the vocative case].
l and J - ending Vocatives

transliteration:
eñciya iraṇṭiṉ iṟutip peyarē
niṉṟa īṟṟu ayal nīṭṭam vēṇṭum.
translation:
As for the nouns with the other two consonantal endings [/l/ and A),
They take the vocative form
With their penultimate vowels lengthened [see 613].

transliteration: ayal neṭitu āyiṉ iyaṟkai ākum.
translation:
Vocative it is without lengthening [as above (629)]
Where the penultimate phoneme is a long vowel.

transliteration:
viṉaiyiṉum paṇpiṉum
niṉaiyat tōṉṟum āḷ eṉ iṟuti
āy ākummē viḷivayiṉāṉa.
translation:
Examination of usage shows that
Verbal nouns and nouns designating one's attribute
Have their å] - ending
Changed to åy in the vocative case.

transliteration: muṟaippeyark kiḷavi muṟaippeyar iyala.
translation:
/YV-ending kinship terms
Take to the same mode
As the /n-ending ones [621]
[They take the vocative particle /ë/ after them).

transliteration:
cuṭṭumutaṟ peyarum viṉāviṉ peyarum
muṉ kiḷantaṉṉa eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
//-final demonstrative pronouns [ava], ivaļ, uva]
And /V-final interrogative pronoun [yava]
Are of the same nature
As the demonstratives and interrogatives mentioned before [622, 627]
[They do not decline for the vocative case],
So do the literate hold.

transliteration: aḷapeṭaip peyarē aḷapeṭai iyala.
translation:
/VV-final and /lV-final words
Preceded by elongation
Behave in the manner of
/n/- and /r/-final words
Preceded by elongation [616, 620, 626]
[The word-final remains undeclining
And the elongation marks more than two phonic measures]

title: Mixed Generic Class in the Vocative
transliteration:
kiḷanta iṟuti aḵṟiṇai viravuppeyar
viḷampiya neṟiya viḷikkum kālai.
translation:
Nouns common to human and non-human classes
With the word-finals mentioned above
[/i/, W, /ai/, /3/ and /w, /r/, /1/, / (606, 613)]
Behave in the vocative case
As do the nouns of human generic class.

title: Non-human Class in the Vocative
transliteration:
puḷḷiyum uyirum iṟuti ākiya
aḵṟiṇai maruṅkiṉ ellāp peyarum
viḷi nilai peṟūum kālam tōṉṟiṉ
teḷi nilai uṭaiya ēkāram varalē.
translation:
Where a need arises for them to take the vocative,
Consonant-ending and vowel-ending nouns
That belong to the non-human generic class,
Take the vocative particle /ë8/
Marked explicitly after their word-finals.

title: Vocative for the Non-proximate Addressee
transliteration:
uḷa eṉappaṭṭa ellāp peyarum
aḷapu iṟantaṉavē viḷikkum kālai
cēymaiyiṉ icaikkum vaḻakkattāṉa.
translation:
All the nouns referred to so far
Which find declension in the vocative case
Have the phonic measures of their vowels increased
Where one seeks the attention of the addressee at a distance.

transliteration:
amma eṉṉum acaiccol nīṭṭam
am muṟaippeyaroṭu civaṇātu āyiṉum
viḷiyoṭu koḷpa teḷiyumōrē.
translation:
The expletive particle amma.
No kinship term though it is,
Has its final /a/ lengthened
To draw the addressee's attention,
And men of discernment find it
Declension in the vocative case.

title: Indeclinable Terms
transliteration:
ta na nu e eṉa avai mutal ākit
taṉmai kuṟitta ṉa ra ḷa eṉ iṟutiyum
aṉṉa piṟavum peyar nilai variṉē
iṉmai vēṇṭum viḷiyoṭu koḷalē.
translation:
Relationship designating nominal terms
Which have ta, na, nu and /e/ for word-initials
And /yp, /r/ and /V/ for word-finals,
And terms of their sort
Do not decline for the vocative case.

title: Words as Sense Units
transliteration: ellāc collum poruḷ kuṟittaṉavē.
translation: All words are sense designators.

title: Form and Meaning
transliteration:
poruṇmai teritalum coṉmai teritalum
colliṉ ākum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The meaning and the form
Stand revealed through the word,
So do the learned hold.

title: Twofold Sense Designation
transliteration:
teripu vēṟu nilaiyalum kuṟippiṉ tōṉṟalum
iru pāṟṟu eṉpa poruṇmai nilaiyē.
translation:
The sense stands classified in two ways:
Direct signification' and suggestive implied sense.

title: Primary Word Classes
transliteration:
col eṉappaṭupa peyarē viṉai eṉṟu

translation:
All these foregoing indeclinable terms,
That are in vogue and use,
Have their sense designations
In the contexts of words preceding and succeeding them,
And in relation to the words they define or inform.
They reveal their sense thus in accord with usage.

Conveyed in terms explicit,
The meanings mark no obscurity.

For one to draw in the untreated
The varied indeclinables of varying contexts;
And to determine their sense-designations
One should therefore go in accord
With the ruling conventions of usage
Holding them to be the law of protection,
And should make appropriate sense of them each,
So have the learned laid it down.

iyarcol, tiricol, ticaiccołl and vațacol.

That is in accord with the usage in the Tamil land,
And that occurs with its semantic core unaffected.

Comprises four kinds:

Wherein.
Nouns and verbs defining the order,
Words of one group in an utterance
Are linked for sense
With corresponding words of another group in the same utterance.
Cuņņam

Cunnņam is the mode of construing
Wherein,
Words in a two-lined stanza
Of four feet each
Are transposed in a deft manner,
And the meaning is construed
By finding their order right.

By finding the order of lines right.

translation:

It is not disallowed that
The final foot of the last line
Gets linked to a preceding foot
For the meaning to be construed.
