title: Adjectival Compounds
transliteration:
vaṇṇattiṉ vaṭiviṉ aḷaviṉ cuvaiyiṉ eṉṟu
aṉṉa piṟavum ataṉ kuṇam nutali
iṉṉatu itu eṉa varūum iyaṟkai
eṉṉa kiḷaviyum paṇpiṉtokaiyē.
translation:
Adjectival compounds are those
Wherein
The first member carries designations of quality
Such as colour, shape, extent and taste
By which is the second member informed.

transliteration:
iru peyar pala peyar aḷaviṉpeyarē
eṇṇiyaṟpeyarē niṟaippeyark kiḷavi
eṇṇiṉpeyaroṭu av aṟu kiḷaviyum
kaṇṇiya nilaittē ummaittokaiyē.
translation:
Conjunctive relations compounds are those
Wherein
Two nouns’, several nouns’
Nouns denoting measures`,
Nouns denoting objects enumerated‘,
Nouns denoting weight’
And enumerative nouns‘
Stand in conjunctive relations
[With elliptical conjunctive morpheme {um) in between}.

title: Compounds of Elliptical Head
transliteration:
paṇpu toka varūum kiḷaviyāṉum
ummai tokka peyarvayiṉāṉum
vēṟṟumai tokka peyarvayiṉāṉum
īṟṟu niṉṟu iyalum aṉmoḻittokaiyē.
translation:
There marks the compound of elliptical head
Wherein precede
Nouns with ellipticąl attribute designation,
Nouns with elliptical conjunctive morpheme
Or nouns with elliptical case morphemes
[With the elliptical head of the compound in the end]

transliteration:
avaitām,
muṉ moḻi nilaiyalum piṉ moḻi nilaiyalum
iru moḻi mēlum oruṅkuṭaṉ nilaiyalum
am moḻi nilaiyātu al moḻi nilaiyalum
an nāṉku eṉpa poruḷ nilai marapē.
translation:
Four kinds of sense focus compound words mark:
Focus on the following element!,
Focus on the first element of the compound’,
Simultaneous focus on both the elements’
And focus on the elliptical head beyond these elements‘,
So has it been ruled.

title: Compounds as Single Words
transliteration: ellāt tokaiyum oru col naṭaiya.
translation:
All compounds [referred to above (895)] behave
As do single words.

transliteration:
uyartiṇai maruṅkiṉ ummaittokaiyē
palarcol naṭaittu eṉa moḻimaṉār pulavar.
translation:
In the human generic class,
Compounds connected by elliptical um morpheme
Take the plural inflection,
So do the learned hold.

title: Pathetic Fallacy
transliteration:
vārā marapiṉa varak kūṟutalum
eṉṉā marapiṉa eṉak kūṟutalum
aṉṉavai ellām avaṟṟu avaṟṟu iyalpāṉ
iṉṉa eṉṉum kuṟippurai ākum.
translation:
Attributing to stative objects
Qualities that mark the dynamic ones,
Attributing communicative functions
To objects not given to such functions,
And attributions such as these
Are all suggestive references to the nature of the objects given.

title: Reduplication of Euphonic Terms
transliteration: icaip paṭu poruḷē nāṉku varampu ākum.
translation:
Reduplication of euphonic complements [894]
Marks a four-time repetition for the upper limit.

title: Reduplication of 'Swift' Words
transliteration: virai col aṭukkē mūṉṟu varampu ākum.
translation:
Words designating swiftness and immediacy
Mark a three-time repetition for the upper limit.

title: Empty Morphemes in Reduplication
transliteration:
kaṇṭīr eṉṟā koṇṭīr eṉṟā
ceṉṟatu eṉṟā pōyiṟṟu eṉṟā
aṉṟi aṉaittum viṉāvoṭu civaṇi
niṉṟa vaḻi acaikkum kiḷavi eṉpa.
translation:
When they take the interrogative terminations,
The terms kanțtir, koņtfir, cenratu and põōyirru [in reduplication]
Are but empty morphemes [signalling attention],
So has it been ruled.

transliteration:
kēṭṭai eṉṟā niṉṟai eṉṟā
kāttai eṉṟā kaṇṭai eṉṟā
aṉṟi aṉaittum muṉṉilai al vaḻi
muṉṉuṟak kiḷanta iyalpu ākummē.
translation:
When they do not denote the second person,
The terms kêttai, ninrai, kattai and kaņtai
Are empty morphemes as above [908].

title: The Finite Verb
transliteration:
iṟappiṉ nikaḻviṉ etirviṉ eṉṟa
ciṟappuṭai marapiṉ am muk kālamum
taṉmai muṉṉilai paṭarkkai eṉṉum
am mū iṭattāṉ viṉaiyiṉum kuṟippiṉum
meymmaiyāṉum iv iraṇṭu ākum
av āṟu eṉpa muṟṟu iyal moḻiyē.
translation:
The finite verb
Shows three tenses - the past, present and future,
Which is its trait distinctive and explicit;
It marks the three persons - the first person, second person and third
Into two categories it falls - verbs with explicit tense markers and appellativeverbs;
Each of these two categories
Taking human class, non-human class and mixed class forms,
The finite verb branches into six,
So has it been ruled.

transliteration: ev vayiṉ viṉaiyum av iyal nilaiyum.
translation:
All classes of finite verbs
Go in accord with the norms above [910].

transliteration:
avaitām,
tamtam kiḷavi aṭukkuna variṉum
et tiṟattāṉum peyar muṭipiṉavē.
translation:
These finite verbs,
Even as they occur in succession,
Shall go with a nominal element
Either explicitly or implicitly.

title: Forms of Incomplete Signification
transliteration:
pirinilai viṉaiyē peyarē oḻiyicai
etirmaṟai ummai eṉavē collē
kuṟippē icaiyē āyīr aintum
neṟippaṭat tōṉṟum eñcu poruṭ kiḷavi.
translation:
Teri are the incomplete significations:
Forms of [implied] exclusion, participial forms, relative participles,
Suggestive [elliptical] forms, forms of fimplied] negation,
Elliptical conjunctive forms, ena forms,
Sentence ellipsis, forms of inference
And euphonic [elliptical] forms.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
pirinilai eccam pirinilai muṭipiṉa.
translation:
Forms of [elliptical] exclusion are those
Wherein
The term that stands excluded [in ellipsis]
Marks the completion of sense.

transliteration:
viṉaiyeñcukiḷavikku viṉaiyum kuṟippum
niṉaiyat tōṉṟiya muṭipu ākummē
āvayiṉ kuṟippē ākkamoṭu varumē.
translation:
As for participial forms,
There follow
The verb with explicit tense marker and the appellative verb
To complete the sense;
Where the appellative verb occurs,
1t is marked by the sense of becoming’.

transliteration: peyareñcukiḷavi peyaroṭu muṭimē.
translation:
Premodifiers of relative clauses
Take [an elliptical] noun after them.

transliteration: oḻiyicai eccam oḻiyicai muṭipiṉa.
translation:
Premodifiers of clauses with implied heads
Have those implied heads as sense complements.

transliteration: etirmaṟai eccam etirmaṟai muṭipiṉa.
translation:
Premodifiėrs of clauses with negative forms
Take [elliptical] heads that imply the negative.

transliteration:
ummai eccam iru īṟṟāṉum
taṉ viṉai oṉṟiya muṭipu ākummē.
translation:
Premodifiers of clauses with um connectives
Have implied premodifier with um connective
Going with the same verb.

transliteration:
taṉmēl ceñcol varūum kālai
nikaḻum kālamoṭu vārāk kālamum
iṟanta kālamoṭu vārāk kālamum
mayaṅkutal varaiyār muṟainilaiyāṉa.
translation:
Where the [elliptical] preceding term unsuffixed by um connective
Is in present tense or past tense,
The occurrence of the succeeding term in the future tense
Is not disallowed.

transliteration: eṉa eṉ eccam viṉaiyoṭu muṭimē.
translation:
[In elliptical constructions]
The relative clause connective morpheme
Has a succeeding finite verb
For the sense to be completed.

transliteration:
eñciya mūṉṟum mēl vantu muṭikkum
eñcu poruṭ kiḷavi ila eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The remaining three forms —
Sentence ellipsis, forms of inference and euphonic elliptical forms [913] —
Do have no elliptical forms
By which to complete the sense.

transliteration:
avaitām,
tamtam kuṟippiṉ eccam ceppum.
translation:
These three [922]
Look to the respective contexts
For sense to attain completion.

transliteration:
col eṉ eccam muṉṉum piṉṉum
col aḷavu allatu eñcutal iṉṟē.
translation:
Sentence ellipsis is that
Where there stands an elliptical word
Either at the beginning
Ọr at the end
For the sense to be completed.

title: Conventions of Use of Certain Classes of Words
transliteration: avaiyal kiḷavi maṟaittaṉar kiḷattal.
translation:
Expressions unfit for use in an assembly,
Must be substituted by words indirect and mild.

transliteration: maṟaikkum kālai marīiyatu orāal.
translation:
We go not for euphemistic expressions [925],
For such terms as are in vogue and use for long.

transliteration:
ī tā koṭu eṉak kiḷakkum mūṉṟum
iraviṉ kiḷavi āku iṭaṉ uṭaiya.
translation:
The three verbs 1, tā and kotu
Designate acts of begging and entreaty.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
ī eṉ kiḷavi iḻintōṉ kūṟṟē.
translation:
Of these three [927],
The verb 7
Has one of inferior standing for the beneficiary.

transliteration: tā eṉ kiḷavi oppōṉ kūṟṟē.
translation:
Of these three [927],
The verb tå
Represents the giver and recipient
As being of equal status.

transliteration: koṭu eṉ kiḷavi uyarntōṉ kūṟṟē.
translation:
Of these three [927],
The verb kotu
Has the recipient
Standing superior to the giver.

transliteration:
koṭu eṉ kiḷavi paṭarkkai āyiṉum
taṉṉaip piṟaṉ pōl kūṟum kuṟippiṉ
taṉṉiṭattu iyalum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Although the verb kotțu [give] is in the third person,
It is treated as belonging to the first person
When the addresser-recipient: speaks of himself in the third person,
So do the learned hold. > .

title: Classes of Words Outside the Conventions
transliteration:
peyarnilaik kiḷaviyiṉ āakunavum
ticainilai kiḷaviyiṉ āakunavum
tol neṟi moḻivayiṉ āakunavum
meyn nilai mayakkiṉ āakunavum
mantirap poruḷvayiṉ āakunavum
aṉṟi aṉaittum kaṭappāṭu ilavē.
translation:
Nouns designating either of the human and non-human class names,
Dialectal words specific to the twelve regions of the Tamil land,
Antique expressions coming down through usage long,
Significations transferred from one to another of cognate objects,
Incantatory formulaic expressions,
And expressions of such of these classes
Do not stand confined to norms and conventions set.

title: Residual Norms of Usage
transliteration:
ceyyāy eṉṉum muṉṉilai viṉaiccol
cey eṉ kiḷavi āku iṭaṉ uṭaittē.
translation:
Contexts there are too
Where
The second person singular verb of the formulaic pattern ceyyäy
Does come to substitute for verbs of cey pattern.

transliteration:
muṉṉilai muṉṉar īyum ēyum
an nilai marapiṉ mey ūrntu varumē.
kaṭi col illai kālattup paṭiṉē.
translation:
Neologisms,
As they find a context alive,
Are not discardable.

transliteration: kuṟaiccoṟ kiḷavi kuṟaikkum vaḻi aṟital.
translation:
Omission of letter(s) in a word is in order
Where sense and norm do permit.

transliteration: kuṟaittaṉa āyiṉum niṟaip peyar iyala.
translation:
Omission of letter(s) there is though,
The resulting word stands complete in form and sense.

transliteration: iṭaiccol ellām vēṟṟumaic collē.
translation:
The structural morphemes
Facilitate sense distinctions
[Of nouns and verbs].

transliteration: uriccol maruṅkiṉum uriyavai uriya.
translation:
Among the indeclinables too
There are those
That modify the sense
[Of nouns and verbs].

transliteration: viṉaiyeñcukiḷaviyum vēṟu pal kuṟiya.
translation:
Verbal participles too
Assume varied grammatical forms.

transliteration: uraiyiṭattu iyalum uṭaṉilai aṟital.
translation:
It is the context in connected speech
That determines the sense contiguity
Of words of apparent contradiction.

transliteration:
muṉṉattiṉ uṇarum kiḷaviyum uḷavē
iṉṉa eṉṉum col muṟaiyāṉa.
translation:
There are cases in discourse
Where
The speaker's intention too
Points to the sense conveyed.

transliteration: oru poruḷ iru col pirivu ila varaiyār.
translation:
Two terms that denote the same sense
Going together
Is not debarred.

transliteration:
orumai cuṭṭiya peyar nilaik kiḷavi
paṉmaikku ākum iṭaṉumār uṇṭē.
translation:
There are contexts
Where
A noun in the singular number
Will designate plural sense too.

transliteration:
muṉṉilai cuṭṭiya orumaik kiḷavi
paṉmaiyoṭu muṭiyiṉum varai nilai iṉṟē
āṟṟuppaṭai maruṅkiṉ pōṟṟal vēṇṭum.
translation:
Especially in modes of utterance
Where one guides another towards a goal beneficial,
The second person singular
Taking a plural verb
1s not disallowed.

transliteration:
ceyyuḷ maruṅkiṉum vaḻakkiyal maruṅkiṉum
mey peṟak kiḷanta kiḷavi ellām
pal vēṟu ceytiyiṉ nūl neṟi piḻaiyātu
col varaintu aṟiya pirittaṉar kāṭṭal.
translation:
One should go in for classification and analysis
Of what all has been treated explicitly here
In accord with conventions in literature and life
With the norms of usage being kept unviolated.
SEMANTICS - POETICS

title: The Modes of Akam Love Behaviour
transliteration:
kaikkiḷai mutalāp peruntiṇai iṟuvāy
muṟpaṭak kiḷanta eḻu tiṇai eṉpa.
translation:
Primarily,
The Akam love behaviour
Comprises seven strands
From kaikkilai through peruntinņai,
So has it been held.

title: Geographical Identities to the Modes of Akam Love
transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
naṭuvaṇ aintiṇai naṭuvaṇatu oḻiya
paṭu tirai vaiyam pāttiya paṇpē.
translation:
The sea-girt world
Stands apportioned
To the middle five* of these strands [947]
Save for the middle of the five.

title: The Structural Constituents of Akam Poetry
transliteration:
mutal karu uripporuḷ eṉṟa mūṉṟē
nuvalum kālai muṟai ciṟantaṉavē
pāṭaluḷ payiṉṟavai nāṭum kālai.
translation:
Mutarporul, karupporuļ and uripporul*
In this order of precedence
Do define the structure of [Akam] poetry,
Which on examination one discerns.

title: Mutarporul
transliteration:
mutal eṉappaṭuvatu nilam poḻutu iraṇṭiṉ
iyalpu eṉa moḻipa iyalpu uṇarntōrē.
translation:
Mutarporuj is
Aspects of land and time,
So do men of discernment find.

title: The Landscape Division
transliteration:
māyōṉ mēya kāṭu uṟai ulakamum
cēyōṉ mēya mai varai ulakamum
vēntaṉ mēya tīm puṉal ulakamum
varuṇaṉ mēya peru maṇal ulakamum
mullai kuṟiñci marutam neytal eṉac
colliya muṟaiyāṉ collavum paṭumē.
translation:
The forest tract which Māayön* tends,
The hilly tract which Cêēyön* tends,
The fertile cultivable tract which Ventan* tends
And the littoral tract which Varuņan* tends
Are known to be
Mullai, kuriñci, marutam and neytal respectively.

title: Season and Time
transliteration: kārum mālaiyum mullai.
translation:
The rainy season and evening
Arê assigned to the forest tract*.

title: The Hilly Tract
transliteration:
kuṟiñci,
kūtir yāmam eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The learned find
The cold season and midnight hour
Assigned to the hilly tract.

transliteration: paṉi etir paruvamum urittu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The early dewy season
Does also go with the hilly tract,
So has it been said.

title: The Cultivable Tract
transliteration: vaikaṟai viṭiyal marutam.
translation:
The wee hours just before daybreak
Are assigned to the cultivable tract.

title: The Littoral Tract
transliteration:
eṟpāṭu,
neytal ātal mey peṟat tōṉṟum.
translation:
The day's close before sunset
Belongs to the littoral tract.

title: The Arid Tract
transliteration:
naṭuvunilait tiṇaiyē naṇpakal vēṉiloṭu
muṭivu nilai maruṅkiṉ muṉṉiya neṟittē.
translation:
As we see it,
The hot season and midday hour
Go with the centrally placed [arid] tract.

transliteration: piṉpaṉitāṉum urittu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The late dewy season
Is also held to be proper to the arid tract.

title: Two Modes of Separation
transliteration:
iru vakaip pirivum nilai peṟat tōṉṟalum
uriyatu ākum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The two modes of separation
[The hero parting from the heroine on his male quest,
And the hero and heroine going on elopement)]*
Do stand assigned to the arid tract,
So do the learned men hold.

title: Acceptable Deviation
transliteration:
tiṇai mayakkuṟutalum kaṭi nilai ilavē
nilaṉ oruṅku mayaṅkutal ila eṉa moḻipa
pulaṉ naṉku uṇarnta pulamaiyōrē.
translation:
That
Aspects of land and time
Assigned to a given tract
Do get mixed with those of another tract
Is no deviation unacceptable;
Yet,
No commingling is permitted among the tracts themselves;
So goes the norm by men of discernment.

transliteration: uripporuḷ allaṉa mayaṅkavum peṟumē.
translation:
Those [aspects of land and time, and distinctive features of the tracts]
Other than the Akam love behaviour
Do mark intermingling.

title: The Fivefold Akam Love Behaviour
transliteration:
puṇartal pirital iruttal iraṅkal
ūṭal avaṟṟiṉ nimittam eṉṟivai
tērum kālai tiṇaikku uripporuḷē.
translation:
Union, separation, endurance
Pining and sulking,
And the motives therein
Are perceived to be
The strands of Akam love behaviour
[Proper to the five tracts of kuriñci, pālai, mullai, neytal and marutam respectively].

transliteration:
koṇṭu talaikkaḻitalum pirintu avaṇ iraṅkalum
uṇṭu eṉa moḻipa ōr iṭattāṉa.
translation:
Elopement of the hero with the heroine
And the pining of her kin thereon
Are events marked too at times though.

transliteration: kalanta poḻutum kāṭciyum aṉṉa.
translation:
So are the occurrences
Attending on
The encounter and the first sight
Of the heroine by the hero.

transliteration: mutal eṉappaṭuvatu āyiru vakaittē.
translation:
Mutalporuļ comprises two aspects
[Of land and time],
As noted above [950].

title: The Physical Features of Land
transliteration:
teyvam uṇāvē mā maram puḷ paṟai
ceyti yāḻiṉ pakutiyoṭu tokaii
av vakai piṟavum karu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
God, food, animal, tree,
Bird, drum, occupation and lute
And such of these
Constitute the distinctive physical features of the given tract of land.

transliteration:
en nila maruṅkiṉ pūvum puḷḷum
an nilam poḻutoṭu vārā āyiṉum
vanta nilattiṉ payatta ākum.
translation:
Where the flora and fauna occur
Not marked proper to the land and season in question though,
They be deemed
Characteristic of that land and that season.

title: The Naming of Characters
transliteration:
peyarum viṉaiyum eṉṟu āyiru vakaiya
tiṇaitoṟum marīiya tiṇai nilaip peyarē.
translation:
The persons that people a tract of land
Have names specific to that region;
These names fall into two categories:
Names in tune with the mores of the region
And names derived from occupations of that region.

transliteration:
āyar vēṭṭuvar āṭūut tiṇaip peyar
āvayiṉ varūum kiḻavarum uḷarē.
translation:
Cowherds and huntsmen
Designate region-specific persons of the masculine gender;
There are other names of principal characters such as these too
Drawn that they are on the region's occupation.

transliteration:
ēṉōr maruṅkiṉum eṇṇum kālai
āṉā vakaiya tiṇai nilaip peyarē.
translation:
We find on reflection that
Inhabitants of other regions too
Have their names derived from the mores of their region
And from the occupation of that region.
Lowly men as Akam Personae

transliteration:
aṭiyōr pāṅkiṉum viṉaivalar pāṅkiṉum
kaṭivarai ila puṟattu eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
That
Men in servitude and those of the attendant class
Find portrayed as personae
In kaikkiļai and peruntiņai modes of love,
Which lie outside the sphere of the 'middle five'
Is not debarred,
So do the learned hold.

transliteration:
ēval marapiṉ ēṉōrum uriyar
ākiya nilaimai avarum aṉṉar.
translation:
Such representation in kaikkiļai and peruntiņai [971]
Does mark men of other menial occupations too.

title: Modes of Separation
transliteration: ōtal pakaiyē tūtu ivai pirivē.
translation:
Pursuit of learning,
Call of war against foemen
And missions ambassadorial
Will occasion the hero's parting from thè Tieroite.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
ōtalum tūtum uyarntōr mēṉa.
translation:
Of these three [973],
Pursuit of learning
And ambassadorial mission
Are proper to men of superior social classes.

transliteration:
tāṉē cēṟalum taṉṉoṭu civaṇiya
ēṉōr cēṟalum vēntaṉ mēṟṟē.
translation:
Going on war against his own enemy
And going as help to the king facing hostilities
Will be occasions
For a king to stand separated from his love.

transliteration:
mēviya ciṟappiṉ ēṉōr paṭimaiya
mullai mutalāc colliya muṟaiyāṉ
piḻaittatu piḻaiyātu ākal vēṇṭiyum
iḻaitta oṇ poruḷ muṭiyavum pirivē.
translation:
Conduct of prayers and festivities
For those of abiding note other than the humans (i.e. deities);
Restoration of righteousness where it turns deviant |
In all regions extending through the forest tract:
And to make riches through virtue abroad |
Are occasions too
For the hero to remain parted from the heroine.*

transliteration: mēlōr muṟaimai nālvarkkum urittē.
translation:
The conduct of prayers and festivities [976]
Stands enjoined on the inhabitants of the four regions.*

transliteration: maṉṉar pāṅkiṉ piṉṉōr ākupa.
translation:
The administering of righteous conduct [976]
Also rests upon the classes [merchants and farmers]
Next in order to the king.

transliteration: uyarntōrkku uriya ōttiṉāṉa.
translation:
Separation on account of learning
Is proper to men of superior classes.

transliteration:
vēntu viṉai iyaṟkai vēntaṉ orīiya
ēṉōr maruṅkiṉum eytu iṭaṉ uṭaittē.
translation:
Apart from the king,
The other classes of people
Are at times
Enjoined on the kingly functions.

transliteration: poruḷvayiṉ piritalum avarvayiṉ urittē.
translation:
Quest for wealth
Occasioning separation
Marks those (merchant class and cultivators)
Other than the rulers of the land too.

transliteration: uyarntōr poruḷvayiṉ oḻukkattāṉa.
translation:
As men of upper strata
Part from their loves in quest of riches,
They do so
To uphold the mores they live by.

title: Voyage on the Sea
transliteration: munnīr vaḻakkam makaṭūuvoṭu illai.
translation:
The hero does not take the heroine with him
While he undertakes a voyage on the seas.
A Convention on Palmyra-horse riding

transliteration:
ettiṇai maruṅkiṉum makaṭūu maṭalmēl
poṟpuṭai neṟimai iṉmaiyāṉa.
translation:
No strand of Akam love behaviour
Does enjoin on the heroine
To ride the horse of palmyra stems,
As it goes contrary to the norms of feminine propriety.

title: Utterance by the Heroine's Mother
transliteration:
taṉṉum avaṉum avaḷum cuṭṭi
maṉṉum nimittam moḻip poruḷ teyvam
naṉmai tīmai accam cārtal eṉṟu
aṉṉa piṟavum avaṟṟoṭu tokaii
muṉṉiya kālam mūṉṟuṭaṉ viḷakki
tōḻi tēettum kaṇṭō r pāṅkiṉum
pōkiya tiṟattu naṟṟāy pulampalum
ākiya kiḷaviyum av vaḻi uriya.
translation:
As the heroine goes on elopement with the hero,
The utterances appropriate to her mother are:
She would pour out her anguished concern
To the
She would speak prognostications
Referring to predictions unsought and divinations and
Weighing the good and bad that might befall the lovers,
Expressing apprehensions about the path they trod
And about the help that might come their way,
Reflecting the past, the now and the future of her daughter.

title: Foster-mother in Search of the Eloped Heroine
transliteration:
ēmap pērūrc cēriyum curattum
tāmē cellum tāyarum uḷarē.
translation:
There are mothers (and foster-mothers) too
Who go themselves
In search of their daughters
[Gone on elopement with their lovers]
Along the streets of well-guarded towns
And through arid desert-like tracts.

title: A Convention of Elopement as Separation
transliteration: ayalōr āyiṉum akaṟci mēṟṟē.
translation:
Even when the elopement takes the lovers
To another house close by within the town,
It is to be regarded as separation mode
[Of the Akam love conduct].

title: Utterance by the Confidante
transliteration:
talaivarum viḻuma nilai eṭuttu uraippiṉum
pōkkaṟkaṇṇum viṭuttaṟkaṇṇum
nīkkaliṉ vanta tam uṟu viḻumamum
vāymaiyum poymmaiyum kaṇṭō ṟ cuṭṭit
tāy nilai nōkkit talaippeyarttuk koḷiṉum
nōy mikap perukit taṉ neñcu kaluḻntōḷai
aḻintatu kaḷai eṉa moḻintatu kūṟi
vaṉpuṟai neruṅki vantataṉ tiṟattoṭu
eṉṟu ivai ellām iyalpuṟa nāṭiṉ
oṉṟit tōṉṟum tōḻi mēṉa.

title: Utterance by the Passers-by
transliteration:
poḻutum āṟum uṭku varat tōṉṟi
vaḻuviṉ ākiya kuṟṟam kāṭṭalum
ūratu cārpum cellum tēyamum
ārva neñcamoṭu ceppiya vaḻiyiṉum
puṇarntōr pāṅkiṉ puṇarnta neñcamoṭu
aḻintu etir kūṟi viṭuppiṉum āṅkat
tāy nilai kaṇṭu taṭuppiṉum viṭuppiṉum
cēy nilaikku akaṉṟōr celaviṉum varaviṉum
kaṇṭō r moḻital kaṇṭatu eṉpa.
translation:
The patterns of utterance
Enjoined on those
Who meet on the way
The lovers in elopement are:
Warning the hero and heroine on elopement
Against the perilous nature of their journey
At such a time and along such a tract
As would be wrought with fright;
Telling them through words of kindness and concern
To stay in the village nearby
Since their destination stands removed afar;
Exhorting the couple united in love
Through words of compassion
Against the course of deed they took to;
Forbidding the foster-mother to pursue the lovers
As she has set out in search of them;
Guiding the foster-mother's pursuit of the lovers;
Speaking of the long distance the lovers traversed,
And speaking of the return of the lovers,
So goes the norm of utterance types in Akam poetry.

title: Utterance by the Hero
transliteration:
oṉṟāt tamariṉum paruvattum curattum
oṉṟiya moḻiyoṭu valippiṉum viṭuppiṉum
iṭaic cura maruṅkiṉ avaḷ tamar eytik
kaṭaik koṇṭu peyartaliṉ kalaṅku añar eytik
kaṟpoṭu puṇarnta kauvai uḷappaṭa
ap pāl paṭṭa oru tiṟattāṉum
nāḷatu ciṉmaiyum iḷamaiyatu arumaiyum
tāḷāṇ pakkamum takutiyatu amaitiyum
iṉmaiyatu iḷivum uṭaimaiyatu uyarcciyum
aṉpiṉatu akalamum akaṟciyatu arumaiyum
oṉṟāp poruḷvayiṉ ūkkiya pāliṉum
vāyiṉum kaiyiṉum vakutta pakkamoṭu
ūtiyam karutiya oru tiṟattāṉum
pukaḻum māṉamum eṭuttu vaṟpuṟuttalum
tūtu iṭaiyiṭṭa vakaiyiṉāṉum
ākit tōṉṟum pāṅkōr pāṅkiṉum
mūṉṟaṉ pakutiyum maṇṭilattu arumaiyum
tōṉṟal cāṉṟa māṟṟōr mēṉmaiyum
pācaṟaip pulampalum muṭinta kālattup
pākaṉoṭu virumpiya viṉaittiṟa vakaiyiṉum
kāvaṟ pāṅkiṉ āṅkōr pakkamum
parattaiyiṉ akaṟciyiṉ parintōṭ kuṟuki
irattalum teḷittalum eṉa iru vakaiyoṭu
urait tiṟa nāṭṭam kiḻavōṉ mēṉa.
translation:
The contexts of situations
That warrant utterance by the hero are:
As the heroine's kin would not consent
To their union in wedlock;
As the rendezvous becomes scarce;
As he finds a pretext
In the impassability of the desert-like tract
For her to accompany him;
As the heroine is persuaded into eloping with him;
As he sets out without taking the heroine with him;
As the heroine,
On elopement with him along the arid tract,
Falls into apprehension of pursuit by her kin and her being taken home,
And as she ponders public knowledge of their union which elopement brings;
As he goes,
Leaving the heroine in solitude,
In quest of wealth,
A quest that implicates
The shortness of life's span,
The preciousness of youth,
The hazards and exertions that the quest entails,
The unbecomingness of the lust for wealth
For men of nobility and standing,
The despisedness of indigence,
The search for eminence through greed of possession,
The alienation of the loved one's worth,
And the parting from the love who stands resolute in separation.
As he intends going after mind's enrichment and physical prowess
And the rewards attendant therein;
As he dilates to the heroine
Upon the abiding note such quests yield,
And upon the ignominy keeping off these quests would result in;
As he responds to the calling of being a royal emissary;
As he takes to aiding an ally in need;
As he sets out to take on hostile foemen
Who pride over their might, the might of their allies and the difficulty of
And over the secured unapproachability of their fortresses;
And as he remains in a war-camp away from his love;
As he,
Returning after the task accomplished,
Addresses his charioteer urging him to make it swift;
As he parts from his love
For purpose of security and protection of the state;
And,
As he importunes her
After his return from prostitutes
And seeks resolution of her sulking.

title: Utterance by Others
transliteration: eñciyōrkkum eñcutal ilavē.
translation:
Characters other than those mentioned above
[Such as the heroine, foster-mother, singer-messenger, etc.]
Are not denied utterances.

title: Other Contexts of Utterance
transliteration: nikaḻntatu niṉaittaṟku ētuvum ākum.
translation:
An event of the past
Recollected by the protagonists
May occasion their utterance at the moment too.

transliteration: nikaḻntatu kūṟi nilaiyalum tiṇaiyē.
translation:
The theme of palai (separation)
May also encompass
Recalling an event of the past
And finding consolation of the mind,

title: Blending of Land-time Features
transliteration:
marapunilai tiriyā māṭciya āki
viravum poruḷum viravum eṉpa.
translation:
Where they do not entail
Breach of the conventions set,
There are blendings of features
Of land and time and flora and fauna
Marked region-specific and conduct specific,
So has it been laid down.

title: A Function of Similes
transliteration:
uḷḷuṟai uvamam ēṉai uvamam eṉat
taḷḷātu ākum tiṇai uṇar vakaiyē.
translation:
Suggestive simile and the other (explicit) simile
Are pointers unmistakable
To the identification of the strands of Akam love [cf 1171-73 and 1184-86].

title: Nature and Function of the Suggestive Simile
transliteration:
uḷḷuṟai teyvam oḻintatai nilam eṉak
koḷḷum eṉpa kuṟi aṟintōrē.
translation:
The suggestive simile
Has for its vehicle
All distinctive features of the physical world of the given tract [966],
Saving the deities,
So does the authority hold.

transliteration:
uḷḷuṟuttu itaṉoṭu ottup poruḷ muṭika eṉa
uḷḷuṟuttu iṟuvatai uḷḷuṟai uvamam.
translation:
The suggestive simile is one
Where
The tenor comes revealing
As it draws implicitly on the vehicle described.

title: Nature of Non-suggestive Similes
transliteration: ēṉai uvamam tāṉ uṇar vakaittē.
translation:
The other, explicit simile
Marks
A tenor-vehicle relationship obviously stated.

transliteration:
kāmam cālā iḷamaiyōḷvayiṉ
ēmam cālā iṭumpai eyti
naṉmaiyum tīmaiyum eṉṟu iru tiṟattāṉ
taṉṉoṭum avaḷoṭum tarukkiya puṇarttu
col etir peṟāaṉ colli iṉpuṟal
pullit tōṉṟum kaikkiḷaik kuṟippē.
translation:
The defining features of unrequited love conduct [kaikkilai] are:
One falls in for a lass
With a passion of sex unformed yet
And yet,
One turns incurably afflicted;
One enters into conversation with that lass
Which alternates between praise and dispraise;
No reciprocity on her part marked though,
One persists indulgently in one's address.
The Defining Features of Peruntiņai

transliteration:
ēṟiya maṭal tiṟam iḷamai tīr tiṟam
tēṟutal oḻinta kāmattu miku tiṟam
mikka kāmattu miṭaloṭu tokaii
ceppiya nāṉkum peruntiṇaik kuṟippē.
muṉṉaiya nāṉkum muṉṉataṟku eṉpa.
translation:
The four states of love conduct,*
Which precede the four marked for abnormal passion above [1000]
[Threat of riding the palmyra stem horse,
Man drawn to woman in the prime of youth,
The passion of love remaining within bounds,
And intense passion not seeking forced union],
Do go with the unrequited love conduct [kaikkilai].

title: Metrical Forms Proper to Akam Poetry
transliteration:
nāṭaka vaḻakkiṉum ulakiyal vaḻakkiṉum
pāṭal cāṉṟa pulaṉeṟi vaḻakkam
kaliyē paripāṭṭu āyiru pāviṉum
uriyatu ākum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The authority holds that
kalippā and paripata! metrical forms
Are appropriate to (Akam) literary compositions
Which are informed by
Dramatic and worldly conventions.

title: Non-naming Convention
transliteration:
makkaḷ nutaliya akaṉ aintiṇaiyum
cuṭṭi oruvarp peyar koḷap peṟāar.
translation:
No proper names
Shall designate the human characters
That people the compositions
Treating the [centrally placed] fivefold Akam love conduct.

transliteration:
puṟattiṇai maruṅkiṉ poruntiṉ allatu
akattiṇai maruṅkiṉ aḷavutal ilavē.
translation:
Such proper names go right with the Puram [non-Akam] characters
And not with the Akam characters [1003].

title: Vetci Theme
transliteration:
akattiṇai maruṅkiṉ aril tapa uṇarntōr
puṟattiṇai ilakkaṇam tiṟappaṭak kiḷappiṉ
veṭcitāṉē kuṟiñciyatu puṟaṉē
uṭku varat tōṉṟum īr ēḻ tuṟaittē.
translation:
Looking into Puram composition
With an unmistakable grasp of Akam poetics,
One does discern that
Vetci is the non-Akam parallel to kuriñci theme,
And it ramifies into fourteen substrands of awesome nature.

transliteration:
vēntu viṭu muṉaiñar vēṟṟup pulak kaḷaviṉ
ā tantu ōmpal mēvaṟṟu ākum.
translation:
Vetțci is
Men at the border-posts,
Charged by their ruler,
Capturing the cows of the hostile king by stealth
And keeping them right under guard.

title: Substrands of the Vetci Theme
transliteration:
paṭai iyaṅku aravam pākkattu viricci
puṭai keṭap pōkiya celavē puṭai keṭa
oṟṟiṉ ākiya vēyē vēyppuṟam
muṟṟiṉ ākiya puṟattu iṟai muṟṟiya
ūr kolai ā kōḷ pūcal māṟṟē
nōy iṉṟu uyttal nuvalvaḻit tōṟṟam
tantu niṟai pātīṭu uṇṭāṭṭu koṭai eṉa
vanta īr ēḻ vakaiyiṟṟu ākum.

maṟam kaṭaikkūṭṭiya kuṭinilai ciṟanta
koṟṟavai nilaiyum at tiṇaip puṟaṉē.
translation:
Extolling the clan of warriors rooted in valour,
And worshipping Korravai the Goddess of victory
Also fall under the theme of veftci
The non-Akam parallel to the Akam theme kuriñci.

title: The Ramifications of the Vetci Theme
transliteration:
veṟi aṟi ciṟappiṉ vev vāy vēlaṉ
veṟiyāṭṭu ayarnta kāntaḷum uṟu pakai
vēntiṭai terital vēṇṭi ēntu pukaḻ
pōntai vēmpē ār eṉa varūum
mā peruntāṉaiyar malainta pūvum
vāṭā vaḷḷi vayavar ēttiya
ōṭāk kaḻal nilai uḷappaṭa ōṭā
uṭal vēntu aṭukkiya uṉṉa nilaiyum
māyōṉ mēya maṉ peruñ ciṟappiṉ
tāvā viḻup pukaḻp pūvai nilaiyum
ār amar ōṭṭalum ā peyarttut tarutalum
cīr cāl vēntaṉ ciṟappu eṭuttu uraittalum
talait tāḷ neṭumoḻi taṉṉoṭu puṇarttalum
aṉaikku uri marapiṉatu karantai aṉṟiyum
varu tār tāṅkal vāḷ vāyttuk kaviḻtal eṉṟu
iru vakaip paṭṭa piḷḷai nilaiyum
vāḷ malaintu eḻuntōṉai makiḻntu paṟai tūṅka
nāṭu avaṟku aruḷiya piḷḷaiyāṭṭum
kāṭci kālkōḷ nīrppaṭai naṭutal
cīrtta marapiṉ perumpaṭai vāḻttal eṉṟu
iru mūṉṟu marapiṉ kalloṭu puṇarac
collappaṭṭa eḻu mūṉṟu tuṟaittē.

vañcitāṉē mullaiyatu puṟaṉē
eñcā maṇ nacai vēntaṉai vēntaṉ
añcu takat talaic ceṉṟu aṭal kuṟittaṉṟē.
translation:
Vañci is the Puram parallel to the Akam theme muilai;
It is
The vanquishing of a king,
Marked by uncontained hunger for other's soil,
By another king
Through a frightful display of prowess.
Substrands of the Vañci Theme

transliteration:
iyaṅku paṭai aravam eri parantu eṭuttal
vayaṅkal eytiya perumaiyāṉum
koṭuttal eytiya koṭaimaiyāṉum
aṭuttu ūrntu aṭṭa koṟṟattāṉum
mārāyam peṟṟa neṭumoḻiyāṉum
poruḷiṉṟu uytta pērāṇ pakkamum
varu vicaip puṉalaik kaṟ ciṟai pōla
oruvaṉ tāṅkiya perumaiyāṉum
piṇṭam mēya peruñcōṟṟu nilaiyum
veṉṟōr viḷakkamum tōṟṟōr tēyvum
kuṉṟāc ciṟappiṉ koṟṟa vaḷḷaiyum
aḻi paṭai taṭṭō r taḻiñciyoṭu tokaii
kaḻi peruñ ciṟappiṉ tuṟai patiṉmūṉṟē.

uḻiñaitāṉē marutattup puṟaṉē
muḻu mutal araṇam muṟṟalum kōṭalum
aṉai neṟi marapiṟṟu ākum eṉpa.
translation:
Uliñai is the Puram parallel to the Akam theme marutam;
It is
Laying siege to the fortress well-fortified
And having it captured too,
So stands the norm set.

transliteration: atuvētāṉum iru nāl vakaittē.
translation:
Into eight substrands the uliñai theme ramifies.
Substrands of the Uliñai Theme

transliteration:
koḷḷār tēem kuṟitta koṟṟamum
uḷḷiyatu muṭikkum vēntaṉatu ciṟappum
tol eyiṟku ivartalum tōlatu perukkamum
akattōṉ celvamum aṉṟiyum muraṇiya
puṟattōṉ aṇaṅkiya pakkamum tiṟal paṭa
oru tāṉ maṇṭiya kuṟumaiyum uṭaṉṟōr
varu pakai pēṇār ār eyil uḷappaṭa
collappaṭṭa nāl iru vakaittē.

kuṭaiyum vāḷum nāḷkōḷ aṉṟi
maṭai amai ēṇimicai mayakkamum kaṭaiic
cuṟṟu amar oḻiya veṉṟu kaikkoṇṭu
muṟṟiya mutirvum aṉṟi muṟṟiya
akattōṉ vīḻnta nocciyum maṟṟu ataṉ
puṟattōṉ vīḻnta putumaiyāṉum
nīrc ceru vīḻnta pāciyum atāaṉṟu
ūrc ceru vīḻnta maṟṟataṉ maṟaṉum
matilmicaikku ivarnta mēlōr pakkamum
ikal matil kuṭumi koṇṭa maṇṇumaṅkalamum
veṉṟa vāḷiṉ maṇṇoṭu oṉṟa
tokainilai eṉṉum tuṟaiyoṭu tokaii
vakai nāl mūṉṟē tuṟai eṉa moḻipa.

title: Tumpai Theme
transliteration:
tumpaitāṉē neytalatu puṟaṉē
maintu poruḷāka vanta vēntaṉaic
ceṉṟu talai aḻikkum ciṟappiṟṟu eṉpa.
translation:
Tumpai is the Puram parallel to the Akam theme neytal,
It is in particular
The theme of undoing the might of an invading monarch
Burning with an overweening pride in his prowess.

transliteration:
kaṇaiyum vēlum tuṇaiyuṟa moyttaliṉ
ceṉṟa uyiriṉ niṉṟa yākkai
iru nilam tīṇṭā aru nilai vakaiyoṭu
iru pāṟ paṭṭa oru ciṟappiṉṟē.
translation:
The life of the warrior in action departing,
With his body having been pierced thick and fast
By the rain of arrows and spears of foemen,
There ís the wondrous spectacle of the man in two pieces —
The body standing erect without falling on the ground
In the manner of the leech cut into parts staying alive.

title: Substrands of the Tumpai Theme
transliteration:
tāṉai yāṉai kutirai eṉṟa
nōṉār uṭkum mū vakai nilaiyum
vēl miku vēntaṉai moyttavaḻi oruvaṉ
tāṉ mīṇṭu eṟinta tār nilai aṉṟiyum
iruvar talaivar taputip pakkamum
oruvaṉ oruvaṉai uṭai paṭai pukku
kūḻai tāṅkiya erumaiyum paṭai aṟuttu
pāḻi koḷḷum ēmattāṉum
kaḷiṟu eṟintu etirntōr pāṭum kaḷiṟṟoṭu
paṭṭa vēntaṉai aṭṭa vēntaṉ
vāḷōr āṭum amalaiyum vāḷ vāyttu
iru peru vēntartāmum cuṟṟamum
oruvarum oḻiyāt tokainilaikkaṇṇum
ceruvakattu iṟaivaṉ vīḻnteṉa ciṉaii
oruvaṉ maṇṭiya nal icai nilaiyum
pal paṭai oruvaṟku uṭaitaliṉ maṟṟavaṉ
oḷ vāḷ vīciya nūḻilum uḷappaṭap
pullit tōṉṟum paṉṉiru tuṟaittē.
translation:
The theme of tumpai above [1015]
Ramifies into twelve substrands:
The three columns of infantry, elephantry and cavalry
That strike terror among the foemen;
The deed of mettle by a warrior
That leaves his charge aside
And puts the enemy soldiers to rout
Who come to surround his king
As he keeps daring them with his spear;
The chiefs of the two contending monarchs
Falling to death in personal combat
Besides their prop for their rulers in action;-
The daring of an army chief
That comes up braving the odds like a buffalo
To stand at the head of the rear of his army
As it tends to retreat in disarray;
The grit of a warrior in action
Though he stands disarmed of his weapons;
The death of the warriors
That braved the charging elephants;
The clamour of singing and dancing
Of the warriors of the victorious king
Who felled his enemy king to death along with his elephant;
The annihilation of the two contending monarchs
Along with their kindred folk in deed
In their bloody conflict with swords;
The famed act of a warrior
Who finds his king felled in action
And rises in ire uncontained to fight the foe
And the feat exceptional of the warrior
That sends columns of enemy's army into disarray
And goes about waving his brilliant winning sword.
Vākai Theme

transliteration:
vākaitāṉē pālaiyatu puṟaṉē
tā il koḷkait tamtam kūṟṟaip
pākupaṭa mikutip paṭuttal eṉpa.
translation:
Vākai is the Puram parallel to the Akam theme pālai,
Which informs
Exaltation of the unsullied attainments of persons
As they abide in their vocations of expertise.

title: Modes of Vocations
transliteration:
aṟu vakaip paṭṭa pārppaṉap pakkamum
ai vakai marapiṉ aracar pakkamum

translation:
The seven modes of vocations
Which the theme of väkai celebrates are:
The sixfold occupations of the brahmins
[Learning, instruction, performing sacrifices,
Making others perform sacrifices,
Munificence and being beneficiaries of munificence];
The fivefold occupations of the kings
[Learning, performing sacrifices, munificence,
Protecting the country and administering justice];
The sixfold occupations of the other [tradesmen and cultivating] classes
[Learning, farming, trading, rearing cattle
Forms of worship and acts of liberality];
The calling of sages and astrologers —
The flawless reading of planetary movements
In relation to their effects on the past, present and future 1-1
The eightfold functions of ascetics
[Bathing, lying on the bare ground
Wearing leather covering, consecrated fire worship,
Keeping away from habitations of men,
Keeping undressed hair,
Eating forest produce and worshipping god];
The demarcated skills of excellence of the warrior class;
And the myriad callings other than the above
[Such as music, drama and singing}.

Who are the recipients of rich gifts from a patron

And directing them to the very same patron
For them to gain such bounteous rewards too;
Perumañkalam, the celebration of the king's birth anniversary

Or to distress when they turn to be adverse;

As adaptable to the changing mores of the world,
Of the past, the present and the future.

urai eṉat tōḻikku uraittaṟkaṇṇum

translation:
As she suffers the pangs of, separation
When the hero goes off in quest of wealth for their marriage;
As the hero persisting in his clandestine love career
Runs into her confidante or a maid of hers;
As she suggests to her confidante
To reveal her clandestine course to her [heroine's] kin —
Situations there are of this kind too
That provide for utterance by the heroine.

transliteration:
uyiriṉum ciṟantaṉṟu nāṇē nāṇiṉum
ceyir tīr kāṭcik kaṟpuc ciṟantaṉṟu eṉat
kamak kiļavaņ uļvalip patiņum,
tā il nal moli kiļlavi kiļappiņum,
a vakai piravum tōnņnruman porujļē.
translation:
As the heroine goes herself
Seeking the hero she has fallen in love with,
Or as she says such words as are freed of wilfulness and guile,
Armed she is
With the saying of the ancients that
'Bashfulness is of greater worth than life itself,
And chastity unsullied stands superior to bashfulness too' —
And things lofty such as these
Constitute the thematic modes of Akam love proper.

title: Contexts of Confidante's Utterance
transliteration:
nāṟṟamum tōṟṟamum oḻukkamum uṇṭiyum

varaivu uṭaṉpaṭṭō ṟ kaṭāval vēṇṭiṉum
āṅku ataṉ taṉmaiyiṉ vaṉpuṟai uḷappaṭa
pāṅkuṟa vanta nāl eṭṭu vakaiyum
tāṅka aruñ ciṟappiṉ tōḻi mēṉa.
translation:
Thirty-two are the contexts of situations
That warrant utterances considered
By the heroine's confidante the singular stay that she is:
As she probes the heroine's mind,
Without overstepping her position,
Through verities and means imaginative
Using undefined expressions varied therein,
After having discerned her union with the hero
Betrayed as it is
By the seven things marked sure in her —
The odorous smell that issues from her body,
The gracefulness of her appearance,
The changed behaviour with maids and kin,
The reduced intake of food,
Keeping routine acts off others' sight,
Her unidirectional movement,
And remaining fixed at one place;
As she turns back the hero
On the pretext of his honour
When he petitions her to aid his union with the heroine;
As she turns him away
Telling him to abide by the ways of the world
[To approach the heroine's kin requesting her hand in marriage};
As she keeps him off
Saying her lady is hard of access;
As she asks him to take his love right to the heroine
Before coming to her;
As she impresses on him
The credulousness of the heroine;
As she tells him to have his own ways of rendezvous
As he did earlier;
As she takes her apprehension of obstacles
On to the hero;
The union coming to materialize
Through her offices;
As she ponders her lady's indulgence,
With the hero coming to her under pretexts contrived;
As she turns deferential towards him
On discerning the truth of their union;
As she takes the hero's entreaties for union to the heroine;
As she conveys the myriad things she discerned
Of the intended deeds of passion of the hero
To the reticent heroine holding off her consent,
And as she speaks of them as if to herself `
All in words of suggestive import;
As she takes the heroine's words of consent
To the expectant hero;
As she marks the assorted sports of scandal
That attend on their union; :
As the hero comes seeking her lady's union;
As he seeks to part with a heart unwilling;
As they hold forth acts of hospitality to the ħero;
As she feigns discreet innocence as to their union;
As she entrusts the heroine to the hero
Commending his loving protection;
As she offers, through words veiled in harshness, comfort
To the disconsolate heroine
That turns dispirited .
At her slight on the hero's ways of conduct;
As she counsels his taking her lady's hand in marriage
Bringing home to him their disquiet
At the perils of his journey to their place,
And at the rigours of watch over the heroine's movements,
Changing the venues and hours of trysting,
Impressing on him the intensity of her lady's passion for him,
Reminding him of his honour at stake
Which issues from
The greatness of his country and town,
His family and clan, his birth and lineage
And things such as these;
As she clears the doubt
From the mind of the heroine's mother
As to the heroine's proclivity to fall in love
Showing it to be specious, :
And bringing her around to her [confidante's] word;
As there occasion
The divining of the heroine's ‘sickness’,
The frenzied dance of Murukañ's priest
To cure the heroine of her 'sickness',
The rival proposal for her hand in marriage,
And the denial of consent to unite her with the hero —
The confidante intervenes with unsullied words in two modes:
With address direct to the [foster] mother
Or with revelation of.the heroine's clandestine love.
By successive steps to her kin's hierarchy;
As she takes to the hero
The consent of the heroine's kin for their. marriage;
And as she comes back to the heroine
With words therein of assurance and comf ort.

title: Utterance by Heroine's Mother
transliteration: tāykkum varaiyār uṇarvu uṭampaṭiṉē.
translation:
The utterances above [1059]
Are not forbidden for the heroine's mother too
Where she discerns the things .
As does the foster-mother.

title: Mother and Foster-mother Understanding Heroine's Love
transliteration:
kiḻavōṉ aṟiyā aṟiviṉaḷ ivaḷ eṉa
mai aṟu ciṟappiṉ uyarntōr pāṅkiṉ
aiyak kiḷaviyiṉ aṟitalum urittē.
translation:
It is proper for the mother and foster-mother
To take the heroine
To be too credulous and dewy-eyed to know of the hero,
And seek the counsel of men of unsullied bearing,
And get their minds cleared of their misgivings.

title: The Nature of Heroine's Expression of Love
transliteration:
taṉ uṟu vēṭkai kiḻavaṉ muṉ kiḷattal
eṇṇum kālai kiḻattikku illai
piṟa nīr mākkaḷiṉ aṟiya āyiṭaip
peyn nīr pōlum uṇarviṟṟu eṉpa.
translation:
Unlike in the case of the people in lové
Whose affections find variance in various ways,
The heroine is not given to opening her heart t0 the hero;
Her love comes home to him
In the of water oozing from the fresh earthen pot,
So does the convention hold.

title: Hero and Heroine as Messengers of Their Love
transliteration:
kāmak kūṭṭam taṉimaiyiṉ politaliṉ
tāmē tūtuvar ākalum urittē.
translation:
The union of the lovers par excellence
Being the union apart secured from others,
The lover and the loved are the messengers unto themselves too
[Besides the heroine's confidante and the hero's companion].

title: Heroine Suggesting the Trysting Spot
transliteration:
avaṉ varampu iṟattal aṟam taṉakku iṉmaiyiṉ
kaḷam cuṭṭuk kiḷavi kiḻaviyatu ākum
tāṉ celaṟku uriya vaḻi ākalāṉa.
translation:
Propriety of conduct in love career
Not permitting the heroine
To trample on the hero's word of love,
It is for her to suggest the trysting spot
Used as she is to the tract around.

title: Confidante Prearranging Rendezvous
transliteration: tōḻiyiṉ muṭiyum iṭaṉumār uṇṭē.
translation:
Contexts there are too
Where the heroine's confidante prearranges the trysting spot.

title: Occasions That Do not Need the Confidante's Aid
transliteration:
mun nāḷ allatu tuṇai iṉṟu kaḻiyātu
an nāḷ akattum atu varaivu iṉṟē.
translation:
The confidante's offices the lovers ever need
Save those three occasions
[The first pre-destined meeting, the second meeting at the same spot,
Anđd the union through the aid of the hero's confidant];
Even on these three occasions,
The confidante helping their rendezvous
Is not disallowed.

title: Confidante as Facilitator of Heroine's Love
transliteration:
pal nūṟu vakaiyiṉum taṉ vayiṉ varūum
nal naya maruṅkiṉ nāṭṭam vēṇṭaliṉ
tuṇaic cuṭṭuk kiḷavi kiḻaviyatu ākum
tuṇaiyōr karumam ākalāṉa.

title: The Uniqueness of Foster-mother
transliteration:
āy peruñ ciṟappiṉ aru maṟai kiḷattaliṉ
tāy eṉappaṭuvōḷ cevili ākum.
translation:
The foster-mother is rightly treated as mother
For it is she
In whom is confided the worthy clandestine love career.

title: The Confidante vis-a-vis Heroine's Love
transliteration: tōḻitāṉē cevili makaḷē.
translation:
The confidante of the heroine
Is by birth
The daughter of the foster-mother.

transliteration: cūḻtalum ucāttuṇai nilaimaiyiṉ polimē.
translation:
The confidante there stands preeminent
Perceiving all that passes for the heroine
And counselling her therein.

transliteration:
kuṟaiyuṟa uṇartal muṉ uṟa uṇartal
iruvarum uḷvaḻi avaṉ varavu uṇartal eṉa
matiyuṭampaṭuttal oru mū vakaittē.
translation:
Three means there exist.
For the confidante to come fully aware
Of the existence of union between her lady and the hero:
As the hero stands petitioning her,
As there marks changed demeanour on the heroine's person,
And as the hero approaches them when they are together.

transliteration:
aṉṉa vakaiyāṉ uṇarnta piṉ allatu
piṉṉilai muyaṟci peṟāḷ eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The hero's petitioning wouldn't move the confidante
To extend her hand of help for his rendezvous with the heroine,
Unless she becomes fully aware of their union
Through the three means noted above [1071]
So has it been pronounced.

transliteration:
muyaṟcik kālattu ataṟpaṭa nāṭi
puṇarttal āṟṟalum avaḷvayiṉāṉa.
translation:
As the hero seeks union with the heroine,
Discerning the mind acquiescent of the heroine
And bringing about their union
Is all the charge of the confidante.

title: Trysting
transliteration:
kuṟi eṉappaṭuvatu iraviṉum pakaliṉum
aṟiyak kiḷanta āṟṟatu eṉpa.
translation:
The rendezvous is
The trysting spot
Where the hero and heroine meet
By night and by day
By mutual acquiescence.

title: Trysting Spot by Night
transliteration:
iravuk kuṟiyē illakattuḷḷum
maṉaiyōr kiḷavi kēṭkum vaḻiyatuvē
maṉaiyakam pukāak kālaiyāṉa.
translation:
Trysting by night occurs
In the precincts of the heroine's house,
A spot within hearing of the household,
And it occasions
Before the hero finds access into her house.

title: Trysting Spot by Day
transliteration:
pakal puṇar kaḷaṉē puṟaṉ eṉa moḻipa
avaḷ aṟivu uṇara varu vaḻiyāṉa.
translation:
Trysting by day occurs
In the outskirts of the heroine's town,
The access to which she must be conversant with,
So has it been said.

transliteration:
allakuṟippaṭutalum avaḷvayiṉ urittē
avaṉ kuṟi mayaṅkiya amaivoṭu variṉē.
translation:
The heroine does fall a victim
Of missed trysts too,
When casually happening signs
` Bewilder her mind into taking them
For the marks prearranged to be given by the hero.

title: Other Spots of Rendezvous
transliteration:
āṅku āṅku oḻukum oḻukkamum uṇṭē
ōṅkiya ciṟappiṉ oru ciṟaiyāṉa.
translation:
[Besides the spots of trysting fixed by night and by day],
There occasions union between the lovers ` `
At other places fitting and proper too.

title: The Hero During Trysting
transliteration:
maṟainta oḻukkattu ōraiyum nāḷum
tuṟanta oḻukkam kiḻavōṟku illai.
translation:
During the clandestine career
The hero does not go by
Signs of the zodiac and auspicious day
For his rendezvous with the heroine.

transliteration:
āṟṟiṉatu arumaiyum aḻivum accamum
ūṟum uḷappaṭa ataṉ ōraṉṉa.
translation:
Deterred the hero is not too
From his rendezvous with the heroine
By the hardness of the path,
The dispiritedness [born of hostile men and things around],
And by the fear of perils and obstacles to his love.
Knowledge of Heroine's Love by her Kin

transliteration: tantaiyum taṉṉaiyum muṉṉattiṉ uṇarpa.
translation:
The heroine's love career
Her father and elder brother discern
By inference from things seen and heard.

translation:
The heroine's love career
Stands revealed to the mother [by the foster-mother]
As does the foster-mother know of it
[From the heroine's confidante].

title: Heroine's Love Coming into the Public
transliteration:
ampalum alarum kaḷavu veḷippaṭuttaliṉ
aṅku ataṉ mutalvaṉ kiḻavaṉ ākum.
translation:
In so far as
The love career of the hero and the heroine
Unfolds to be inferred in discourses private,
And in so far as
It is thrown into the subject of gossip in public,
The acts of the hero must bear the prime responsibility for it.
Modes of Wedded Union.

transliteration:
veḷippaṭa varaital paṭāmai varaital eṉṟu
āyiraṇṭu eṉpa varaital āṟē.
translation:
The hero and the heroine
Enter into marital union
Either after their clandestine union becomes public knowledge
Or before it happens.

transliteration:
veḷippaṭaitāṉē kaṟpiṉoṭu oppiṉum
ñāṅkark kiḷanta mūṉṟu poruḷāka
varaiyātu pirital kiḻavōṟku illai.
translation:
Even as the clandestine course revealed
Does stand equated with wedded love,
The parting of the hero from the heroine
On the three pursuits noted above [973]
[Learning, call of war and embassy]
Does not occasion before their marriage is solemnized.

title: The Wedded Union
transliteration:

koḷaṟku uri marapiṉ kiḻavaṉ kiḻattiyai
koṭaikku uri marapiṉōr koṭuppa koḷvatuvē.
translation:
The wedded course is
The hero, who comes from a worthy lineage, `
Taking the hand in marriage
Of the heroine
As she is offered by those of a line worthy and compatible,
With the rites and ceremonies attendant thereon. |

transliteration:
koṭuppōr iṉṟiyum karaṇam uṇṭē
puṇarntu uṭaṉ pōkiya kālaiyāṉa.
translation:
Even as the heroine's kin do not consent to their union [1086]
There does occasion wedding solemnized
With the two taking to ełopement.

mēlōr mūvarkkum puṇartta karaṇam
kīḻōrkku ākiya kālamum uṇṭē.
translation:
The ceremonies and rites
Attendant on the three superior social classes
[Kings, brahmins and trading folk]
Came to mark the marriage
Among those down the ladder in the course of time.

poyyum vaḻuvum tōṉṟiya piṉṉar
aiyar yāttaṉar karaṇam eṉpa.
translation:
Sage men there conceived solemnized wedding
When falsity and breach of trust cropped up,
So has it been said.
