pariviṉ nīkkiya pakutikkaṇṇum
niṉṟu naṉi piriviṉ añciya paiyuḷum
ceṉṟu kaiyikantu peyarttu uḷḷiya vaḻiyum
kāmattiṉ valiyum kaiviṭiṉ accamum
tāṉ avaṭ piḻaitta nilaiyiṉkaṇṇum
uṭaṉ cēṟal ceykaiyoṭu aṉṉavai piṟavum
maṭam paṭa vanta tōḻikkaṇṇum
vēṟṟu nāṭṭu akalvayiṉ viḻumattāṉum
mīṭṭu varavu āynta vakaiyiṉkaṇṇum
av vaḻip perukiya ciṟappiṉkaṇṇum
pēr icai ūrtip pākar pāṅkiṉum
kāmak kiḻatti maṉaiyōḷ eṉṟu ivar
ēmuṟu kiḷavi colliya etirum
ceṉṟa tēettu uḻappu naṉi viḷakki
iṉṟic ceṉṟa taṉṉilai kiḷappiṉum
arun toḻil muṭitta cemmal kālai
viruntoṭu nallavai vēṇṭaṟkaṇṇum
mālai ēntiya peṇṭirum makkaḷum
kēḷir oḻukkattup pukaṟcikkaṇṇum
ēṉaiya vāyilōr etiroṭu tokaii
paṇ amai pakuti muppatiṉorumūṉṟum
eṇṇa aruñ ciṟappiṉ kiḻavōṉ mēṉa.

title: Contexts of Heroine's Utterance
transliteration:
avaṉ aṟivu āṟṟa aṟiyum ākaliṉ
ēṟṟaṟ kaṇṇum niṟuttaṟkaṇṇum
urimai koṭutta kiḻavōṉ pāṅkil
perumaiyiṉ tiriyā aṉpiṉkaṇṇum
kiḻavaṉai makaṭūup pulampu peritu ākaliṉ
alamaral perukiya kāmattu mikutiyum
iṉpamum iṭumpaiyum ākiya iṭattum
kayantalai tōṉṟiya kāmar neyyaṇi
nayanta kiḻavaṉai neñcu puṇṇuṟīi
naḷiyiṉ nīkkiya iḷi varu nilaiyum
pukaṉṟa uḷḷamoṭu putuvōr cāyaṟku
akaṉṟa kiḻavaṉaip pulampu naṉi kāṭṭi
iyaṉṟa neñcam talaip peyarttu arukki
etir peytu maṟutta īrattu maruṅkiṉum
taṅkiya oḻukkattuk kiḻavaṉai vaṇaṅki
eṅkaiyarkku urai eṉa irattaṟkaṇṇum
cellāk kālai celka eṉa viṭuttalum
kāmak kiḻatti taṉ makat taḻīi
ēmuṟu viḷaiyāṭṭu iṟutikkaṇṇum
ciṟanta ceykai av vaḻit tōṉṟi
aṟam puri uḷḷamoṭu taṉ varavu aṟiyāmai
puṟam ceytu peyarttal vēṇṭu iṭattāṉum
tantaiyar oppar makkaḷ eṉpataṉāl
antam il ciṟappiṉ makap paḻittu neruṅkalum
koṭiyōr koṭumai cuṭum eṉa oṭiyātu
nal icai nayantōr colloṭu tokaii
pakutiyiṉ nīṅkiya takutikkaṇṇum
koṭumai oḻukkam kōṭal vēṇṭi
aṭimēl vīḻnta kiḻavaṉai neruṅki
kātal eṅkaiyar kāṇiṉ naṉṟu eṉa
mātar cāṉṟa vakaiyiṉkaṇṇum
tāyar kaṇṇiya nal aṇip putalvaṉai
māyap parattai uḷḷiya vaḻiyum
taṉvayiṉ ciṟaippiṉum avaṉ vayiṉ pirippiṉum
iṉṉāt tol cūḷ eṭuttaṟkaṇṇum
kāmakkiḻattiyar nalam pārāṭṭiya
tīmaiyiṉ muṭikkum poruḷiṉkaṇṇum
koṭumai oḻukkattut tōḻikku uriyavai
vaṭu aṟu ciṟappiṉ kaṟpiṉ tiriyāmai
kāytalum uvattalum pirittalum peṭṭalum
āvayiṉ varūum pal vēṟu nilaiyiṉum
vāyiliṉ varūum vakaiyoṭu tokaii
kiḻavōḷ ceppal kiḻavatu eṉpa.
translation:
The contexts of situations `
Wherein the heroine has her utterances right |
In her wedded course are:
As she adores the hero
Knowing his mind so closely that she is; |
As she holds him off
When he seeks her union;
As she showers her heart's affections
Upon the hero who has privileged her to this wedded state
Deviating not from the honour and virtue ingrained;
As she is weighed down by passion's affliction
When there intervenes a protracted separation;
As there occasion ecstasy and joy all together;
As she keeps off the hero in a state of indignity
When he seeks her access in love
At her ceremonial oil-bath
After the birth of a son to her;
As she marks her conjugal love abiding
When she refuses union with her wedded lord
By drawing up before his mind's eye
His acts of debauchery,
And holding her loving heart away from him in resentment,
The heart that suffered the anguish of lonesomeness
With him having gone lusting for the fresh beauties of prostitutes;
As she makes solicitations veiled in rebuke
To take his protestations of love
Back to her younger sisters (his paramours)
In whose lustful company he had been all along;
As she feels constrained to let him go
When he stands before her with persistent entreaties;
As the hero's concubine cuddles her son up in love
And lets him after play with him;
As the hero approaches her unknown from behind
When she is absorbed in play with her son
And nestles up against her
In an act of virtuous conduct
And seeks to resolve her sulking;
As she turns thereon to her son,
The source of unending joy that he is,
And holds him to reproach
Finding the adage 'like father like son' true;
As she abides in the virtue of conjugal love
When she does not go dispirited
At the unkindly act of debauchery of the hero,
And takes the word of conciliation of the men of note;
As she reveals her lofty trait of a wedded wife
When she tells him at his face
'It would look dishonourable
Were my younger sisters (the hero's concubines) to see it,
With the hero prostrating before her
And soliciting her pardon for his act of debauchery;
As her ire against her promiscuous husband
Is turned into reproof of her son
When he returns with ornaments
His mothers (father's concubines) have bedecked him with;
As she ponders,
Given her fulness of love for him
And his unkindly acts of severance,
The ill-effects of his oath of non-separation from her;
As she praises the beauties of his concubine
With a view to showing his deed of debauchery;
As she reveals her ire,
Feels pleasure with his union,
Spurns his advances,
Takes him in a mood of conciliation
And her diverse acts such as these —
All befitting her unsullied passion of wedded love
When her confidante speaks of his unloving acts of debauchery;
And
As the singing minstrel
And the other messengers
There intercede on behalf of the promiscuous | hero.

transliteration:
puṇarntu uṭaṉ pōkiya kiḻavōḷ maṉai iruntu
iṭaic curattu iṟaicciyum viṉaiyum cuṭṭi
aṉpuṟu takka kiḷattal tāṉē
kiḻavōṉ cey viṉaikku accam ākum.
translation:
Another context of the heroine's utterance
Is her apprehension,
Now at home in her wedded state, :
Whether her husband could get his mission on hand accomplished
As she pondered his having pointed to her
When they trod the arid tract in elopement,
The beasts and birds in loving union around
[Which might induce him to return to her loving fold}.

transliteration:
tōḻi uḷḷuṟutta vāyil pukuppiṉum
āvayiṉ nikaḻum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The utterance of such apprehension [1091]
There will also occasion
When the heroine despatches her confidante
And other messengers too
To get the hero's journey deferred,
So have the literate men held.

title: Contexts of Confidante's Utterance
transliteration:
peṟaṟku arum perum poruḷ muṭinta piṉ vanta
teṟaṟku aru marapiṉ ciṟappiṉkaṇṇum
aṟṟam aḻivu uraippiṉum aṟṟam illāk
kiḻavōṭ cuṭṭiya teyvak kaṭattiṉum
cīruṭaip perum poruḷ vaittavaḻi maṟappiṉum
aṭaṅkā oḻukkattu avaṉvayiṉ aḻintōḷai
aṭaṅkak kāṭṭutaṟ poruḷiṉ kaṇṇum
piḻaittu vantu irunta kiḻavaṉai neruṅki
iḻaittu āṅku ākkik koṭuttaṟkaṇṇum
vaṇaṅku iyal moḻiyāṉ vaṇaṅkaṟkaṇṇum
puṟampaṭu viḷaiyāṭṭup pulliya pukaṟciyum
ciṟanta putalvaṉait tērātu pulampiṉum
māṇ nalam tā eṉa vakuttaṟkaṇṇum
pēṇā oḻukkam nāṇiya poruḷiṉum
cūḷvayiṉ tiṟattāl cōrvu kaṇṭu aḻiyiṉum
periyōr oḻukkam peritu eṉak kiḷantu
peṟu takai illāp piḻaippiṉum av vaḻi
uṟu takai illāp pulaviyuḷ mūḻkiya
kiḻavōḷpāl niṉṟu keṭuttaṟkaṇṇum
uṇarppuvayiṉ vārā ūṭal uṟṟōḷvayiṉ
uṇarttal vēṇṭiya kiḻavōṉpāl niṉṟu
tāṉ vekuṇṭu ākkiya takutikkaṇṇum
arumaik kālattup perumai kāṭṭiya
eḷimaik kālattu irakkattāṉum
pāṇar kūttar viṟaliyar eṉṟu ivar
pēṇic colliya kuṟaiviṉai etirum
nītta kiḻavaṉai nikaḻumāṟu paṭīiyar
kātta taṉmaiyiṉ kaṇ iṉṟu peyarppiṉum
piriyum kālai etir niṉṟu cāṟṟiya
marapu uṭai etirum uḷappaṭa piṟavum
vakai paṭa vanta kiḷavi ellām
tōḻikku uriya eṉmaṉār pulavar.

title: Utterance by Concubines
transliteration:
pullutal mayakkum pulavikkaṇṇum
illōr ceyviṉai ikaḻccikkaṇṇum
pal vēṟu putalvark kaṇṭu naṉi uvappiṉum
maṟaiyiṉ vanta maṉaiyōḷ ceyviṉai
poṟai iṉṟu perukiya paruvaraṟkaṇṇum
kātal cōrviṉ kaṭappāṭṭu āṇmaiyiṉ
tāy pōl taḻīik kaḻaṟi am maṉaiviyaik
kāyvu iṉṟu avaṉvayiṉ poruttaṟkaṇṇum
iṉ nakaip putalvaṉait taḻīi iḻai aṇintu
piṉṉar vanta vāyiṟkaṇṇum
maṉaiyōḷ ottaliṉ taṉṉōr aṉṉōr
mikai eṉak kuṟitta koḷkaikkaṇṇum
eṇṇiya paṇṇai eṉṟu ivaṟṟoṭu piṟavum
kaṇṇiya kāmakkiḻattiyar mēṉa.
translation:
The contexts of situations
Wherein occasion utterances
By the hero's concubines of steadfast love are:
As they stand sulking
When the hero's union with them
Alternates with his union with others;
As they disparage the acts of the hero and his wedded wife;
As they stand with joy exceeding
At the sight of the hero's children;
As their spirits go down in anguish uncontained
On hearing the innuendoes about them
From the wife wedded through the clandestine career;
As they,
Enervated passion of love
And benignity of mind impelling,
Empathize with the wedded heroine
As does the mother
Bearing no ill-will against her,
And pave the way for the hero's union with her;
As he comes holding his son decked with ornaments,
Who wears a lighted up face,
And bringing the child for his interceder
[As they denied admission to other interceders];
As they take themselves to be on a par with the heroine,
And consider other women of their kind unwanted;
As they seek enjoyment of sport with the hero;
And situations such as these.

title: Utterance by Interceders
transliteration:
kaṟpum kāmamum naṟpāl oḻukkamum
mel iyal poṟaiyum niṟaiyum vallitiṉ
viruntu puṟantarutalum cuṟṟam ōmpalum
piṟavum aṉṉa kiḻavōḷ māṇpukaḷ
mukam pukal muṟaimaiyiṉ kiḻavōṟku uraittal
akam pukal marapiṉ vāyilkaṭku uriya.
translation:
Bringing home to the hero
In a manner winning and efficacious
The attributes lofty of the heroine
Her steadfast fidelity, affections for the hero,
Her virtuous demeanour, forbearance born of tenderness innate,
Her fortitude, her hospitality unfailing,
Attending to the needs of the kinsfolk
And traits such as these —
Comprises the context
That occasions utterances by interceders
Who by wont have access to the hero's dwelling.

title: Utterance by Foster-mother
transliteration:
kaḻiviṉum nikaḻviṉum etirviṉum vaḻi koḷa
nallavai uraittalum allavai kaṭitalum
cevilikku uriya ākum eṉpa.
translation:
The utterance of the foster-mother
Is such as to counsel one to take to virtuous ways
And to rebuke one straying from righteousness,
With an eye on the present,
What's gone and what's to come,
So has it been said.

title: Utterance by the Wise
transliteration: colliya kiḷavi aṟivarkkum uriya.
translation:
Counsel and censure
Such as above [1097]
Do mark the utterance of the sage men too.

transliteration:
iṭittu varai niṟuttalum avaratu ākum
kiḻavaṉum kiḻattiyum avar varai niṟṟaliṉ.
translation:
Since the hero and heroine stand
Heeding words of the sage men above [1098],
They are entitled to hand words of reproof
Where the two overstep bounds of righteousness.

title: Contexts of Hero's Variance
transliteration:
uṇarppu varai iṟappiṉum cey kuṟi piḻaippiṉum
pulattalum ūṭalum kiḻavōṟku uriya.
translation:
The hero does resort to
Feigned dislike and pretence of resentment
Where the heroine's sulks defy persuasion
And where she is the cause of the missed tryst.

title: Confidante's Intercession
transliteration:
pulattalum ūṭalum ākiya iṭattum
colat taku kiḷavi tōḻikku uriya.
translation:
There is the utterance (of intercession)
By the heroine's confidante,
When there intervene
Feigned dislike and pretence of resentment
In the love career of the hero and heroine.

transliteration:
parattaimai maṟuttal vēṇṭiyum kiḻatti
maṭat taku kiḻamai uṭaimaiyāṉum
aṉpilai koṭiyai eṉṟalum uriyaḷ.
translation:
The confidante of the heroine
Does hold the right to tell the hero,
‘Loveless is your heart
And 'stony-hearted you are'
With a view to ending his acts of debauchery
And on account of her lady's credulousness.

title: Heroine's Sulking
transliteration:
avaṉ kuṟippu aṟital vēṇṭiyum kiḻavi
akam mali ūṭal akaṟcikkaṇṇum
vēṟṟumaik kiḷavi tōṟṟavum peṟumē.
translation:
Words of variance
The heroine's tongue does betray
As she seeks to read the hero's mind
And as her sulking marks an extended course.

title: Solicitude by Hero
transliteration:
kāmak kaṭappiṉuḷ paṇinta kiḷavi
kāṇum kālai kiḻavōṟku urittē
vaḻipaṭu kiḻamai avaṭku iyalāṉa.
translation:
Given to adoring the hero
As the heroine is wont to,
Words of solicitude,
Are seen to belong to the hero
When he suffers intensity of love's passion.

title: Heroine's Loving Response
transliteration:
aruḷ muntuṟutta aṉpu poti kiḷavi
poruḷ paṭa moḻital kiḻavōṭkum urittē.
translation:
Uttering words of solicitude
Pregnant with affections of the heart
And clothed in benignity
Does characterize
The heroine's utterances £00.
Gossip about the Love Career

transliteration: kaḷavum kaṟpum alar varaivu iṉṟē.
translation:
That there occasions
Gossip around
During the clandestine course and wedded career
Is inevitable.

transliteration: alariṉ tōṉṟum kāmattu mikuti.
translation:
The public gossip
Does fuel the vehemence of love's passion.

title: Acts of Sport
transliteration: kiḻavōṉ viḷaiyāṭṭu āṅkum aṟṟē.
translation:
The affections of the lovers
Have their impetus
Through the hero's acts of sport too.
Rołe of Interceders

transliteration:
maṉaivi talaittāḷ kiḻavōṉ koṭumai
tam uḷa ātal vāyilkaṭku illai.
translation:
To speak of the acts of lovelessness of the hero
In the presence of the heroine
Is not proper for the interceders.

transliteration:
maṉaivi muṉṉark kaiyaṟu kiḷavi
maṉaivikku uṟuti uḷvaḻi uṇṭē.
translation:
Rueful words of helplessness by the interceders
Before the heart-sick heroine
Are in place too, .
Where they serve to soothe- her disquieted mind.

transliteration:
muṉṉilaip puṟamoḻi ellā vāyiṟkum
piṉṉilait tōṉṟum eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Address in the third person
To those standing in their presence
Is allowed for all interceders
Where they do make entreaties,
So has it been ruled.

title: Utterance by Minstrel Messengers
transliteration:
tollavai uraittalum nukarcci ēttalum
pal āṟṟāṉum ūṭaliṉ takaittalum
uṟuti kāṭṭalum aṟivu meyn niṟuttalum
ētuviṉ uraittalum tuṇivu kāṭṭalum
aṇi nilai uraittalum kūttar mēṉa.
translation:
The minstrels of dancing and singing class
Shall have their utterances informed of:
References to the precedents,
Commending the bliss of conjugal union,
Seeking to resolve the feigned variance of the lovers
Through varied means,
Indicating the ends of wedded life,
Helping to steer the mind toward right courses,
Demonstrating the nature of things cause and effect marked,
Taking to firmness of mind and resolute course
And counselling abiding gracefulness of features.

transliteration:
nilam peyarntu uraittal avaḷ nilai uraittal
kūttarkkum pāṇarkkum yāttavai uriya.
translation:
Taking the lonesome anguish of the heroine
To the hero in a land afar on his mission,
And conveying to her
The state of affairs obtaining in that country
Comprise the utterance proper
For the minstrels of singing and dancing class
And for the minstrels of the singing class.

title: Utterance by Attendant Class Youth
transliteration:
āṟṟatu paṇpum karumattu viḷaivum
ēval muṭivum viṉāvum ceppum
āṟṟiṭaik kaṇṭa poruḷum iṟaicciyum
tōṟṟam cāṉṟa aṉṉavai piṟavum
iḷaiyōrkku uriya kiḷavi eṉpa.
translation:
Describing the nature of the tract to be taken to,
Reporting the result of the deed undertaken,
Accomplishment of the task charged with,
Taking the order given,
Detailing the response to the charge assigned,
Recounting the occurrences enroute,
And relating the flora and fauna distinctive of the tract seen
And whatever that comes into view,
And things such as these :
Go into the utterance of the attendant class youth,
So has it been ruled.

transliteration:
uḻaik kuṟun toḻilum kāppum uyarntōr
naṭakkai ellām avarkaṇ paṭumē.
translation:
Personal chores of the menial kind and guarding
And all deeds of attendance upon the superior classes
Are the charges proper to the youth of the attendant class above [114].

title: Hero's Remorse
transliteration:
piṉ muṟai ākkiya perum poruḷ vatuvait
tol muṟai maṉaivi etirppāṭu āyiṉum
iṉ iḻaip putalvaṉai vāyil koṇṭu pukiṉum
iṟantatu niṉaiik kiḻavōṉ āṅkaṇ
kalaṅkalum uriyaṉ eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The hero stands weighed down with remorse
Pricked by his union with strumpets
As he is back home
To the heroine of ancient connectedness
Who has handed him a prized heir to his legacy
And entering his house
With his son decked with lustrous ornaments
For his interceder,
So do the literate men hold.

title: And the Heroine's Response
transliteration:
tāy pōl kaḻaṟit taḻīik kōṭal
āy maṉaik kiḻattikkum urittu eṉa moḻipa
kavavoṭu mayaṅkiya kālaiyāṉa.
translation:
When her husband* remains weighed down by disquietude,
It is proper for the discerning heroine at home
To critique him after a mother,
And hold him in her loving embrace too.

transliteration:
avaṉ cōrpu kāttal kaṭaṉ eṉappaṭutaliṉ
makaṉ tāy uyarpum taṉ uyarpu ākum
celvaṉ paṇi moḻi iyalpu ākalāṉa.
translation:
To keep her husband secured against words of infamy
Being held to be the heroine's charge,
The honour of the heroine* his son's mother
Is verily the honour of the husband too;
It is therefore his wont to keep a benign tongue.

title: Hero in War-camp
transliteration: eṇ arum pācaṟai peṇṇoṭu puṇarār.
translation:
The union of love will be kept off
From the war-camp the place of onerous charge.

transliteration: puṟattōr āṅkaṇ puṇarvatu ākum.
translation:
Women assigned to duties other than love
Will be there around in war-camps.

title: Utterance by Brahminfolk
transliteration:
kāma nilai uraittalum tēr nilai uraittalum
kiḻavōṉ kuṟippiṉai eṭuttuk kūṟalum
āvoṭu paṭṭa nimittam kūṟalum
celavu uṟu kiḷaviyum celavu aḻuṅku kiḷaviyum
aṉṉavai piṟavum pārppārkku uriya.
translation:
The contexts of situations
That mark utterances by brahminfolk are:
To speak of the nature and import of the passion of love,
To indicate the state of preparedness of the hero's chariot,
To explain the hero's intent to the heroine,
To clarify such omens as are associated with cows,
To convey the hero's departure on his mission,
To persuade the hero to defer journey on his mission,
And occasions such as these.

title: The Intent of Interceders
transliteration:
ellā vāyilum iruvar tēettum
pulliya makiḻccip poruḷa eṉpa.
translation:
The intent of all interceders
Is to see the hero and heroine
In joy abiding,
So has it been said.

transliteration:
aṉpu talaippirinta kiḷavi tōṉṟiṉ
ciṟaippuṟam kuṟittaṉṟu eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Where there warrant
Words shorn of tenderness and pleasing import,
The interceders shall utter them
-Standing aside within earshot though,
Thus goes the ruling of the learned.

title: Heroine's Self-praise
transliteration:
taṟ pukaḻ kiḷavi kiḻavaṉ muṉ kiḷattal
et tiṟattāṉum kiḻattikku illai
muṟpaṭa vakutta iraṇṭu alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
The heroine,
Whatever the circumstances,
Is not given to self-praise
In the presence of the hero,
Save the two contexts aforasaid [990, 1117).

title: Hero's Self-adulation
transliteration:
kiḻavi muṉṉart taṟ pukaḻ kiḷavi
kiḻavōṉ viṉaivayiṉ uriya eṉpa.
translation:
Self-praise there marks the hero's utterance
In the presence of the heroine
As he sets .out on his mission
Parting from the heroine.

title: Confidant as Critic
transliteration: moḻi etir moḻital pāṅkaṟku urittē.
translation:
The confidant of the hero is privileged
To offer refutations
To the assertions of the hero.

transliteration: kuṟittu etir moḻital aḵkit tōṉṟum.
translation: Rarely do such refutations occasion [1126].

title: Hero's Reassurance
transliteration:
tuṉpuṟu poḻutiṉum ellām kiḻavaṉ
vaṉpuṟuttallatu cēṟal illai.
translation:
On all occasions
When the heroine turns disconsolate at parting,
The hero leaves her not
Without words of comfort and reassurance to her.

title: Hero's Desisting from Parting
transliteration:
celaviṭai aḻuṅkal cellāmai aṉṟē
vaṉpuṟai kuṟitta tavircci ākum.
translation:
That the hero desists from setting eut on his journey
Is not the abandonment of his mission;
It is a deed deferred
To see her deferring to words of comfort and reassurance.
Hero on his Mission

transliteration:
kiḻavi nilaiyē viṉaiyiṭattu uraiyār
veṉṟik kālattu viḷaṅkit tōṉṟum
translation:
No reflection of the heroine at home
Finds utterance from the hero away on his mission;
The task accomplished,
He wears her plight upon his sleeve.

title: Hero's Pursuit of Harlots
transliteration:
pūppiṉ puṟappāṭu īr āṟu nāḷum
nīttu akaṉṟu uṟaiyār eṉmaṉār pulavar
parattaiyiṉ pirinta kālaiyāṉa.
translation:
The literate men say,
While there occasions his separation
In pursuit of harlots,
The hero does not keep off from the heroine
During the twelve days
Since the day of her menstruation.

title: Hero's Quest of Learning
transliteration: vēṇṭiya kalvi yāṇṭu mūṉṟu iṟavātu.
translation:
The hero's separation from the heroine,
As he goes in quest of learning,
Does not go beyond three years.

title: Parting at King's Calling
transliteration: vēntu uṟu toḻilē yāṇṭiṉatu akamē.
translation:
Charge at the king's calling
Keeps him separated from his wife
For a period within a year.

title: Other Missions
transliteration: ēṉaip pirivum av iyal nilaiyum.

title: Acts of Sport
transliteration:
yāṟum kuḷaṉum kāvum āṭi
pati ikantu nukartalum uriya eṉpa.
translation:
Seeking the pleasures of life,
Such as sports in rivers and tanks
And revelry in groves,
Beyond the bounds of their home soil,
Is part of the love career of the hero and heroine.

title: Fruits of Wedded Love
transliteration:
kāmam cāṉṟa kaṭaikkōṭ kālai
ēmam cāṉṟa makkaḷoṭu tuvaṉṟi
aṟam puri cuṟṟamoṭu kiḻavaṉum kiḻattiyum
ciṟantatu payiṟṟal iṟantataṉ payaṉē.
translation:
‘Having relished the felicities of the passion of love,
It is for the hero and heroine in conjugal union
To savour the protective presence of their children
And seek to live on things sublime,
With virtuous kinsfolk around,
Which makes for the fruits the wedded course entailed.

title: Interceders
transliteration:
tōḻi tāyē pārppāṉ pāṅkaṉ
pāṇaṉ pāṭṭi iḷaiyar viruntiṉar
kūttar viṟaliyar aṟivar kaṇṭō r
yātta ciṟappiṉ vāyilkaḷ eṉpa.
translation:
The interceders of benign note in the Akam course are:
The confidante of the heroine, heroine's (foster)-mother,
The brahmin folk, hero's confidant,
The minstrel singer, the woman of the minstrel singer class,
The attendant youth, guests
The men of the singing and dancing class,
The women of the singing and dancing class,
The men of sage wisdom
And the passers-by.

transliteration:
viṉai vayiṉ pirintōṉ mīṇṭu varu kālai
iṭaiccura maruṅkiṉ tavirtal illai
uḷḷam pōla uṟṟuḻi utavum
puḷ iyal kali mā uṭaimaiyāṉa.
translation:
No sojourn does the hero's journey across the parched tract mark
As he is homeward after his mission accomplished;
For he has at his possession
A sturdy horse swift as a bird
That abides at his service
As does his benignant heart.

title: Nature of Signification
transliteration:
icai tirintu icaippiṉum iyaiyumaṉ poruḷē
acai tirintu icaiyā eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The signification there stands unaltered
Even as the patterns of structure find alterations;
Being so,
The syllabic sequences therein
Do abide with no variations,
So have the learned men ruled.

title: The Monologic Utterances of Hero and Heroine
transliteration:
nōyum iṉpamum iru vakai nilaiyiṉ
kāmam kaṇṇiya marapiṭai teriya
eṭṭaṉ pakutiyum viḷaṅka oṭṭiya
uṟuppuṭaiyatu pōl uṇarvuṭaiyatu pōl
maṟuttu uraippatu pōl neñcoṭu puṇarttum
collā marapiṉ avaṟṟoṭu keḻīi
ceyyā marapiṉ toḻiṟpaṭuttu aṭakkiyum
avar avar uṟu piṇi tama pōl cērttiyum
aṟivum pulaṉum vēṟupaṭa niṟīi
iru peyar mūṉṟum uriya āka
uvamavāyil paṭuttalum uvamam
oṉṟu iṭattu iruvarkkum uriya pāṟ kiḷavi.
translation:
The monologic utterances
That issue from the mindscapes
Of the hero and heroine are:
Addresses to the heart
As if it were a living body with sense organs endowed,
That manifest the eightfold emotions
[Laughter, weeping, despisedness, wonder
Fear, pride, anger and joy],
As if it breathed feelings alive and living,
And as if it offered denials and refutations —
Such addresses being informed of the passion of love
The passion that alternates between pain and pleasure;
Apostrophes to things personified
Attributing to them deeds they cannot perform;
Taking the afflictions of the other
As if it were one's own;
Holding the mind and sense impressions apart;
And finding similitude where appropriate
Between the three human class genders
And the two non-human class genders
In relation to their attributes and actions.

title: Occasioning of Dreams
transliteration: kaṉavum urittāl av iṭattāṉa.
translation:
Where denial of union occasions in their love career,
The hero and the heroine fall into dreaming too.

transliteration: tāykkum urittāl pōkku uṭaṉ kiḷappiṉ.
translation:
The elopement of her daughter with the hero revealed,
The mother too has visions of dream.

title: Characters Given to Monologic Utterances
transliteration:
pāl keḻu kiḷavi nālvarkkum urittē
naṭpiṉ naṭakkai āṅku alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
The monologic utterances above [1140]
Are proper to
The heroine, her confidante,
Foster-mother and heroine's mother,
Where the things addressed are non-humans
Which are alien tọ the warmth of intimacy.

title: Traits of Principal Women Characters
transliteration:
uyirum nāṇum maṭaṉum eṉṟu ivai
ceyir tīr ciṟappiṉ nālvarkkum uriya.
translation:
The four women of unsullied excellence above [H43]
Are endowed with
Soul's intimacy amongst themselves,
Coyness and credulity.

title: The Unique Delineation of the Heroine
transliteration:
vaṇṇam pacantu pulampuṟu kālai
uṇarnta pōla uṟuppiṉaik kiḻavi
puṇarnta vakaiyāṉ puṇarkkavum peṟumē.
translation:
As the heroine suffers the anguish of lonesomeness,
With the complexion of her beauties having withered,
Her limbs are spoken of | U
As if they partook of her disconsolate state.

transliteration:
uṭampum uyirum vāṭiyakkaṇṇum
eṉ uṟṟaṉakol ivai eṉiṉ allatai
kiḻavōṟ cērtal kiḻattikku illai.
translation:
ven when the lonesome heroine turns dispirited
And wears withering, emaciated limbs,
She never goes out seeking the hero's union,
But abides, exclaiming
'O whatever has befallen them’!

transliteration:
oru ciṟai neñcamoṭu ucāvum kālai
uriyatākalum uṇṭu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Hero's union she does think of
At those lonesome momens
When she addresses her hert.

transliteration:
taṉvayiṉ karattalum avaṉvayiṉ vēṭṭalum
aṉṉa iṭaṅkaḷ al vaḻi ellām
maṭaṉoṭu niṟṟal kaṭaṉ eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
At all moments,
Save the ones of the kind
When the hero covers up his debauchery with strumpets
And when she longs for his union,
The heroine does exercise her credulousness,
So has it been ruled.

title: Revelation of Clandestine Love
transliteration:
aṟattoṭu niṟkum kālattu aṉṟi
aṟattu iyal marapu ilaḷ tōḻi eṉpa.
translation:
The heroine's confidante
Wons nat reveal the clandestine love career of her lady,
Unu! e moment
The heroine should prefer
To make the revelation.
Thus goes the convention.

transliteration:
eḷittal ēttal vēṭkai uraittal
kūṟutal ucāatal ētīṭu talaippāṭu
uṇmai ceppum kiḷaviyoṭu tokaii
av eḻu vakaiya eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The confidante's revelation to the foster-mother
Of the clandestine love career of her lady
Manifests in seven modes:
Speaking of the hero's humbleness of conduct towards them,
Extolling his worth and loftiness of behaviour,
Disclosing the longing of one for the other,
Suggesting the need to unite them in marriage,
Tendentious queries to the diviners and frenzied dancer,
Mentioning the chance occurrence of an event
That brought the two into the union of love,
And presenting the truths of clandestine course.

transliteration:
uṟṟuḻi allatu collal iṉmaiyiṉ
ap poruḷ vēṭkai kiḻaviyiṉ uṇarpa.
translation:
The features and conduct of the heroine betraying,
Her passion of love comes to be inferred;
For she would not reveal it by verbal modes
Save in moments of disconsolate passion.

title: Traits of Women Characters
transliteration:
ceṟivum niṟaivum cemmaiyum ceppum
aṟivum arumaiyum peṇpālāṉa.
translation:
Temperance, fulness of bearing, uprightness,
Facility of the tongue, discrimination and discernment
Are traits marked in women.

title: Modes of Urging the Hero to Marry the Heroine
transliteration:
poḻutum āṟum kāppum eṉṟu ivaṟṟiṉ
vaḻuviṉ ākiya kuṟṟam kāṭṭalum
taṉṉai aḻitalum avaṇ ūṟu añcalum
iraviṉum pakaliṉum nī vā eṉṟalum
kiḻavōṉ taṉṉai vāral eṉṟalum
naṉmaiyum tīmaiyum piṟitiṉaik kūṟalum
purai paṭa vanta aṉṉavai piṟavum
varaital vēṭkaip poruḷa eṉpa.
translation:
Pointing to the perils attendant on
The hero's coming for union at inopportune time,
The hazards of the tract that he comes through,
The rigours of watch around,
Speaking of her anxiety and concern therein,
Expressing her apprehension of harm to the hero,
Changing the hour of trysting
From day to night and from night to day,
And instructing him not to come for trysting,
Drawing on things righteous and evil
To bring her point home
Anđd things such as these [by the confidante]
Are all the ones marked with the intent
To see the hero take the heroine in marriage,
Thus has it been ruled.

transliteration:
vēṭkai maṟuttuk kiḷantāṅku uraittal
marīiya maruṅkiṉ urittu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
It is enjoined on the heroine's confidante
To deny the hero trysts with her lady,
And speak her mind out in favour of marriage
When he keeps an extended clandestine career,
So has it been held.

title: Modes of Conveyance
transliteration:
tērum yāṉaiyum kutiraiyum piṟavum
ūrntaṉar iyaṅkalum uriyar eṉpa.
translation:
The hero takes
Chariot, elephant, horse and such of them too
As he journeys for trysting with the heroine
In his clandestine love career.

title: An Imaginative Device
transliteration:
uṇṭaṟku uriya allāp poruḷai
uṇṭaṉa pōlak kūṟalum marapē.
translation:
Usage admits of things
Being spoken of as 'having eaten’,
While they are endowed with no such faculty.

title: Heroine Subjected to Rigours of Watch
transliteration:
poruḷ eṉa moḻitalum varai nilai iṉṟē
kāppuk kaimmikutal uṇmaiyāṉa
aṉpē aṟaṉē iṉpam nāṇoṭu
tuṟanta oḻukkam paḻittu aṉṟu ākaliṉ
oṉṟum vēṇṭā kāppiṉuḷḷē.
translation:
When the heroine is subjected to rigours of watch,
That the confidante attributes it
To the heroine's parents looking for the gift of wealth:from the hero
Is not disallowed.
The heroine restrained at home
And subjected to the rigours of watch,
It is not unbecoming of her
To stay inattentive to thé virtues of
Kindness, righteousness of conduct,
The bliss of the passion of love
And her feminine reserve;
They are not looked for from her either.

title: Heroine Forbidden to Accompany the Hero
transliteration: curam eṉa moḻitalum varai nilai iṉṟē.
translation:
It is not disallowed
For the hero to forbid the heroine
To accompany him on his mission for riches,
Saying
'The tract I will journey through is an arid waste’.

title: Usage in Poetry
transliteration:
uyarntōr kiḷavi vaḻakkoṭu puṇartaliṉ
vaḻakku vaḻippaṭutal ceyyuṭkuk kaṭaṉē.
translation:
Usage
Being the word of the learned,
Propriety in poetry
Draws on conformity to the usage.

transliteration:
aṟak kaḻivu uṭaiyaṉa poruṭ payam paṭa variṉ
vaḻakku eṉa vaḻaṅkalum paḻittu aṉṟu eṉpa.
translation:
Where things removed from norms of propriety
Are seen structured in the Akam course,
It is not improper
For them to be treated as part of imaginative usage.

transliteration:
mikka poruḷiṉuḷ poruḷ vakai puṇarkka
nāṇut talaippiriyā nalvaḻip paṭuttē.
translation:
Propriety of demeanour of the heroine
Shall be deemed indispensable
In compositions of Akam mode
That embody contents of a lofty nature.

transliteration:
muṟaippeyar maruṅkiṉ keḻutakaip potuc col
nilaikku uri marapiṉ iru vīṟṟum urittē.
translation:
Among the kinship terms sanctified by convention,
Expressions felicitous there are [such as ellá]
Which stand designating both the sexes.

transliteration:
tāyattiṉ aṭaiyā īyac cellā
viṉaivayiṉ taṅkā vīṟṟuk koḷappaṭā
em eṉa varūum kiḻamait tōṟṟam
allāvāyiṉum pulluva uḷavē.
translation:
That which is not inherited by right of lineage,
That which does not come to one through acts of liberality,
That which is not earned through perseverance,
And that which is not extracted by means of variance —
Such of these claims of possession by one
Shall come appropriate in poetry
Albeit their contrarieties in worldly mores.

transliteration:
oru pāl kiḷavi eṉaip pāṟkaṇṇum
varu vakaitāṉē vaḻakku eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Usage is
What is specific and particular to one
Extends to things and persons of one's species [cf. 1159-61].

title: Pursuit of Pleasure
transliteration:
ellā uyirkkum iṉpam eṉpatu
tāṉ amarntu varūum mēvaṟṟu ākum.
translation:
Joy is
The joy of union between the sexes
That every living being accomplishes
As it unites in passion with its loving mate.

title: Pursuit of Prostitutes
transliteration:
parattai vāyil nālvarkkum urittē
nilat tiripu iṉṟu aḵtu eṉmaṉār pulavar.

title: Heroine's Mindscape
transliteration:
orutalai urimai vēṇṭiṉum makaṭūup
pirital accam uṇmaiyāṉum
ampalum alarum kaḷavu veḷippaṭukkum eṉṟu
añca vanta āṅku iru vakaiyiṉum
nōkkoṭu vanta iṭaiyūṟu poruḷiṉum
pōkkum varaivum maṉaivikaṇ tōṉṟum.
translation:
The heroine's mindscape encompasses:
Privileging her right of love for the hero,
Apprehension of separation by the hero,
Fear of her clandestine love career
Coming to be inferred by men
And becoming the subject of idle talk around,
Her longed for rendezvous with the hero
Running into impediments,
Willing desire to go on elopement with the hero,
And wanting the hero to take her in marriage.

title: Hero's Debauchery and the Interceders
transliteration:
varutta mikuti cuṭṭum kālai
urittu eṉa moḻipa vāḻkkaiyuḷ irakkam.
translation:
Felt concern and pity about the heroine's conjugal life
Mark the interceders
As they stand pointing to her parched anguish
At the hero's ways of debauchery.

title: Moments of Sulking and Passion
transliteration:
maṉaivi uyarvum kiḻavōṉ paṇivum
niṉaiyum kālai pulaviyuḷ uriya.
translation:
The dominance of the wife
And the suppliant postures of the husband
Are seen to mark
The moments of tiffs of passion between the two.

transliteration:
nikaḻ takai maruṅkiṉ vēṭkai mikutiyiṉ
pukaḻ takai varaiyār kaṟpiṉuḷḷē.
translation:
That the hero and the heroine in the fulness of passion
Adore each other
As they are in through the wedded course
Is not disallowed.

transliteration: iṟaiccitāṉē urip puṟattatuvē.
translation:
Iraicci is
The suggestive import
Paralleling the Akam thematic strand explicit [cf. 995-97, and 1184-85}.

transliteration:
iṟaicciyiṉ piṟakkum poruḷumār uḷavē
tiṟattu iyal maruṅkiṉ teriyumōrkkē.
translation:
That from iraicci
There emerges an implied subtext
Beside its evocative designation of flora and fauna
Will be obvious to men of discernment.

transliteration:
aṉpuṟu takuvaṉa iṟaicciyuḷ cuṭṭalum
vaṉpuṟai ākum varuntiya poḻutē.
translation:
Designating sights of flora and fauna in nature
That are evocative of love and tenderness
Is intended to bring comfort and reassurance
To the heroine in lonesome anguish.

title: The Import of the Hero's Praise
transliteration:
cey poruḷ accamum viṉaivayiṉ pirivum
meypeṟa uṇarttum kiḻavi pārāṭṭē.
translation:
That the hero resorts to praising his love
Will indicate by suggestion
His apprehension of her putting impediments
To his quest away from her,
And his intent to go on his mission
Parting from her.
Heroine's Attitude towards the Concubine

transliteration:
kaṟpuvaḻip paṭṭavaḷ parattaimai ēttiṉum
uḷḷattu ūṭal uṇṭu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Men of discernment will find that
That the heroine chooses praising the paramour
Is but a manifestation of her jealous variance.

transliteration:
kiḻavōḷ piṟaḷ kuṇam ivai eṉak kūṟi
kiḻavōṉ kuṟippiṉai uṇartaṟkum uriyaḷ.
translation:
The heroine will seek to read her husband's mind
By speaking of the presumed traits of the woman
Whom she suspects to be his paramour.

transliteration:
tam uṟu viḻumam parattaiyar kūṟiṉum
meymmaiyāka avarvayiṉ uṇarntum
talaittāṭ kaḻaṟal tam etirppoḻutu iṉṟē
malitalum ūṭalum avai alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
When her husband's paramours come
Relating tales of their grievance against him,
And when her heart feels these tales to be all truths,
She does not choose to admonish him at his face
Except in moments of the bliss of union with him
Andđd at the intervention of tiffs of feigned variance.

title: Mindscape of the Lonesome Heroine
transliteration:
poḻutu talaivaitta kaiyaṟu kālai
iṟanta pōlak kiḷakkum kiḷavi
maṭaṉē varuttam maruṭkai mikutiyoṭu
avai nāṟ poruṭkaṇ nikaḻum eṉpa.
translation:
Credulousness, despondence, bewilderment and passion exceeding
Mark the mindscape of the heroine
As she,
Remaining in lonesome distress at the advent of the season
When the hero has promised to be back home,
Gives vent to her anguished mind
As if there marked the season's close.

title: Confidante's Response to Hero's Solicitations
transliteration:
irantu kuṟaiyuṟṟa kiḻavaṉait tōḻi
nirampa nīkki niṟuttal aṉṟiyum
vāymai kūṟalum poy talaippeytalum
nal vakaiyuṭaiya nayattiṉ kūṟiyum
pal vakaiyāṉum paṭaikkavum peṟumē.

title: Nature of Utterances by the Hero
transliteration:
uyar moḻik kiḷavi uṟaḻum kiḷavi
aiyak kiḷavi āṭūuviṟku urittē.
translation:
Praising the heroine in terms lofty,
Comparing her with things and beings,
And speaking of her in awed wonder—
The hero's utterances shall comprise.

title: Confidante's Ruling Trait
transliteration:
uṟukaṇ ōmpal taṉ iyalpu ākaliṉ
uriyatākum tōḻikaṇ uraṉē.
translation:
Wit is verily the forte of the heroine's confidante,
Charged with guarding against
The impediments to the lovers’ union
That she is.

transliteration: uyar moḻik kiḷaviyum uriyavāl avaṭkē.
translation:
The confidante has the right to
Expressions of heightened signification too.

title: Nature of Interceder's Utterances
transliteration:
vāyiṟ kiḷavi veḷippaṭak kiḷattal
tā iṉṟu uriya tamtam kūṟṟē.
translation:
Expressions of undisguised import
Are but allowed
In the utterances of the interceders
Between the hero and heroine.
Ulļurai

transliteration:
uṭaṉuṟai uvamam cuṭṭu nakai ciṟappu eṉak
keṭal aru marapiṉ uḷḷuṟai aintē.
translation:
The suggestive device ullurai [995-97]
Representing a tradition of unbroken note
Has a fivefold ramification:
That which is co-existent (utanurai)',
Correlation between the tenor and vehicle (uvamam)’,
One signifier pointing to the other (cuffu)’,
Signification disguised in wit and humour (nakai),
And a unique event in nature implying a human signification (cirappu)’.

transliteration:
antam il ciṟappiṉ ākiya iṉpam
taṉvayiṉ varutalum vakutta paṇpē.
translation:
Ullurai the suggestive mode
Is also structured in poetry
For the bliss and ecstasy of the passion of love,
That abides without an end,
To be taken by the hero for good.

transliteration:
maṅkala moḻiyum vaiiya moḻiyum
māṟu il āṇmaiyiṉ colliya moḻiyum
kūṟiya maruṅkiṉ koḷḷum eṉpa.
translation:
The suggestive designation of passion's bliss apart,
Ulļļurai takes in
Euphemistic expressions such as
Auspicious words denoting things inauspicious’,
Decorous terms covering words of impropriety’,
And ascribing a slight to one's manly worth’.

title: Negative Traits Implying Positive Worth
transliteration:
ciṉaṉē pētaimai nimpiri nalkuravu
aṉai nāl vakaiyum ciṟappoṭu varumē.
translation:
The four traits of the hero and heroine —
Anger, ignorance, envy and penury —
Do occur in one
As attributes (implied) of their positive worth.

title: A Poetic Convention
transliteration:
aṉṉai eṉṉai eṉṟalum uḷavē
tol neṟi muṟaimai colliṉum eḻuttiṉum
tōṉṟā marapiṉa eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Annai and ennai* are terms
Not sanctioned in the grammar of letters or words;
But they are terms of wont and use in poetry
From days of old,
So do the literate hold.

title: Abstractions in Poetry
transliteration:
oppum uruvum veṟuppum eṉṟā
kaṟpum ērum eḻilum eṉṟā
cāyalum nāṇum maṭaṉum eṉṟā
nōyum vēṭkaiyum nukarvum eṉṟu āṅku
āvayiṉ varūum kiḷavi ellām
nāṭṭu iyal marapiṉ neñcu koḷiṉ allatu
kāṭṭalākāp poruḷa eṉpa.
translation:
Likeness, awe and abundance,
Fidelity of the loved to the lover, growth and loveliness,
Delicacy, coyness and credulousness,
Affliction, longing and enjoyment
Are all terms of the abstract kind
Discernible to the mind's eye;
They elude definitions of a concrete nature.

transliteration:
imaiyōr tēettum eṟi kaṭal varaippiṉum
avai il kālam iṉmaiyāṉa.
translation:
Whether it is the world of the celestials
Endowed with unwinking eyes,
Or the world encircled by the roaring seas,
There is no moment
When these abstractions [1189] are not marked.

title: Poetic Sentiments
transliteration:
paṇṇait tōṉṟiya eṇ nāṉku poruḷum
kaṇṇiya puṟaṉē nāl nāṉku eṉpa.
translation:
As the literate men say,
Thirty-two are the sources
That represent spheres of human sport
Wherein are born the eight emotions
With each emotion having four sources.*

transliteration: nāl iraṇṭu ākum pālumār uṇṭē.
translation:
These sixteen poetic sentiments
Come down to emotions of eight kinds.

title: Principal Emotions as Treated in Poetry
transliteration:
nakaiyē aḻukai iḷivaral maruṭkai
accam perumitam vekuḷi uvakai eṉṟu
ap pāl eṭṭē meyppāṭu eṉpa.
translation:
These eight kinds of manifest emotions are
Laughter, grief, disgust, wonder,
Fear, pride, anger and joy.

title: Sources of the Principal Emotions
transliteration:
eḷḷal iḷamai pētaimai maṭaṉ eṉṟu
uḷḷappaṭṭa nakai nāṉku eṉpa.
translation:
The four sources of laughter are
Ridicule, childishness, stupidity and credulity.

transliteration:
iḷivē iḻavē acaivē vaṟumai eṉa
viḷivu il koḷkai aḻukai nāṉkē.
translation:
The inexorable four sources of grief are
Contempt, deprivation, decline in stature and indigence.

transliteration:
mūppē piṇiyē varuttam meṉmaiyoṭu
yāppuṟa vanta iḷivaral nāṉkē.
translation:
The abiding four sources of disgust are
Decrepitude, sickliness, vexation and incapacitation.

transliteration:
putumai perumai ciṟumai ākkamoṭu
matimai cālā maruṭkai nāṉkē.
translation:
The four sources of wonder that overwhelm one's mind are
Novelty, hugeness, minuteness and transmutation.

transliteration:
aṇaṅkē vilaṅkē kaḷvar tam iṟai eṉap
piṇaṅkal cālā accam nāṉkē.
translation:
The four sources of unmitigated fear are
Demoniac beings, wild animals, thieves and monarchs.

transliteration:
kalvi taṟukaṇ pukaḻmai koṭai eṉac
collappaṭṭa perumitam nāṉkē.
translation:
The considered four sources of rightful pride are
Learning, prowess, unsullied fame and munificence absolute.

transliteration:
uṟuppaṟai kuṭikōḷ alai kolai eṉṟa
veṟuppiṉ vanta vekuḷi nāṉkē.
translation:
The four sources of detestable anger are
Cutting one's limbs, harming one's kin,
Inflicting pain and anguish and ‘killing’.

transliteration:
celvam pulaṉē puṇarvu viḷaiyāṭṭu eṉṟu
allal nītta uvakai nāṉkē.
translation:
The four sources of unmixed joy are
Riches, mind's might, sexual union and play.
Emotions other than the Principal Eight

transliteration:
āṅkavai oru pāl āka oru pāl
uṭaimai iṉpuṟal naṭuvunilai aruḷal
taṉmai aṭakkam varaital aṉpu eṉāa
kaimmikal nalital cūḻcci vāḻttal
nāṇutal tuñcal araṟṟu kaṉavu eṉāa
muṉital niṉaital verūutal maṭimai
karutal ārāycci viraivu uyirppu eṉāa
kaiyāṟu iṭukkaṇ poccāppu poṟāmai
viyarttal aiyam mikai naṭukku eṉāa
ivaiyum uḷavē avai alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
These eight emotions apart [1193],
There do manifest others too that inform of:
The sense of possession, being pleased,
Equipoise, benevolence, being true to one's nature,
Forbearance, discipline of the mind, amiability,
Abnormality, straining others, deliberation,
Benediction, shrinking off from acts of infamy
Slumberousness, faltering speech, dreaming,
Hating, reminiscing, fright, slothfulness,
Intention, study, sense of haste,
Sighing, helpless anguish, suffering,
Forgetfulness, envy, perspiration,
Irresoluteness, intemperance and trembling.

title: Emotions Proper to the Fivefold Akam Love: First Phase
transliteration:
puku mukam purital poṟi nutal viyarttal
naku nayam maṟaittal citaivu piṟarkku iṉmaiyoṭu
taku muṟai nāṉkē oṉṟu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The states of mind that there aptly manifest
As the hero and heroine are drawn by passion
In their clandestine pre-marital course are:
Her receptive posture as the hero's passionate eyes fall on her,
Her forehead wearing beads of sweating,
Her coyness concealing her inward longing and delight
And her keeping off from others
Her heart having been lost to him.

title: Second Phase
transliteration:
kūḻai virittal kātu oṉṟu kaḷaital
ūḻ aṇi taivaral uṭai peyarttu uṭuttaloṭu
ūḻi nāṉkē iraṇṭu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Her tresses flowing in loosened strands,
Dropping off an ear-ornanħent of hers,
Holding her ornaments fast worn in order though,
And keeping on setting her dress to order —
The second phase of the states of mind of the lovers,
As they are through their clandestine love career,
Stands betrayed in the deeds of passion above.

title: Third Phase
transliteration:
alkul taivaral aṇintavai tiruttal
il valiyuṟuttal iru kaiyum eṭuttaloṭu
colliya nāṉkē mūṉṟu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The third phase of the clandestine love manifests in:
Her seeing her hips down off from exposure as the garments slip,
Correcting the waist-ornaments thereon,
Her pretence to be unassailed by slings of passion,
And her hands rising her pretence notwithstanding.

title: Fourth Phase
transliteration:
pārāṭṭu eṭuttal maṭam tapa uraittal
īram il kūṟṟam ēṟṟu alar nāṇal
koṭuppavai kōṭal uḷappaṭat tokaii
eṭutta nāṉkē nāṉku eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The heroine's ecstactic recollecting and praise
Of the hero's acts of love towards her,
Her utterances shorn of her native credulousness,
Being down with coyness at the gossip
The unkind tongues of the town indulge in about their love,
And her willing acceptance of the hero's gifts of love —
Such are the externalizations of the fourth phase
That mark the clandestine love career of the two.

title: Fifth Phase
transliteration:
terintu uṭampaṭutal tiḷaippu viṉai maṟuttal
karantiṭattu oḻital kaṇṭavaḻi uvattaloṭu
poruntiya nāṉkē aintu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The fifth phase of their clandestine love career manifests in —
The heroine's consent for her clandestine course
To be revealed to her kin at home
Having weighed the consequences thereof,
Her shunning sports and such acts of pleasure
With her clandestine career revealed to kinsmen,
Her willed solitude off her lover's access
As she is subjected to rigours of watch at home,
And her feeling of ecstasy
As there occasions her meeting the hero.

title: Sixth Phase
transliteration:
puṟam ceyac citaital pulampit tōṉṟal
kalaṅki moḻital kaiyaṟavu uraittaloṭu
viḷampiya nāṉkē āṟu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The state of mind that is revealed in
The sixth phase of the clandestine course are:
The lonesome heroine turning heart-sick
Her falling into a mood of despondence,
Her utterances of dismay and distress,
And her wearing a sense of helplessness.

title: Manifestation and Absence of Emotions
transliteration:
aṉṉa piṟavum avaṟṟoṭu civaṇi
maṉṉiya viṉaiya nimittam eṉpa.
translation:
These states of mind in the six phases above
[Which ramify into twenty-four emotional manifestations]
And other kindred emotions too
Inform the mutuality of union between the hero and heroine.

transliteration: viṉai uyir melivu iṭattu iṉmaiyum urittē.
translation:
There may manifest
None of the emotions mentioned above
Where there marks
The extreme torment of passion
That keeps the heroine's heart disconsolate.

transliteration: avaiyum uḷavē avai alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
There do occasion other emotions too
Where the twenty-four above [1209]
Do not come to the fore. |
Other Emotions Proper to the Passion of Love.

transliteration:
iṉpattai veṟuttal tuṉpattup pulampal
etir peytu parital ētam āytal
paci aṭa niṟṟal pacalai pāytal
uṇṭiyiṉ kuṟaital uṭampu naṉi curuṅkal
kaṇ tuyil maṟuttal kaṉavoṭu mayaṅkal
poyyāk kōṭal meyyē eṉṟal
aiyam ceytal avaṉ tamar uvattal
aṟaṉ aḷittu uraittal āṅku neñcu aḻital
em mey āyiṉum oppumai kōṭal
oppuvaḻi uvattal uṟu peyar kēṭṭal
nalat taka nāṭiṉ kalakkamum atuvē.
translation:
They are [1211]:
Disrelishing objects of pleasure, lonesome wailing,
Holding the hero before her mind's eye and grieving,
Reflecting on the impediments to her union with the hero,
Shunning the call of hunger,
Her complexion wearing a pallid hue,
Reduced intake of food,
Her body emaciating and wasting away,
Her eyes refusing to get to sleep,
Getting disconcerted in dreamy visions of the hero,
Taking things authentic for things of guile,
Calling delusions truths seen and felt,
Being gladdened at heart at the sight of his kinsfolk,
Standing reproachful at things righteous,
Turning disheartened thereat,
Finding parallels between the hero and whatever she sees,
Such imagined parallels bringing her delight,
Rejoicing at words about the hero's lofty note
And marked with ways irresolute.

title: Emotions Preparatory to the Wedded Course
transliteration:
muṭṭuvayiṉ kaḻaṟal muṉivu meyn niṟuttal
accattiṉ akaṟal avaṉ puṇarvu maṟuttal
tūtu muṉivu iṉmai tuñcic cērtal
kātal kaimmikal kaṭṭurai iṉmai eṉṟu
āyiru nāṉkē aḻivu il kūṭṭam.
translation:
The undistressed states of mind
That lead into the wedded course are:
Utterances of assertion by the heroine
As her union with the hero runs into obstacles,
Her expressions of overt indignation therein,
Her shunning trysts due to fear of public knowledge,
Her keeping off from union with him by day and by night,
Her not frowning at interceders from the hero,
Her feigned sleep in a mood of despondency,
Her giving in to passion of love exceeding,
And her falling into speechlessness.

title: Emotions Proper to the Wedded Course
transliteration:
teyvam añcal purai aṟam teḷital
illatu kāytal uḷḷatu uvarttal
puṇarntuḻi uṇmai poḻutu maṟuppu ākkam
aruḷ mika uṭaimai aṉpu toka niṟṟal
pirivu āṟṟāmai maṟaintavai uraittal
puṟañcol māṇāk kiḷaviyoṭu tokaii
ciṟanta pattum ceppiya poruḷē.
translation:
The emotional states manifest
Attendant on the wedded course are:
The heroine being in awe of the deity,
Her realizing the virtues as meets wedded life,
Her being angry at a failing imagined in the hero,
Her fastidious discountenance about the hero's love,
Her acquiescence in the ecstasy of union,
Her access to the joy of union
Sans the restraints of trysts apportioned,
The springs of love marked with abundant flow,
Heart's affections all at play,
The pain of separation weighing heavily on her,
And pouring out her heart
At the heartless words of slander around
During the course of their clandestine career.

title: Traits of Compatibility
transliteration:
piṟappē kuṭimai āṇmai āṇṭoṭu
uruvu niṟutta kāma vāyil
niṟaiyē aruḷē uṇarvoṭu tiru eṉa
muṟaiyuṟak kiḷanta oppiṉatu vakaiyē.
translation:
The hero and heroine united in love,
There mark a harmony and compatibility in
Lineage, conduct as behoving such ancestry,
Fortitude, age, physical form,
Propensity and inclination to sexual passion,
Steadfastness, graciousness of demeanour,
A discerning mind and material endowment.

title: Negatives that Mar Conjugal Harmony
transliteration:
nimpiri koṭumai viyappoṭu puṟamoḻi
vaṉcol poccāppu maṭimaiyoṭu kuṭimai
iṉpuṟal ēḻaimai maṟappoṭu oppumai
eṉṟu ivai iṉmai eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The traits undesirable
Between the hero and heroine are:
Jealousy, hard-heartedness, egocentricity,
Slander, harsh words, irresoluteness,
Indolence, pride in one's high birth,
Naivety, forgetfulness and finding parallels outside.

title: Subtleties of Emotional Manifestations
transliteration:
kaṇṇiṉum ceviyiṉum tiṇṇitiṉ uṇarum
uṇarvuṭai māntarkku allatu teriyiṉ
nal nayap poruḷkōḷ eṇṇa aruṅkuraittē.

title: Grounds of Comparison
transliteration:
viṉai payaṉ mey uru eṉṟa nāṉkē
vakai peṟa vanta uvamat tōṟṟam.
translation:
Four are the grounds for comparison
Between the tenor and the vehicle:
The deed done’, the effect thereof’,
The form’ and the complexion‘.

transliteration: viraviyum varūum marapiṉa eṉpa.
translation:
The grounds for comparison above [1218]
Do get intermingled too.

transliteration: uyarntataṉ mēṟṟē uḷḷum kālai.
translation:
As we examine them,
The vehicles of comparison
Do stand loftier than the tenors.

title: Sources of Similitude
transliteration:
ciṟappē nalaṉē kātal valiyoṭu
an nāl paṇpum nilaikkaḷam eṉpa.
translation:
Pre-eminence', loveliness’, love? and might‘
Are the four characteristics
That abide as sources of similitude.

transliteration: kiḻakkiṭu poruḷoṭu aintum ākum.
translation:
Five characteristics the sources above [1221] come to
As one includes things lowly.

transliteration:
mutalum ciṉaiyum eṉṟu āyiru poruṭkum
nutaliya marapiṉ uriyavai uriya.
translation:
The whole and the part of a thing
Do stand tenors and vehicles of comparison
In tune with the usage sanctioned.

title: Inexplicit Vehicle
transliteration:
cuṭṭik kūṟā uvamam āyiṉ
poruḷ etir puṇarttup puṇarttaṉa koḷalē.
translation:
Where the vehicle does not point to the tenor
In terms manifest,
They need to be correlated appropriately.

title: Nature of Similitude
transliteration: uvamamum poruḷum ottal vēṇṭum.
translation:
The vehicle and the tenor in similitude
Must be in accord with norms of propriety.

transliteration:
poruḷē uvamam ceytaṉar moḻiyiṉum
maruḷ aṟu ciṟappiṉ aḵtu uvamam ākum.
translation:
Where the tenor is made the vehicle
[And the vehicle the tenor],
It is the mode of comparison proper
Insofar as the vehicle-turned tenor
Abides as one of a loftier note.

transliteration:
perumaiyum ciṟumaiyum ciṟappiṉ tīrāk
kuṟippiṉ varūum neṟippāṭu uṭaiya.
translation:
Correlation of things loftier and lowly
Is but in accord with the norm set
That the pre-eminence of a thing
Is a source of similitude [1221].

title: Comparison Markers
transliteration:
avaitām,
aṉṉa ēyppa uṟaḻa oppa
eṉṉa māṉa eṉṟavai eṉāa
oṉṟa oṭuṅka oṭṭa āṅka
eṉṟa viyappa eṉṟavai eṉāa
eḷḷa viḻaiya viṟappa nikarppa
kaḷḷa kaṭuppa āṅkavai eṉāa
kāyppa matippa takaiya maruḷa
māṟṟa maṟuppa āṅkavai eṉāa
pulla poruva poṟpa pōla
vella vīḻa āṅkavai eṉāa
nāṭa naḷiya naṭuṅka nanta
ōṭa puraiya eṉṟavai eṉāa
āṟu āṟu avaiyum aṉṉa piṟavum
kūṟum kālaip pal kuṟippiṉavē.

title: Functional Delimitation of Comparison Markers
transliteration:
aṉṉa āṅka māṉa viṟappa
eṉṉa uṟaḻa takaiya nōkkoṭu
kaṇṇiya eṭṭum viṉaippāl uvamam.
translation:
Where the ground for comparison is the deed done,
The markers of similitude therein are eight in number:
Anna, āñka, māņa, irappa,
Enna, urala, takaiya and nokka.

transliteration: aṉṉa eṉ kiḷavi piṟavoṭum civaṇum.
translation:
The similitude marker anna above [1229]
Does go with other grounds for comparison too
[Effect of a deed, form and complexion (1218)].

transliteration:
eḷḷa viḻaiya pulla poruva
kaḷḷa matippa vella vīḻa
eṉṟu āṅku eṭṭē payaṉilai uvamam.
translation:
Ella, viļlaiya, pulla, poruva,
Kalla, matippa, vella and vila
Are the eight markers of similitude
Where the ground for comparison is the effect of a deed.

transliteration:
kaṭuppa ēyppa maruḷa puraiya
oṭṭa oṭuṅka ōṭa nikarppa eṉṟu
ap pāl eṭṭē meyppāl uvamam.
translation:
Where the ground for comparison is the form,
The markers of similitude therein are eight in number:
Kațuppa, ēyppa, maruļa, puraiya
Otta, otunka, ota and nikarppa.

transliteration:
pōla maṟuppa oppa kāytta
nēra viyappa naḷiya nanta eṉṟu
ottu varu kiḷavi uruviṉ uvamam.
translation:
Where the ground for comparison is the complexion,
The markers of similitude therein are:
Pōla, maruppa, oppa, kāytta
Neēra, viyappa, naļiya and nanta.

transliteration: tamtam marapiṉ tōṉṟumaṉ poruḷē.
translation:
The delimitation of designations above [1229-1233]
Is what is handed down by tradition.

title: Ramification of Grounds for Comparison
transliteration: nāl iraṇṭu ākum pālumār uṇṭē.
translation:
The fourfold grounds for comparison [1218]
May ramify into eight* too.

title: Similitude and the Eightfold Emotions
transliteration:
perumaiyum ciṟumaiyum meyppāṭu eṭṭaṉ
vaḻi maruṅku aṟiyat tōṉṟum eṉpa.
translation:
Similes informing greatness and smallness
Will have the eightfold manifestations of emotions [1193]
For their sources explicit and well-defined.

title: Tenor and Vehicle
transliteration:
uvamap poruḷiṉ uṟṟatu uṇarum
teḷi maruṅku uḷavē tiṟattu iyalāṉa.
translation:
That one discerns
The nature and import of the tenor
Through the vehicle known
Is possible in contexts of a discourse.

transliteration:
uvamap poruḷai uṇarum kālai
marīiya marapiṉ vaḻakkoṭu varumē.
translation:
The discernment of the tenor's import above [1237]
Shall go in accord with the tradition long set.

transliteration: iraṭṭaikkiḷavi iraṭṭai vaḻittē.
translation:
The tenor too marks the same structuring
Where the vehicle holds two components.

title: Ullurai Uvamam
transliteration:
piṟitoṭu paṭātu piṟappoṭu nōkki
muṉṉai marapiṉ kūṟum kālai
tuṇivoṭu varūum tuṇiviṉōr koḷiṉē.
translation:
The vehicle stands correlated with a tenor
Which cries for no explicit manifestation;
The vehiçle does bear on the land of its origin,
And is related to an occurrence therein
Vis-a-vis the flora and fauna of that land;
And the tenor there unfolds by implication,
Which the literate mind discerns right.
(A definition of the unique suggestive mode called uļļurai uvamam. e.g.
The red-eyed buffalo
Detesting its stay in the muddy place
During the evening when the village sleeps,
Breaks the strong rope,
Removes the sharp thorny fence with horns,
Plunges into the watery field,
The fish to flee,
Twists the water-creepers
And eats the coo! flower thronged by bees.
Here the conduct of the Akam hero is set on a buffalo: buffalo hero; breaking
the rope - destroying prestige; horn - his messenger; flower courtesan; field
- her residence; fish - her attendants; bees - other men attracted towards her cf.
verses 995, 996, 997, 1184, 1185, 1186, 1241, 1242).

transliteration: uvamap pōli aintu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The suggestive mode [ul]urai uvamam] mentioned above [1240]
Is said to be of five kinds.

transliteration:
taval aruñ ciṟappiṉ at taṉmai nāṭiṉ
viṉaiyiṉum payattiṉum uṟuppiṉum uruviṉum
piṟappiṉum varūum tiṟatta eṉpa.
translation:
As we examine these five kinds [1241]
In relation to their flawless excellence,
The parallelism between the explicit vehicle
And the implied tenor
Operates on five factors of similitude:
Deed, effect of the deed, form, complexion and origin.

title: Vehicles in the Similitude of Characters
transliteration: kiḻavi colliṉ avaḷ aṟi kiḷavi.
translation:
The things she is familiar with
Shall go into the vehicle of the similitude
Which the utterance of the heroine embodies.

transliteration: tōḻikku āyiṉ nilam peyarntu uraiyātu.
translation:
The vehicle in the similitude
Which goes into the utterance of the heroine's confidante
Shall not hold things
Outside of the region she belongs to.

transliteration: kiḻavōṟku āyiṉ uraṉoṭu kiḷakkum.
translation:
The vehicle of the similitude
In the utterance of the hero
Shall encompass all things
That come within the province of his knowledge.

transliteration: ēṉōrkku ellām iṭam varaivu iṉṟē.

Run through kalippa verses.
Closing of Vañcippa

transliteration: vañcit tūkkē centūkku iyaṟṟē.
translation:
The closing of vañcippa
Resembles that of åciriyappa
[With three-footed penultimate lines}.

title: Venpā Ending
transliteration:
veṇpāṭṭu īṟṟu aṭi muc cīrttu ākum
acai cīrttu ākum av vaḻiyāṉa.
translation:
Three-footed is the end line of venpa,
The last of which is
A foot of one metrical syllable.

transliteration:
nēr īṟṟu iyaṟcīr niraiyum niraipum
cīr ēṟṟu iṟūum iyaṟkaiya eṉpa.
translation:
Where the foot of a penultimate venpa line
Is the nêr-formulaic-ending iyarcir,
The end-foot of the line shall be
Niraiyacai or niraipacai metrical syllable.

transliteration:
nirai avaṇ niṟpiṉ nērum nērpum
varaivu iṉṟu eṉpa vāy moḻip pulavar.
translation:
Where the foot of a penultimate veņpā line
Is the nirai-formulaic-ending iyarcir,
The occurrence of neracai or nêērpacai
As the end-foot of the line
Shall not be disallowed,
As do men of discernment hold.

title: Kalippa Ending
transliteration: eḻu cīr iṟuti āciriyam kaliyē.
translation:
The penultimate and ending lines of kalippā
Shall have three and four feet respectively
After the structure of āciriyappā lines.

transliteration: veṇpā iyaliṉum paṇpuṟa muṭiyum.
translation:
The ending of kalippā
Shall be after the nature of veņpå's.

title: Structure of a Composition
transliteration:
eḻuttu mutalā īṇṭiya aṭiyiṉ
kuṟitta poruḷai muṭiya nāṭṭal
yāppu eṉa moḻipa yāppu aṟi pulavar.
translation:
Learned men versed in prosody hold that
A composition is —
To treat of the fulness of the subject intended
Through the lines of verse
Made of the limbs aforesaid
From letters through syllables and feet.

title: Modes of a Composition
transliteration:
pāṭṭu urai nūlē vāymoḻi piciyē
aṅkatam mutucol av ēḻ nilattum
vaṇ pukaḻ mūvar taṇ poḻil varaippiṉ
nāṟ peyar ellai akattavar vaḻaṅkum
yāppiṉ vaḻiyatu eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Poetry, prose;
Expository works, gnomic writings,
Riddles, satires, and proverbs
Are the seven classes of composition in verse
That have been in vogue and use
Among folks of the land of four extended boundaries,
The land abounding in cool groves
And .under the reign of three monarchs of benign note,
Thus have the literate held. ‘

title: Usage
transliteration:
marapētāṉum,
nāṟ col iyalāṉ yāppuvaḻip paṭṭaṉṟu.
translation:
Conventions of usage are
What has been marked in compositions in verse
Whose constituents are the four classes of words [880].

title: Verse Rhythm
transliteration: akaval eṉpatu āciriyammē.
translation:
The akava! rhythm
[The loud notes of call like those of a peacock]
Is proper to āciriyappā verse kind.

transliteration: atāaṉṟu eṉpa veṇpā yāppē.
translation:
The notes of call above [1333]
Do not go with the veņpā verse kind
[It is of a recitative sort). |

transliteration: tuḷḷal ōcai kali eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The jumping rhythmic cadence
Is appropriate to kalippå verse kind
So has it been ruled.

transliteration: tūṅkal ōcai vañci ākum.
translation:
The one suited to vañcippā verse kind is
The balanced sleeping rhythm.

transliteration:
maruṭpā ēṉai iru cār allatu
tāṉ itu eṉṉum taṉinilai iṉṟē.
translation:
Marutpa `
[Wherein veņpā and āciriyappā metres occur alternately]
Has no rhythm unique to itself
Apart from the rhythms of veņpa and ācíriyappa.

transliteration: av iyal allatu pāṭṭu āṅkuk kiḷavār.
translation:
No verse kind structured there is
In rhythmic cadences other than the above [1333-37].

transliteration: tūkku iyal vakaiyē āṅku eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
These four
[Notes of call, recitative, jumping and sleeping rhythms]
Are the verse rhythms proper,
So has it been ruled.

title: Modes of Rhyming
transliteration:
mōṉai etukai muraṇē iyaipu eṉa
nāl neṟi marapiṉa toṭai vakai eṉpa.
translation:
Fourfold are the modes of rhyming in verse:
Monai, etukai, muraņ and iyaipu*.

transliteration: aḷapeṭai talaippeya aintum ākum.
translation:
Aļapetai
[Vowel elongations] including,
The modes of rhyming come to five [1340].

transliteration:
poḻippum orūuvum centoṭai marapum
amaittaṉar teriyiṉ avaiyumār uḷavē.
translation:
If one were to examine
Polippu [occurrence of mōnai, etc in the first and third feet of
Orūu [agreement of sound features between the first and fourth feet
And centotai [mõnai, etc being ignored],
They too would come under patterns of rhyming.

transliteration:
niral niṟuttu amaittalum iraṭṭai yāppum
moḻintavaṟṟu iyalāṉ muṟṟum eṉpa.
translation:
Niralnirai [words being so arranged in groups that each word of one group
And irațttaittotai [the same word being repeated throughout a verse line]
Do complement the classes of rhyming.

title: Monaittotai
transliteration: aṭitoṟum talai eḻuttu oppatu mōṉai.
translation:
Mõnņaittotai is the kind of rhyming
Where there marks
The same letter at the beginning of every metrical line.

transliteration: aḵtu oḻittu oṉṟiṉ etukai ākum.
translation:
Etukaittotțai is the kind of rhyming
Where it is
The second letter agreement in every line. .

transliteration: āyiru toṭaikkum kiḷaiyeḻuttu uriya.
translation:
In both mōnņai and etukai above [1344-45],
The agreement is also among
The kindred letters of the same class.

transliteration: moḻiyiṉum poruḷiṉum muraṇutal muraṇē.
translation:
Muraņ is the kind of rhyming in every line
Marked by antithesis or contrast
In words or in their senses.

transliteration: iṟuvāy oṉṟal iyaipiṉ yāppē.
translation:
Iyaiputtoțai is the kind of rhyming
Where at the end of every line
There occurs the same |letter.

transliteration: aḷapu eḻiṉ avaiyē aḷapeṭait toṭaiyē.
translation:
Aļapetțaittoțai is the kind of rhyming
Where elongation of letters marks every line.

transliteration:
oru cīr iṭaiyiṭṭu etukai āyiṉ
poḻippu eṉa moḻital pulavar āṟē.
translation:
Poļipputtoțtai is the kind of rhyming
Where there is
Agreement of second letters*
In the alternate feet of a line.
Orūttoţtai

transliteration: iru cīr iṭaiyiṭiṉ orūu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Orūuttotai is the kind of rhyming
Where marks agreement in the feet of a line
With the intervention of two feet in between.

title: Centotai
transliteration:
colliya toṭaiyoṭu vēṟupaṭṭu iyaliṉ
col iyaṟ pulavar atu centoṭai eṉpa.
translation:
Centotțai is the kind of rhyming
Which finds variation
From the patterns of rhyming mentioned above [1340-51]

transliteration:
mey peṟu marapiṉ toṭai vakaitāmē
ai īr āyirattu āṟu aiñṟṟoṭu
toṇṭu talai iṭṭa pattuk kuṟai eḻunūṟṟu
oṉpaḵtu eṉpa uṇarnticiṉōrē.
translation:
Those versed in conventions of prosody
That have since evolved hold that
The cadences of rhyming in verse
Number thirteen thousand six hundred and ninety-nine.*

transliteration: terintaṉar virippiṉ varampu ila ākum.
translation:
They might ramify into numbers illimitable
Were the discerning minds to go into these rhymes [1353].

transliteration: toṭai vakai nilaiyē āṅku eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Such is the nature
Of the patterns of rhyming in verse,
As the literate men have pronounced.
Nõkku

transliteration:
māttirai mutalā aṭinilai kāṟum
nōkkutal kāraṇam nōkku eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
The Nökku is the interpretive device
That draws on its constituents
From its phonic measure of sounds
Through its metrical line.

title: Verse Classes
transliteration:
āciriyam vañci veṇpā kali eṉa
nāl iyaṟṟu eṉpa pā vakai viriyē.
translation:
Four are the classes of versification:
Åciriyappa, vañcippāa, veņpa and kalippa.

title: Subjects Treated in Verse Compositions
transliteration:
an nilai maruṅkiṉ aṟam mutal ākiya
mum mutal poruṭkum uriya eṉpa.
translation:
The three themes of human pursuit —
Aram [modes of righteous living]
Porul [aspects of material fulfilment]
And ippam [the bliss of love between a man and woman] —
Stand treated through these four verse kinds [1357].
The Inclusiveness of Åciriyappā and Veņpā

transliteration:
pā viri maruṅkiṉaip paṇpuṟat tokuppiṉ
āciriyappā veṇpā eṉṟu āṅku
āyiru pāviṉuḷ aṭaṅkum eṉpa.
translation:
The four classes of verse above [1357]
Are said to be encompassed within
Aciriyappā and veņpā kinds.

transliteration:
āciriya naṭaittē vañci ēṉai
veṇpā naṭaittē kali eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
[For]
Vañcippā is composed after áciriyappa
And kalippā stands kindred to veņpā.

title: Compositions of Benediction
transliteration: vāḻttiyal vakaiyē nāṟpākkum urittē.
translation:
All the four classes of versification [1357]
Do lend themselves to
Compositions of praise and benediction.

transliteration:
vaḻipaṭu teyvam niṉ puṟaṅkāppa
paḻi tīr celvamoṭu vaḻi vaḻi ciṟantu
polimiṉ eṉṉum puṟanilai vāḻttē
kali nilai vakaiyum vañciyum peṟāa.
translation:
Kalippa and vañcippā however
Do not stand appropriate to puranilaivālttu compositions,
Wherein
The tutelary deity of one is invoked
For one and one's descendants to flourish
Endowed with fortunes of flawlessn9te.
Vayurai, Avaiyațtakkiyal and Ceviyarivuruu

transliteration:
vāyuṟai vāḻttē avaiyaṭakkiyalē
ceviyaṟivuṟūu eṉa avaiyum aṉṉa.
translation:
Vāyurai vālttu, avaiyatakkiyal and ceviyarivurūu*
Are not treated in kalippā and vañcippa compositions either.

transliteration:
vāyuṟai vāḻttē vayaṅka nāṭiṉ
vēmpum kaṭuvum pōla veñ col
tāṅkutal iṉṟi vaḻi naṉi payakkum eṉṟu
ōmpaṭaik kiḷaviyiṉ vāyuṟuttaṟṟē.
translation:
As we examine it in terms explicit,
Vayurai vālttu is salutary advice and exhortation
Administered to one nolens volens
For the good of one and one's descendants
Through words that do not exclude
Those of bitter import
As do morgosa and gallnut have.

transliteration:
avaiyaṭakkiyalē aril tapat teriyiṉ
vallā kūṟiṉum vakuttaṉar koṇmiṉ eṉṟu
enm,
translation:
ellā māntarkkum vaji molintaņrēë.
Avaiyațakkiyal, if examined faultlessly,
Is an apologetic petition by one to a public assembly
To exercise discernment and discrimination
And sift out the good from whatever unworthy is said.

transliteration:
ceviyuṟaitāṉē,
poṅkutal iṉṟi puraiyōr nāppaṇ
avital kaṭaṉ eṉac ceviyuṟuttaṉṟē.
translation:
Ceviyurai is exhortation to one
Not to give in to anger and self-adulation
But to stand humble in the midst of the great.

title: Nerati
transliteration:
ottāḻicaiyum maṇṭila yāppum
kuṭṭamum nēraṭikku oṭṭiṉa eṉpa.
translation:
The four-footed nēërati line stands appropriate to
Ottālicai [a constituent of ottālicaik kalippā)
Mantilam [aciriyappā of all four-footed lines]
And kuttam [kalippā constituent of reduced feet].

title: Taravu
transliteration: kuṭṭam eruttaṭi uṭaittum ākum.
translation:
Taravu the opening constituent of kalippaā
Will have its penultimate line
Composed of three feet.
Manņtilam and Kuttam

transliteration:
maṇṭilam kuṭṭam eṉṟu ivai iraṇṭum
centūkku iyala eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The learned find
Maņtilam and kuttam above [1367]
Are limbs of àciriyappā metre.

title: Venpā Metre
transliteration:
neṭuveṇpāṭṭē kuṟuveṇpāṭṭē
kaikkiḷai paripāṭṭu aṅkatac ceyyuḷoṭu

translation:
Veņpā's metrical form does bear upon
Netuvenņpattu [five to twelve-lined veņpa stanza]
Kuruvenpāttu [two to three-lined veņpa stanza],
Kaikkiļai [stanza on unrequited passion of love]
Paripātal [mułti-lined, multi-limbed musical verses with fewer metrical
And añkatam [satirical verses].

title: Kaikkilai
transliteration:
kaikkiḷaitāṉē veṇpā āki
āciriya iyalāṉ muṭiyavum peṟumē.
translation:
Taking veņpa metre apart,
Verses on unrequited passion
Will have venpa metre in the first two lines
And äciriyappāa metre in the next two lines (marutpâ) too.
Paripātal

transliteration:
paripāṭallē tokai nilai vakaiyiṉ
itu pā eṉṉum iyal neṟi iṉṟi
potuvāy niṟṟaṟkum urittu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Paripatal in general
Will have no metrical kind of its own,
And stands composed in all metres, so has it been ruled.

transliteration:
koccakam arākam curitakam eruttoṭu
ceppiya nāṉkum taṉakku uṟuppu āka
kāmam kaṇṇiya nilaimaittu ākum.
translation:
The theme of Akam love for its subject matter,
Paripātal has for its four constituents
Koccakam, arākam, curitakam and eruttu

transliteration:
coṟcīr aṭiyum muṭukiyal aṭiyum
ap pā nilaimaikku uriya ākum.
translation:
Paripatal will be structured in
Corcīratř and mutukiyalatř lines.

title: Corcirati
transliteration:
kaṭṭurai vakaiyāṉ eṇṇoṭu puṇarntum
muṭṭaṭi iṉṟik kuṟaivu cīrttu ākiyum
moḻi acai ākiyum vaḻi acai puṇarntum
coṟcīrttu iṟutal coṟcīrkku iyalpē.
translation:
Corcīrati is characterized by:
Non-metrical prose form of the enumerative kind,
Occurrence of lines of feet fewer than four,
Reduced number of syllables in the last of a line,
Occurrence of single-syllabled foot in a line,
And a word standing for a foot.

title: Ankatam
transliteration:
aṅkatamtāṉē aril tapat teriyiṉ
cemporuḷ karantatu eṉa iru vakaittē.
translation:
Examined with discernment,
Añkatam (satire)
Stands classifiable into two:
Cemporul añkatam and palikarappu abkatam*.

transliteration: cemporuḷ āyiṉa vacai eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
Cemporuļ añkatam is
Vacai (open, undisguised lampoon).

transliteration: moḻi karantu moḻiyiṉ atu paḻikarappu ākum.
translation:
Paļikarappu añkatam is
Veiled rebuke.

title: Modes of Composition
transliteration: ceyyuḷtāmē iraṇṭu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
A composition
[In terms of its subject matter]
Falls into two classes*.

transliteration:
tukaḷoṭum poruḷoṭum puṇarntaṉṟu āyiṉ
ceviyuṟaic ceyyuḷ eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Of the two above [1379],
One is ceviyuraic ceyyul
That treats of
Pointing one's failing
And bringing ‘one on to the path of virtue.

transliteration:
vacaiyoṭum nacaiyoṭum puṇarntaṉṟu āyiṉ
aṅkatac ceyyuḷ eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
The second class of composition is [1379]
Aħñkatac ceyyul
That embodies
Undisguised lampoon and veiled rebuke.

title: Kinds of Kalippa
transliteration:
ottāḻicaikkali kaliveṇpāṭṭē
koccakam uṟaḻoṭu kali nāl vakaittē.
translation:
Kalippā is of four kinds:
Ottalicaikkali, kaliveņpattu
Koccakakkali and uralkali*.

transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
ottāḻicaikkali iru vakaittu ākum.
translation:
Of them [1382],
Ottālicaikkali is further divided into two.

transliteration:
iṭainilaippāṭṭē taravu pōkku aṭai eṉa
naṭai naviṉṟu oḻukum oṉṟu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
One of these two [1383]
Has ifainilaippattu (talicai),
Taravu, pōkku (curitakam)
And afai (taniccol)
For its constituents.

transliteration:
taravētāṉum nāl aṭi iḻipu āy
āṟu iraṇṭu uyarvum piṟavum peṟumē.
translation:
Taravu above [1384] has
Four lines for the minimum
And twelve lines as the upper limit.

transliteration:
iṭainilaippāṭṭē,
taravu akappaṭṭa marapiṉatu eṉpa.
translation:
Itainilaip pattu [tāļicai] comprises lines
That are fewer in number
Than the four-line minimum of taravu [1385],
So has it been said.

transliteration:
aṭai nilaik kiḷavi tāḻicaip piṉṉar
naṭai naviṉṟu oḻukum āṅku eṉ kiḷavi.
translation:
Atțainilaikkiļavi [taņpiccol]
There occurs after tälicai
As ottalicaikkali's constituent [1384].

transliteration:
pōkku iyal vakaiyē vaippu eṉappaṭumē
taravu iyal ottum ataṉ akappaṭumē
purai tīr iṟuti nilai uraittaṉṟē.

ēṉai oṉṟē,
tēvarp parāaya muṉṉilaikkaṇṇē.
translation:
The other kind of ottäļicaikkali [1383] is
Extolling of the gods in the second person.

transliteration:
atuvē,
vaṇṇakam orupōku eṉa iru vakaittē.
translation:
This kind [1389]
Has two types:
Vaņnņakam and orupōku.
Vaņnņnaka Ottāļjicaikkali

transliteration:
vaṇṇakamtāṉē,
taravē tāḻicai eṇṇē vāram eṉṟu
an nāl vakaiyiṉ tōṉṟum eṉpa.
translation:
Of these two [1390],
Vaņņakam comprises four limbs:
Taravu, tàlicai, ep [ampōtaraņkam] and vāram [curitakam].

transliteration:
taravētāṉum,
nāṉkum āṟum eṭṭum eṉṟa
nēraṭi paṟṟiya nilaimaittu ākum.
translation:
The taravu above [1391]
Has four, six or eight four-footed lines.

transliteration:
ottu mūṉṟu ākum ottāḻicaiyē

translation:
The tälļicai of vaņņakam [1391]
Has three stanzas of equal number of feet,
And they have in each fewer lines than that of taravu.

transliteration: aṭakku iyal vāram taravoṭu okkum.
translation:
Atakkiyal [curitakam]
That rounds up the vaņņnakam stanza [1391]
Is structured in the manner of faravu.

transliteration: mutal toṭai perukic curuṅkumaṉ eṇṇē.
translation:
Such is the structure of the en [ampõtarakam] limb [1391]
That its lines mark gradual diminishing.

transliteration:
eṇ iṭai oḻital ētam iṉṟē
ciṉṉam allāk kālaiyāṉa.
translation:
That there marks the absence of en [1391]
Is no inadequacy of note,
Provided there occurs no detached word [tanicco]].

transliteration: orupōku iyaṟkaiyum iru vakaittu ākum.
translation:
The orupōku type of kalippā [1390]
Falls into two sub-classes too.

transliteration:
koccaka orupōku ampōtaraṅkam eṉṟu
oppa nāṭi uṇartal vēṇṭum.
translation:
These sub-classes are,
As the discerning minds see,
Koccaka orupōku and ampōtarańka orupōku.
Koccaka Orupōku

transliteration:

tāḻicai iṉṟit taravu uṭaittu ākiyum

aṭakkiyal iṉṟi aṭi nimirntu oḻukiyum

orupāṉ ciṟumai iraṭṭi ataṉ uyarpē.
translation:
Koccaka orupōku is composed of lines
Ranging from ten to twenty.
Ampõōtaraika Orupōku

transliteration:

translation:
The other sub-class ampõtarañka orupōku
Takes sixty lines for its farthest limit,
With a quarter of this number being its minimum.*

translation:
The limbs of ampõōtarañka orupōku are:
Eruttu [taravu], koccakam, arākam,
Cirreņ and vâram [curitakam].
Kaliveņpattu

translation:
A unified subject matter
Structured in the vellati [a distinctive veņnpā] metre,
With no variations therein,
Marks kaliveņ pattu.

title: Koccakakkali
transliteration:
taravum pōkkum pāṭṭu iṭai miṭaintum

Wherein are kindred things structured in harmony
In the manner of gems of the same species

By men of ripe learning.

Find pintam a unified whole

Brief explicatory notes interspersed among verse lines,
Non-metrical lines in a verse,
Utterances of alien fictional import,
And kindred texts marked with ridicule and laughter.

Find no restriction of the addresser.

translation:
Words of wisdom [such as proverbs] are those
That stand to illustrate a proposition
Through a language of evocation
That is subtle, terse, perspicuous and artless,
So has it been held.

That are born of the minds of sage men
And that stand pregnant with having their effect.
