Medial consonants dominating,
Iyaipu vaņņam is accomplished therein.

transliteration: aḷapeṭai vaṇṇam aḷapeṭai payilum.
translation:
Where there marks
Preponderance of elongation [vocalic and consonantal],
It is ajapetai vaņņam.

transliteration: neṭuñcīr vaṇṇam neṭṭeḻuttup payilum.
translation:
Long letters being close together,
There occasions nefuñcir vanņņam.

transliteration: kuṟuñcīr vaṇṇam kuṟṟeḻuttup payilum.
translation:
Short letters reigning in numbers,
There occurs kuruñcir vaņņam.

transliteration:
cittira vaṇṇam
neṭiyavum kuṟiyavum nērntu uṭaṉ varumē.
translation:
Where there are
Short and long letters in harmony,
Cittira vaņņam is in place there.

transliteration: nalipu vaṇṇam āytam payilum.
translation:
Nalipu vaņņam goes with
The use of the zytam letter.

transliteration:
akappāṭṭu vaṇṇam
muṭiyāt taṉmaiyiṉ muṭintataṉ mēṟṟē.
translation:
Structuring the rhythm of the text
With a sense of apparent incompleteness
While in reality it is through
Is akappāttu vaņņam.

transliteration:
puṟappāṭṭu vaṇṇam
muṭintatu pōṉṟu muṭiyātākum.
translation:
Purappāattu vaņņam is
Investing the text with rhythm
In such a way
That it sounds complete
While in reality it is not so.

transliteration: oḻuku vaṇṇam ōcaiyiṉ oḻukum.
translation:
The rhythm
That flows evenly through
Is oļuku vaņņam.

transliteration: orūu vaṇṇam orīit toṭukkum.
translation:
Orūu vaņņam is that
Where the rhythm flows
Steering clear of
The features of sound metrically wrought.

transliteration: eṇṇu vaṇṇam eṇṇup payilum.
translation:
Enņnņu vaņnņam is realized
Where the structure marks
The enumerative-additive mode.

transliteration: akaippu vaṇṇam aṟuttu aṟuttu oḻukum.
translation:
Breaks in the harmony of a rhythm
Effected through an intervening
Makes for akaippu vaņnņam.

transliteration: tūṅkal vaṇṇam vañci payilum.
translation:
The three-syllabled metrical feet proper to vañcippā
Endows a stanza with tunka! vaņņam.

transliteration:
ēntal vaṇṇam
colliya colliṉ colliyatu ciṟakkum.
translation:
The rhythm accomplished,
When the repetition of choice diction
Entails distinction of the sense intended,
Is called ental vaņņam.

transliteration: uruṭṭu vaṇṇam arākam toṭukkum.
translation:
A succession of short syllables
Rapidly repeated in a four-footed line,
As free rolling on,
Makes for uruttu vaņnam.

transliteration:
muṭuku vaṇṇam
aṭi iṟantu ōṭi ataṉ ōraṟṟē.
translation:
Muțuku vaņņam is
Rapid flow of short syllables in succession
[As in uruttu vaņnņamj]
In a line of feet exceeding four.

transliteration: vaṇṇamtāmē ivai eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The ones treated above [1462-81]
Are kinds of verse rhythm proper [vaņņam],
So has it been ruled.
Vaņnappu

transliteration:
vaṉappu iyaltāṉē vakukkum kālai
cil meṉ moḻiyāṉ tāya paṉuvaliṉ
ammaitāṉē aṭi nimirvu iṉṟē.
translation:
The eight aspects
That ensure a work's elegance [vanappuj]
Examined —
Harmonious succession of mellifluent words,
Fewer in number,
In lines of verse of extended length
Is what is known as ammai.

title: Alaku
transliteration:
ceyyuḷ moḻiyāṉ cīr puṉaintu yāppiṉ
av vakaitāṉē aḻaku eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
Alaku is
Choice poetic diction
Wrought in tuneful metrical lines.

title: Tonmai
transliteration:
toṉmaitāṉē
uraiyoṭu puṇarnta yāppiṉ mēṟṟē.
translation:
Tonņnmai is
Antique thematic source
Treated with
Non-verse elucidations in between.

transliteration:
iḻumeṉ moḻiyāṉ viḻumiyatu nuvaliṉum
paranta moḻiyāṉ aṭi nimirntu oḻukiṉum
tōl eṉa moḻipa tol moḻip pulavar.
translation:
Learned men versed in antique usage say that
Tō! is themes of sublime import
Treated through mellifluous diction,
Or it is of themes expounded
In lines of extended length.

title: Viruntu
transliteration:
viruntētāṉum
putuvatu puṉainta yāppiṉ mēṟṟē.
translation:
Compositions,
With modes and techniques untrodden marked,
Are viruntu.

title: Iyaipu
transliteration:
ñakārai mutalā ḷakārai īṟṟup
puḷḷi iṟuti iyaipu eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
Verses informed by iyaipu are those
That have the consonantal endings
From ñ to p [ñ, n, n, m, n, y, 1, |, v, 1 and |].

title: Pullan
transliteration:
cēri moḻiyāṉ cevvitiṉ kiḷantu
tērtal vēṇṭātu kuṟittatu tōṉṟiṉ
pulaṉ eṉa moḻipa pulaṉ uṇarntōrē.
translation:
Compositions in the popular tongue
That lend to easy comprehension
With no discernment of the mind needed
Are of the pulan kind,
Thus do the learned rule.

title: Ilaipu
transliteration:
oṟṟoṭu puṇarnta valleḻuttu aṭaṅkātu
kuṟaḷaṭi mutalā aintu aṭi oppittu
ōṅkiya moḻiyāṉ āṅku avaṇ moḻiyiṉ
iḻaipiṉ ilakkaṇam iyaintatākum.
translation:
Steering clear of hard consonants [k, ¢, t, t, p, r]
Occurrence of all the five kinds of metrical lines
[kuraļatți, cintați, aļavați, nețilați and kalinetțilatți);
Such is the defining trait of ilaipu.

title: Poetic Norms and Worldly Conventions
transliteration:
ceyyuḷ maruṅkiṉ mey peṟa nāṭi
iḻaitta ilakkaṇam piḻaittaṉa pōla
varuva uḷa eṉiṉum vantavaṟṟu iyalāṉ
tiripu iṉṟi muṭittal teḷḷiyōr kaṭaṉē.
translation:
It is the charge of the discerning men
To study the norms of composition herein said,
And to see those of the norms,
Which might look deviantly formulated,
Brought to order
In accord with the ruling context set.

title: Offspring Designations
transliteration:
māṟṟa aruñ ciṟappiṉ marapu iyal kiḷappiṉ
pārppum paṟaḻum kuṭṭiyum kuruḷaiyum
kaṉṟum piḷḷaiyum makavum maṟiyum eṉṟu
oṉpatum kuḻaviyoṭu iḷamaip peyarē.
translation:
By the great tradition unalterable,
The nine terms parppu, paral, kutti, kuruļai,
kanzu, pilļai, makavu, mari and kulavi
Stand to designate the offsprings
Of the human and animal species.

title: Nouns Denoting Masculine Gender
transliteration:
ēṟum ēṟṟaiyum oruttalum kaḷiṟum
cēvum cēvalum iralaiyum kalaiyum
mōttaiyum takarum utaḷum apparum
pōttum kaṇṭiyum kaṭuvaṉum piṟavum
yātta āṇpāṟ peyar eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
The nouns marking masculine gender by convention are:
Ēru, ērrai, oruttal, kaliru, cë,
Cēval, iralai, kalai, mōttai, takar,
Uta], appar, pōttu, kaņti, katuvan
And others of their kind.

title: Nouns Denoting Feminine Gender
transliteration:
pēṭaiyum peṭaiyum peṭṭaiyum peṇṇum
mūṭum nākum kaṭamaiyum aḷakum
mantiyum pāṭṭiyum piṇaiyum piṇavum
antam cāṉṟa piṭiyoṭu peṇṇē.
translation:
And those that indicate feminine gender are:
Pētțai, petai, pettai, peņ, mūtu,
Naku, kațamai, aļaku, manti, pātti,
Piņai, piņavu and piti.

title: Offsprings of Animal Species
transliteration:
avaṟṟuḷ,
pārppum piḷḷaiyum paṟappavaṟṟu iḷamai.
translation:
Among the nouns designating off springs,
Paārppu and pillai are the young ones of birds.

transliteration: tavaḻpavaitāmum avaṟṟu ōraṉṉa.
translation:
These two terms [1495] designate the young ones
Of the creatures that crawl too.

transliteration:
mūṅkā veruku eli mūvari aṇiloṭu
āṅku avai nāṉkum kuṭṭikku uriya.
translation:
Kutti is the offspring designation of
Mangoose, wild cat, rat and three-striped squirrel.

transliteration: paṟaḻ eṉappaṭiṉum uṟaḻ āṇṭu illai.
translation:
No inaccuracy there entails
If the offsprings of these four [1497]
Are called paral too.

transliteration:
nāyē paṉṟi puli muyal nāṉkum
āyum kālai kuruḷai eṉpa.
translation:
Kuruļai is the offspring name of the four:
Dog, pig, tiger and hare. |

transliteration: nariyum aṟṟē nāṭiṉar koḷiṉē.
translation: Kurulai is the offspring of the fox too.

transliteration: kuṭṭiyum paṟaḻum kūṟṟu avaṇ varaiyār.
translation:
To call kurulai above [1499-1500]
By the terms kutti and paral
Is not disallowed too.

transliteration:
piḷḷaip peyarum piḻaippu āṇṭu illai
koḷḷum kālai nāy alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
To call the young ones of these animals pilai,
Save that of the dog,
Is not inappropriate.

transliteration:
yāṭum kutiraiyum navviyum uḻaiyum
ōṭum pulvāy uḷappaṭa maṟiyē.
translation:
Mari is the designation of offsprings
Of sheep, horse, spotted deer, and deer and antelope.

transliteration: kōṭu vāḻ kuraṅkum kuṭṭi kūṟupa.
translation:
Kuttți is the young one of the monkey,
That has the boughs of trees for its home.

transliteration:
makavum piḷḷaiyum paṟaḻum pārppum
avaiyum aṉṉa ap pālāṉa.
translation:
Makavu, pilļai, paral and pārppu
Are also the offspring designations of the monkey.

transliteration:
yāṉaiyum kutiraiyum kaḻutaiyum kaṭamaiyum
māṉoṭu aintum kaṉṟu eṉaṟku uriya.
translation:
Kanu is the young one of the five:
Elephant, horse, donkey, elk and cow.

transliteration: erumaiyum maraiyum varaiyār āṇṭē.
translation:
That the young ones of buffalo and wild cow
Are also called by the name kanru
Is no lack of propriety therein.

transliteration: kavariyum karāmum nikar avaṟṟuḷḷē.
translation:
The offsprings of yak(kavari) and alligator
Are similarly called (kaņnru) too.

transliteration: oṭṭakam avaṟṟoṭu oru vaḻi nilaiyum.
translation:
So is the young one of the camel too
[Designated by the term kanu).

transliteration: kuñcaram peṟumē kuḻavip peyarkkoṭai.
translation:
The offspring designation of the elephant
Is kulavi.

transliteration: āvum erumaiyum atu colappaṭumē.
translation:
Kulavi denotes the young ones
Of the cow and the buffalo too.

transliteration: kaṭamaiyum maraiyum mutal nilai oṉṟum.
translation:
The elk and the wild cow
Have their offspring designated by the term kulavi.

transliteration:
kuraṅkum mucuvum ūkamum mūṉṟum
nirampa nāṭiṉ ap peyarkku uriya.
translation:
Examined with care,
Kuļavi is the offspring
Of the monkey, langur and black monkey also.

title: Human Offsprings
transliteration:
kuḻaviyum makavum āyiraṇṭu allavai
kiḻava alla makkaṭkaṇṇē.
translation:
No other terms
Save kulavi and makavu
Go with the human offspring.

title: Offsprings of One Sense Faculty
transliteration:
piḷḷai kuḻavi kaṉṟē pōttu eṉak
koḷḷavum amaiyum ōr aṟivu uyirkkē.
translation:
Pillai, kuļlavi, kaņru and pōttu
Designate the young of the organisms
Endowed with one sense faculty too.

transliteration: nellum pullum nērār āṇṭē.
translation:
These four terms [1515]
Go not with the seedlings of paddy and grass.

transliteration:
colliya marapiṉ iḷamaitāṉē
collum kālai avai ala ilavē.
translation:
Save these terms in use and vogue,
No other words designate the offspring known.

title: Distinctions of Sense Organisms
transliteration:
oṉṟu aṟivatuvē uṟṟu aṟivatuvē
iraṇṭu aṟivatuvē ataṉoṭu nāvē
mūṉṟu aṟivatuvē avaṟṟoṭu mūkkē
nāṉku aṟivatuvē avaṟṟoṭu kaṇṇē
aintu aṟivatuvē avaṟṟoṭu ceviyē
āṟu aṟivatuvē avaṟṟoṭu maṉaṉē
nēritiṉ uṇarntōr neṟippaṭuttiṉarē.

title: One Sense Organisms
transliteration:
pullum maraṉum ōr aṟiviṉavē
piṟavum uḷavē ak kiḷaip piṟappē.

title: Two Sense Organisms
transliteration:
nantum muraḷum īr aṟiviṉavē
piṟavum uḷavē akkiḷaip piṟappē.
translation:
The snail and shell-fish are two-sense organisms;
Others of their species there are too.

title: Three Sense Organisms
transliteration:
citalum eṟumpum mū aṟiviṉavē
piṟavum uḷavē ak kiḷaip piṟappē.
translation:
The termite and ant are three-sense organisms;
There are others of their kind confined to these faculties.

title: Four Sense Organisms
transliteration:
naṇṭum tumpiyum nāṉku aṟiviṉavē
piṟavum uḷavē ak kiḷaip piṟappē.
translation:
The crabs and beetles are four-sense organisms;
Others of their species there are too.

title: Five Sense Organisms
transliteration:
māvum mākkaḷum ai aṟiviṉavē
piṟavum uḷavē ak kiḷaip piṟappē.

title: Six Sense Organisms
transliteration:
makkaḷtāmē āṟu aṟivu uyirē
piṟavum uḷavē ak kiḷaip piṟappē.
translation:
The humans have six senses;
There are others too endowed with six senses.

transliteration: oru cār vilaṅkum uḷa eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Certain species of animals
Are said to have the sixth sense too.

title: Male Designations
transliteration: vēḻakku urittē vitantu kaḷiṟu eṉṟal.
translation: The male of the elephant is kaļiru.

transliteration: kēḻaṟkaṇṇum kaṭi varai iṉṟē.
translation:
Kaļiru denoting the male pig
Is not disallowed too.

transliteration:
pulvāy puli uḻai maraiyē kavari
colliya karāmoṭu oruttal oṉṟum.
translation:
The term oruttal designates the male
Of the antelope, tiger, deer, wild cow, yak and alligator.

transliteration: vār kōṭṭu yāṉaiyum paṉṟiyum aṉṉa.
translation:
The male of long-tusked elephant, and boar
Is similarly called oruttal.

transliteration: ēṟpuṭaittu eṉpa erumaikkaṇṇum.
translation: Oruttal represents the male buffalo too.

transliteration:
paṉṟi pulvāy uḻaiyē kavari
eṉṟu ivai nāṉkum ēṟu eṉaṟku uriya.
translation:
The male of the pig, antelope, deer and yak
Is called êru.

transliteration: erumaiyum maraiyum peṟṟamum aṉṉa.
translation:
The male of buffalo, wild cow and cow
Is called êru too.

transliteration: kaṭal vāḻ cuṟavum ēṟu eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
The shark living in the sea too
Has its male designated by the term @ëru.

transliteration:
peṟṟam erumai puli marai pulvāy
maṟṟu ivai ellām pōttu eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
Põöttu denotes the male species
Of cow, buffalo, tiger, wild cow and antelope.

transliteration: nīr vāḻ cātiyum atu peṟaṟku uriya.
translation:
Põttu is the masculine gender
Denoting the male species of the acquatic animals.

transliteration: mayilum eḻālum payilat tōṉṟum.
translation:
Pòōttu is the masculine gender term
Denoting the male of the peacock and the elal bird too.

transliteration: iralaiyum kalaiyum pulvāykku uriya.
translation:
Iralai and kalai are the masculine forms
Of the antelope.

transliteration:
kalai eṉ kāṭci uḻaikkum urittē
nilaiyiṟṟu ap peyar mucuviṉkaṇṇum.
translation:
Kalai is the male of the deer too;
Kalai is also the male of the langur.

transliteration:
mōttaiyum takarum utaḷum apparum
yātta eṉpa yāṭṭiṉkaṇṇē.
translation:
Mõōttai, takar, utaļ and appar
Designate the male sheep.

transliteration:
cēval peyarkkoṭai ciṟakoṭu civaṇum
mā irun tūvi mayil alaṅkaṭaiyē.
translation:
Save the large-feathered peacock,
All birds have their male
Denoted by the term ceēval.

transliteration:
āṟṟaloṭu puṇarnta āṇpāṟku ellām
ēṟṟaik kiḷavi urittu eṉa moḻipa.
translation:
Ērrai is the term appropriate
By which to specify the male species
That manifest daring, tenacity and prowess.

transliteration:
āṇpāl ellām āṇ eṉaṟku uriya
peṇpāl ellām peṇ eṉaṟku uriya
kāṇpa avai avai appālāṉa.
piṭi eṉ peṇ peyar yāṉai mēṟṟē.
translation: Piti represents the female species of the elephant.

transliteration:
oṭṭakam kutirai kaḻutai marai ivai
peṭṭai eṉṉum peyarkkoṭaikku uriya.
translation:
Pettai is the female proper
Of the camel, horse, donkey and wilá cow.

transliteration: puḷḷum uriya ap peyarkku eṉpa.
translation:
The female species of the birds too
Take pettai for their designation.

transliteration: pēṭaiyum peṭaiyum nāṭiṉ oṉṟum.
translation:
Pēțai and petšai,
As does pettai,
Denote the birds’ female species.

transliteration:
kōḻi kūkai āyiraṇṭu allavai
cūḻum kālai aḷaku eṉal amaiyā.
translation:
Alaku does not indicate the birds' female species
Save the hen and owl.

transliteration: ap peyark kiḻamai mayiṟkum urittē.
translation: Alaku denotes the peahen too.

transliteration:
pulvāy navvi uḻaiyē kavari
colvāy nāṭiṉ piṇai eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
Piņai marks the female
Of the antelope, spotted deer, deer and yak.

transliteration:
paṉṟi pulvāy nāy eṉa mūṉṟum
oṉṟiya eṉpa piṇaviṉ peyarkkoṭai.
translation:
The term piņavu stands fitting
To the female of the pig, antelope and dog.

transliteration: piṇaval eṉiṉum avaṟṟiṉ mēṟṟē.
translation:
The female of the three above [1550]
Is known by the term piņaval too.

transliteration: peṟṟamum erumaiyum maraiyum āvē.
translation:
Å designates the feminine gender
Of the cow, buffalo and wild cow.

transliteration: peṇṇum piṇāvum makkaṭku uriya.
translation:
Pen and piņa represent the feminine gender
Of the human species proper.

transliteration: erumaiyum maraiyum peṟṟamum nākē.
translation:
Naku is the female
Of the buffalo, wild cow and bull.

transliteration: nīr vāḻ cātiyuḷ nantum nākē.
translation:
Naku also represents the female
Of the snail among the aquatic creatures.

transliteration: mūṭum kaṭamaiyum yāṭu ala peṟāa.
translation:
Müūtu and kațamai
Are the female of none but the sheep.

transliteration: pāṭṭi eṉpa paṉṟiyum nāyum.
translation:
The female of the pig and dog
Is called pāttií.

transliteration: nariyum aṟṟē nāṭiṉar koḷiṉē.
translation:
Patti is the term
That designates the female fox too.

transliteration: kuraṅkum mucuvum ūkamum manti.
translation:
Manti is the female
Of the monkey, langur and black monkey.

transliteration:
kuraṅkiṉ ēṟṟiṉaik kaṭuvaṉ eṉṟalum
maram payil kūkaiyaik kōṭṭāṉ eṉṟalum
cev vāyk kiḷiyait tattai eṉṟalum
vev vāy verukiṉaip pūcai eṉṟalum
kutiraiyuḷ āṇiṉaic cēval eṉṟalum
iruḷ niṟap paṉṟiyai ēṉam eṉṟalum
erumaiyuḷ āṇiṉaik kaṇṭi eṉṟalum
muṭiya vanta av vaḻakku uṇmaiyiṉ
kaṭiyal ākā kaṭaṉ aṟintōrkkē.
translation:
That
The male of the monkey is called katuvan,
The owl resident on trees is called köttānņ,
The red-mouthed parrot is called tattai,
The fierce-looking wild cat is called pūcai,
The male of the horse is called cëval,
The dark-hued pig is called ēņam,
And the male of the buffalo is called kaņti
Being part of the usage alive and living,
They cannot be kept off as inappropriate
So do the literate rooted in tradition hold.

transliteration: peṇṇum āṇum piḷḷaiyum avaiyē.
translation:
Such are the conventions [1492 1560]
That govern the designations
Of male and female creatures
And their offspring as well.

title: Possessions of the Brahmins
transliteration:
nūlē karakam mukkōl maṇaiyē
āyum kālai antaṇarkku uriya.
translation:
The sacred thread, pitchers in hoops,
The trident staff and low wooden seat
Are possessions proper to the brahmins.

title: Symbols of Sovereignty
transliteration:
paṭaiyum koṭiyum kuṭaiyum muracum
naṭai navil puraviyum kaḷiṟum tērum
tārum muṭiyum nērvaṉa piṟavum
terivu koḷ ceṅkōl aracarkku uriya.
translation:
The monarchs wielding the just sceptre
Do hold as symbols of sovereignty
Army, royal banner, umbrella,
Drum, swift horse, elephant, chariot,
Garland, crown and such of these.

transliteration:
antaṇāḷarkku uriyavum aracarkku
oṉṟiya varūum poruḷumār uḷavē.
translation:
Such of those things
As going with the brahmins
Come to stand for the rulers too.

transliteration:
paricil pāṭāṇ tiṇait tuṟaik kiḻamaippeyar
neṭuntakai cemmal eṉṟu ivai piṟavum
poruntac collutal avarkku urittaṉṟē.
translation:
Being entreated for gifts,
Being the subject of praise,
Taking appellations
By the ruling tracts of land and features thereon,
And being honoured with titles of attribution
Such as the noble one and the one of spotless virtues —
Are proper to the king but not to the brahmins.

title: Naming of People
transliteration:
ūrum peyarum uṭaittoḻiṟ karuviyum
yārum cārtti avai avai peṟumē.
translation:
The classes of folks are seen
In relation to their places of habitation,
Proper names and given names
And to the instruments of their occupations.

title: Titles of Honour
transliteration:
talaimaik kuṇac colum tamtamakku uriya
nilaimaikku ēṟpa nikaḻttupa eṉpa.
translation:
The titles of honour and eminence folks
Are all in accord with their standing rank.

title: Claims of Kings and Traders
transliteration:
iṭai iru vakaiyōr allatu nāṭiṉ
paṭai vakai peṟāar eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
None but the middle two among the social classes
[The kings and the tradesfolk]
Have the claim to the use of weapons of prowess,
So has it been held.

transliteration: vaicikaṉ peṟumē vāṇika vāḻkkai.
translation:
Vaicikan class draw their living
On the occupation of trade.

transliteration:
mey teri vakaiyiṉ eṇ vakai uṇaviṉ
ceytiyum varaiyār ap pālāṉa.
translation:
Producing the eight kinds of staple food
[Paddy, horsegram, common millet, maize,
Little millet, blackgram, bengalgram and bean]
Is not forbidden to the tradesfolk.

transliteration: kaṇṇiyum tārum eṇṇiṉar āṇṭē.
translation:
The honour of wearing wreaths and garlands too
The tradesmen have a claim to.

title: Farming Class
transliteration:
vēḷāṇ māntarkku uḻutūṇ allatu
il eṉa moḻipa piṟa vakai nikaḻcci.
translation:
The vējaļar class take to no occupation
But farming and cultivation.

transliteration:
vēntu viṭu toḻiliṉ paṭaiyum kaṇṇiyum
vāyntaṉar eṉpa avar peṟum poruḷē.
translation:
Weapons of war and wreaths to wear
The vēļālar have access to
As they go on missions of the state.

title: Brahmins
transliteration: antaṇāḷarkku aracu varaivu iṉṟē.
translation:
The brahmins do not stand removed from
The claim to rulership.

title: Ruling Chieftains
transliteration:
villum vēlum kaḻalum kaṇṇiyum
tārum mālaiyum tērum māvum
maṉ peṟu marapiṉ ēṉōrkkum uriya.
translation:
The others [ruling chieftains] have claim to
Bow, spear, anklet, wreath,
Garland, neck ornaments, chariot and horse.

transliteration: aṉṉar āyiṉum iḻintōrkku illai.
translation:
Fall in standing witnessed
The chieftains above [1575]
Are not entitled to the possessions said.

title: Exogenous and Endogenous Species
transliteration: puṟak kāḻaṉavē pul eṉa moḻipa.
akak kāḻaṉavē maram eṉa moḻipa.
warnings: printed as one sutra with the previous one (shared translation)

transliteration:
tōṭē maṭalē ōlai eṉṟā
ēṭē itaḻē pāḷai eṉṟā
īrkkē kulai eṉa nērntaṉa piṟavum
pulloṭu varum eṉac colliṉar pulavar.
translation:
The limbs of the exogenous grass species are:
Sheath, tagged stem, (palm) leaf, strip of leaf,
Petal, spathe, rib of the leaf, cluster of fruits
And such of these,
So do the learned find.

transliteration:
ilaiyē taḷirē muṟiyē tōṭē
ciṉaiyē kuḻaiyē pūvē arumpē
naṉai uḷḷuṟutta aṉaiyavai ellām
maraṉoṭu varūum kiḷavi eṉpa.
translation:
The limbs of the endogenous plants are:
Leaf, tender leaf, sprout, sheath, bough,
Shoot, flower, bud, inner bud
And such of these.

transliteration:
kāyē paḻamē tōlē cetiḷē
vīḻoṭu eṉṟu āṅku avaiyum aṉṉa.
translation:
The limbs common to both the species [1577] are:
Unripe fruit, fruit, inner rind, bark and aerial root.

title: A Linguistic Convention
transliteration:
nilam tī nīr vaḷi vicumpoṭu aintum
kalanta mayakkam ulakam ātaliṉ
iru tiṇai aim pāl iyal neṟi vaḻāamait
tirivu il colloṭu taḻāal vēṇṭum.
translation:
A structured blend of
Earth, fire, water, air and space
As the world is,
The use words are made of
Must be undistorted
Undeviating from the norms
That go with the classifications of
The human - non-human generic distinction,
And the five genders thereof.

title: Nature of Literary Usage
transliteration:
marapunilai tirital ceyyuṭku illai
marapu vaḻip paṭṭa colliṉāṉē.
translation:
Compositions admit of
No violation of the conventions in vogue;
Use of diction tested through tradition
Should inform the usage therein.

transliteration: marapunilai tiriyiṉ piṟitu piṟitu ākum.
translation:
Where deviations occur thereof [1582],
There entail variations in sense.

transliteration:
vaḻakku eṉappaṭuvatu uyarntōr mēṟṟē
nikaḻcci avar kaṭṭu ākalāṉa.
translation:
Usage is
What is in vogue and use
Among the literate,
From whom issue
The events of popular speech.

title: Primary and Secondary Works
transliteration:
marapunilai tiriyā māṭciya āki
urai paṭu nūltām iru vakai iyala
mutalum vaḻiyum eṉa nutaliya neṟiyiṉa.
translation:
Compositions,
That do not infringe the norms of tradition,
Fall into two classes:
Original or primary works,
And secondary works or adaptations.

transliteration:
viṉaiyiṉ nīṅki viḷaṅkiya aṟiviṉ
muṉaivaṉ kaṇṭatu mutal nūl ākum.
translation:
Primary or original works
Are those compositions
By men of sage wisdom
Whose consummate faculties stand unsullied
By the mire of turpitude.

transliteration: vaḻi eṉappaṭuvatu ataṉ vaḻittu ākum.
translation:
Secondary works or adaptations
Derive from or depend on the primary works.

transliteration: vaḻiyiṉ neṟiyē nāl vakaittu ākum.
translation: Secondary works comprise four modes.

title: Modes of Composition of Secondary Works
transliteration:
tokuttal virittal tokaiviri moḻipeyarttu
atarppaṭa yāttaloṭu aṉai marapiṉavē.
translation:
These four modes [1588] are:
Summarization, elaboration,
Synthesis of summarization and elaboration
And translation in conformity with the tradition of the receptor tongue.
Nüūl

transliteration:
otta cūttiram uraippiṉ kāṇṭikai
meyppaṭak kiḷanta vakaiyatu āki
īr aiṅ kuṟṟamum iṉṟi nēritiṉ
muppattiru vakai uttiyoṭu puṇariṉ
nūl eṉa moḻipa nuṇaṅku moḻip pulavar.
translation:
That whose aphoristic structure
Lends to expositions proper and right,
That steers clear of the ten kinds of defects [1600];
And that embodies the thirty-two structural devices [1602] —
Is what the erudite scholars call a nū! (treatise).

title: Urai
transliteration:
urai eṭuttu ataṉ muṉ yāppiṉum cūttiram
purai tapa uṭaṉpaṭak kāṇṭikai puṇarppiṉum
vitittalum vilakkalum eṉa iru vakaiyoṭu
purai tapa nāṭip puṇarkkavum paṭumē.
translation:
It is in order right for a composition that
Notes of commentary are added,
Expository remarks flawless go thereon,
And prescriptive observations and refutatory critique are appended
All marked with clarity and insight.
Cüttiram

transliteration:
mēṟ kiḷanteṭutta yāppiṉuḷ poruḷoṭu
cil vakai eḻuttiṉ ceyyuṭku āki
collum kālai urai akattu aṭakki
nuṇmaiyoṭu puṇarnta oṇmaittu āki
tuḷakkal ākāt tuṇaimai eyti
aḷakkal ākā arum poruṭṭu āki
pala vakaiyāṉum payaṉ teripu uṭaiyatu
cūttirattu iyalpu eṉa yāttaṉar pulavar.

paḻippu il cūttiram paṭṭa paṇpiṉ
karappu iṉṟi muṭivatu kāṇṭikai ākum.
translation:
Kanņtikai, a mode of commentary,
Is an exposition brief and explicit
Of the well-structured aphoristic text [cuttiram}).

transliteration:
viṭṭu akalvu iṉṟi virivoṭu porunti
cuṭṭiya cūttiram muṭittaṟ poruṭṭā
ētu naṭaiyiṉum eṭuttukkāṭṭiṉum
mēvāṅku amainta meyn neṟittu atuvē.
translation:
The structure of kantikai above said is such that
It does not go beyond the perspective of the text,
It brings in details for the elucidation of the text;
And it is marked by causal explanations and illustrations
For the comprehension of the meaning intended.

title: Urai
transliteration:
cūttirattuṭ poruḷ aṉṟiyum yāppuṟa
iṉṟiyamaiyātu iyaipavai ellām
oṉṟa uraippatu urai eṉappaṭumē.
translation:
Urai, the elaborate commentary,
Unfolding the import of the text apart,
Synthesizes details all and sundry
That come indispensable
To the comprehension of the text's meaning.

transliteration:
maṟutalaik kaṭāa māṟṟamum uṭaittāy
taṉ nūlāṉum muṭinta nūlāṉum
aiyamum maruṭkaiyum cevvitiṉ nīkki
teṟṟeṉa oru poruḷ oṟṟumai koḷīi
tuṇivoṭu niṟṟal eṉmaṉār pulavar.
translation:
Furthermore,
Urai stands authentic as critique
Providing answers to the questions raised on the text,
Clarifying doubts and obscurities that inhere in the text
Through elucidations of its own,
And by references to other works relevant,
Arriving at a definitive interpretation thereon,
So have the learned ruled.

title: Inadequacy of a Composition
transliteration:
collappaṭṭaṉa ellā māṇpum
maṟutalai āyiṉum maṟṟu atu citaivē.
translation:
A work turns flawed and inadequate
Where it goes unmarked
By the above characteristics one and all.

transliteration: citaivu il eṉpa mutalvaṉ kaṇṇē.
translation:
Primary works
Do not suffer this inadequacy [1597].

transliteration:
mutal vaḻi āyiṉum yāppiṉuḷ citaiyum
vallōṉ puṇarā vāram pōṉṟē.
translation:
Even where such a work [1598]
Draws on an original work
It remains defective
In the manner of the song
Sung in accompaniment by an untutored hand.

title: Defects in a Composition
transliteration:
citaivu eṉappaṭupavai vacai aṟa nāṭiṉ
kūṟiyatu kūṟal māṟu koḷak kūṟal
kuṉṟak kūṟal mikai paṭak kūṟal
poruḷ ila kūṟal mayaṅkak kūṟal
kēṭpōrkku iṉṉā yāppiṟṟu ātal
paḻitta moḻiyāṉ iḻukkam kūṟal
taṉṉāṉ oru poruḷ karutik kūṟal
eṉṉa vakaiyiṉum maṉam kōḷ iṉmai
aṉṉa piṟavum avaṟṟu viri ākum.
translation:
A study sharp-eyed
Points to defects that stain a composition:
Tautology, inconsistency, understatement,
Overstatement, verbiage, obscurity,
Cacophony, contemptible things in unworthy diction,
Persisting in one's own pet ideas,
Incomprehensibility of varied sorts
And failings that issue from these.

transliteration: etir maṟuttu uṇariṉ at tiṟattavum avaiyē.
translation:
Where an implication of inverse proposition
Issues from an assertion made,
That too is a fault in composition.

title: Utti (Devices in a Composition)
transliteration:
otta kāṭci utti vakai virippiṉ
nutaliyatu aṟital atikāra muṟaiyē
tokuttuk kūṟal vakuttu meyn niṟuttal
moḻinta poruḷoṭu oṉṟa vaittal
moḻiyātataṉai muṭṭu iṉṟi muṭittal
vārātataṉāṉ vantatu muṭittal
vantatu koṇṭu vārātatu uṇarttal
muntu moḻintataṉ talaitaṭumāṟṟē
oppak kūṟal orutalai moḻital
taṉ kōḷ kūṟal muṟai piṟaḻāmai
piṟaṉ uṭaṉpaṭṭatu tāṉ uṭampaṭutal
iṟantatu kāttal etiratu pōṟṟal
moḻivām eṉṟal kūṟiṟṟu eṉṟal
tāṉ kuṟiyiṭutal orutalai aṉmai
muṭintatu kāṭṭal āṇai kūṟal
pal poruṭku ēṟpiṉ nallatu kōṭal
tokutta moḻiyāṉ vakuttaṉar kōṭal
maṟutalai citaittut taṉ tuṇipu uraittal
piṟaṉ kōḷ kūṟal aṟiyātu uṭampaṭal
poruḷ iṭaiyiṭutal etir poruḷ uṇarttal
colliṉ eccam colliyāṅku uṇarttal
tantu puṇarntu uraittal ñāpakam kūṟal
uyttukkoṇṭu uṇarttaloṭu meyppaṭa nāṭic
colliya alla piṟa avaṇ variṉum
colliya vakaiyāṉ curuṅka nāṭi
maṉattiṉ eṇṇi mācu aṟat terintukoṇṭu
iṉattiṉ cērtti uṇarttal vēṇṭum
nuṉittaku pulavar kūṟiya nūlē.
